# PART I — INVESTMENT COMMITTEE DECISION

## 1. One-Line Decision

`Decision: Watchlist — a fortress balance sheet and a properly-governed company are trading at only an 8.1% discount to fair value, while earnings are decelerating into a print (2026-08-27/28) whose own setup already favors a miss.`

## 3. Would I Buy This With Real Money Today?

**Final answer: I would not buy this today** because the price already reflects most of the good news (only an 8.1% cushion to fair value) while the next two weeks carry a real chance of a third consecutive earnings miss, and the moat — the thing that would justify paying up for Haier over its stronger-margin peers — is confirmed to be eroding, not stabilizing, in the most recent data.

- **Confidence score:** Understanding 75.5/100 (the situation is well understood — audited annual reports on two accounting bases, a Q1 2026 filing, full consensus history, five valuation methods, and a full solvency stress test all sit in the pool). Conviction 42.0/100 (a genuinely non-committal number — this is what "wait and see" looks like on a 0–100 scale, not a rounding error).
- **Position stance:** No position. This is a name to watch through the 2026-08-27/28 print, not to own into it.
- **What would raise confidence:** A H1 2026 print that beats the already-cut consensus (revenue > CNY 75,076mn, EPS > CNY 0.58) on both lines, with a segment P&L that actually reconciles the ">10% ex-North-America operating profit growth" claim management has not yet backed up with numbers; gross margin holding at or above 26.3%; the Haier Group Finance Co. related-party borrowing ratio stabilizing rather than climbing further past 37.7% of its cap.
- **What would lower confidence:** A third consecutive miss; gross margin falling below 26.3%; related-party borrowing utilization climbing further; a second straight year of negative incremental ROIC once FY2026 closes.
- **What would force exit/rejection:** Evidence the North America "one-off weather/tariff shock" story is false (tariffs persisting into H2, not "gradually easing" as management's own unverified forecast claims) combined with China demand deteriorating further — that combination would validate the structural-bear case (CNY 15.90, −26.9%) as the base case, not a tail risk, and this name would move from Watchlist to Avoid.

## 4. The Actual Variant Perception

- **What everyone already knows:** Haier trades at a 25–38% discount to Midea and Gree on every reported multiple; its margins (EBIT 6.9%) trail both peers (Midea 9.8%, Gree 17.4%); China's appliance trade-in subsidy is fading and raw-material costs are rising; the last two reported quarters both missed consensus.
- **What is probably priced in:** Most of it. The peer-relative valuation method — the dominant, market-anchored method in this dossier — finds that once Haier's below-peer margin and confirmed-eroding moat are quality-adjusted for, the residual gap to peers shrinks to a modest +1.5% (CNY 22.08 fair value vs. CNY 21.75 price). The market is not obviously mispricing the known facts.
- **What the engine thinks may be missed:** Two things, both modest, not decisive. First, the common "China SOE-adjacent stock trades cheap on a governance discount" story does not hold here — the management-governance module explicitly tested for a structurally unaligned controlling owner (§24 Filter 6) and did not find one; Haier Group Corporation is a collectively-owned enterprise with no pledging, no dual-class stock, and cumulative voting. Anyone assuming the discount is an ownership discount is wrong; it is an earnings-trajectory discount instead. Second, a genuine cross-module forensic mosaic exists: three separately sub-threshold accounting-integrity signals (rising accruals, an unreconciled favorable regional claim, a recurring subsidy mislabeled "non-recurring") span two different modules (earnings, management-governance) — no single module flagged this as material on its own, but stacked together they are a real, monitorable caution a surface read of "cheap, fortress-balance-sheet appliance maker" would miss.
- **What evidence proves we are actually different:** If the FY2026 annual report (~March 2027) shows Haier Group Finance Co. related-party borrowing continuing to climb past its current 37.7% cap-utilization AND the accrual pattern (receivables/inventory outgrowing revenue/COGS) persists for a third straight year, the forensic-mosaic caution is confirmed as a real, worsening pattern rather than a one-off. If instead borrowing utilization stabilizes or falls and the accrual pattern reverses, the caution is falsified and should be dropped from future runs.

Edge score: **25/100**. This is a real but modest edge — mostly a correction to what the discount is NOT (an ownership discount) plus a genuine but sub-threshold accounting-mosaic caution — not a strong, proprietary insight the market has missed. Per the edge gate, conviction is capped at 60 regardless of anything else in this dossier, and the actual computed conviction (42.0) sits well inside that cap.

## 5. Thesis → Antithesis → Final Thesis

- **Thesis:** Haier is a global-scale appliance maker with a fortress balance sheet (net cash on every basis, 1.61x gross leverage) trading close to fair value — a safe, if unexciting, way to own the China appliance sector.
- **Antithesis:** "Close to fair value" cuts both ways — the 8.1% margin of safety is thin, and the earnings trend feeding that fair-value estimate is deteriorating (revenue growth cut from +12.6% to +5.7% to outright −6.9% in the latest quarter), with the next print already set up to miss.
- **Revised thesis:** The balance-sheet safety is real and should limit how far this can fall in a genuine crisis, but it does not protect the equity from a re-rating if the moat keeps eroding — the valuation module's own structural-bear case (CNY 15.90, a real quarter of the current price, not a remote tail) is exactly what a continuing moat-erosion trend produces.
- **Antithesis:** Two consecutive misses have already happened and consensus has already been cut ~14% — is the bad news already in the price?
- **Final thesis:** Partially. The peer-relative method (the dossier's most trustworthy method, anchored in real market prices) finds most, not all, of the discount already reflects the weaker fundamentals — leaving a genuine but thin ~8% cushion, not a bargain. Combined with a near-term catalyst whose own setup favors another miss and a real (if modest) accounting-mosaic caution, the risk/reward does not clear the bar for a position today. This is a name to watch through the print, not to own into it.
- **Insight threshold reached:** the remaining uncertainty is mostly data-dependent, not reasoning-dependent — the single question that resolves this (does the moat erosion stabilize or continue?) will be answered incrementally by the 2026-08-27/28, ~late-October, and ~March-2027 prints, not by further analysis of what is already in the pool.

## 6. Simple Summary

- **What it does:** Makes and sells major home appliances worldwide under several owned brands, built mostly through acquisitions (GE Appliances 2016, Fisher & Paykel 2018, Candy 2019).
- **Why it may go up:** It clears its own cost of capital, holds more cash than debt, trades near fair value with a real margin of safety, and management's incentive pay genuinely misses its targets rather than getting rubber-stamped.
- **Why it may go down:** Rising raw-material costs (steel, copper, aluminium — 84% of the cost of what it sells) with no way to pass them to customers, a fading government subsidy that was propping up China demand, and a moat that is measurably shrinking against its two closest peers.
- **What data supports the thesis:** Audited annual reports on two accounting bases (translated from Chinese, not treated as a data gap), a Q1 2026 quarterly filing, a fresh (1-day-old) share price, full analyst consensus history, and a complete balance-sheet stress test.
- **What data is missing:** No committed bank credit line total, no formal loan covenant package, no credit rating, and no earnings-call transcript from after 2019 — none of these are severe enough to refuse a rating, but each limits how far this analysis can be pushed.
- **Buy now or wait:** Wait. The H1 2026 results (2026-08-27/28, about two weeks away) are the first real test of whether the earnings deceleration is stabilizing or continuing.
- **The one next thing to check:** The H1 2026 print itself — specifically, whether gross margin holds at or above 26.3% and whether the ">10% ex-North-America operating profit growth" claim management made in Q1 2026 is finally backed up by an actual segment-level number.

## 6. Valuation and Peer Mispricing

*(Deferring in full to `valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md` — see Chapter C for the module's own account.)*

Haier reads as **fairly valued, not cheap**: base fair value of CNY 23.67/share sits only 8.8% above the CNY 21.75 price (1 trading day old, pool-verified). Bull / base / bear-cyclical / headline bear-structural levels are CNY 31.78 / 23.67 / 16.79 / 15.90 — a 2.0x spread from bull to bear-structural. The dominant method is peer-relative valuation (68% weight), the only method anchored in real, dated market prices for named comparables (Midea, Gree, Whirlpool).

| Metric | Company (Haier) | Peer Median (Midea/Gree/Whirlpool) | Premium / Discount | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| EV/LTM EBITDA | ~6.75–7.38x (own-history) | 9.71x (unadjusted peer median) | −24.3% raw discount | Shrinks to ~+1.5% once quality-adjusted for below-peer margin — mostly warranted |
| LTM EBIT margin | 6.9% | Midea 9.8%, Gree 17.4% | Well below both named peers | Reflects the confirmed-eroding moat, not a market error |
| Gross margin | 26.3% | Midea 26.3% (tie), Gree 29.8% | Roughly ties Midea, trails Gree | Consistent with the margin-based multiple discount |

Three explanations for any residual gap were tested explicitly: (1) **True mispricing** — a modest +1.5% residual exists once quality-adjusted, genuinely small; (2) **Cycle fear** — partially supported: China's trade-in subsidy fade and raw-material inflation are real, already-realized headwinds, not merely feared ones; (3) **Balance-sheet, governance, or quality discount** — ruled out on the ownership dimension (no misaligned controlling owner found, §24 Filter 6 not tripped) but confirmed on the moat-quality dimension (460bp five-year gross-margin decline, ROIC down for two straight readings). The valuation gap is an earnings-trajectory discount, not an ownership-driven value trap.

The reverse-DCF read (`05_reverse-dcf.md`) is two-sided: the price implies either a historically unprecedented multi-year cash-flow contraction, or the market is simply discounting ordinary cash flows at a rate roughly 3x the DCF module's own CAPM-derived WACC (12.3% market-implied vs. 4.10% CAPM). Treat this as inconclusive, not a standalone conviction driver, exactly as the valuation module recommends.

## 8. Scenario Model

Fair-value levels are taken verbatim from `valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md` (that module owns the levels); this synthesis owns the probabilities (CLAUDE.md §10).

| Case | Probability | Return | Price Target | What Must Happen |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Bull | 20% | +46.1% | CNY 31.78 | Raw-material excess-cost growth reverts to 0pp AND China domestic demand partially recovers to +5% YoY (a genuine two-condition conjunction); multiple expands to the quality-adjusted ceiling (7.4x). 12-month horizon. |
| Base | 40% | +8.8% | CNY 23.67 | FY2026E consensus growth path holds roughly as guided (revenue +2.24%, EBITDA ~CNY 30.5bn); multiple sits modestly above the current LTM print but short of full reversion to own-history mean. 12-month horizon. |
| Bear-cyclical | 25% | −22.8% | CNY 16.79 | Commodity pressure, competitive intensity, and China property-cycle softness erase the SG&A-driven margin gains posted since FY2021; EBIT margin reverts to the 5-year trough (5.91%). 12-month horizon. |
| Bear-structural (headline bear) | 15% | −26.9% | CNY 15.90 | Moat erosion continues without stabilizing: revenue growth cut to roughly half consensus, EBIT margin fades to 5.00% by FY2030 (below the FY2021 trough), gross margin fades to 23.8%. 24–36 month horizon. |

Probabilities sum to 100%.

**Common driver / correlated-tail check:** All four cases are driven predominantly by ONE underlying variable — whether raw-material cost inflation (no pass-through) and China demand deterioration continue or stabilize. The bull and base cases both require this variable to improve or hold; both bear cases require it to worsen. This is not four independent draws — it is effectively one binary bet (stabilizes vs. continues) expressed across four magnitude bands. The bear-cyclical and bear-structural cases are not diversified from each other; if the driver worsens, both fire together, and the "26.9% downside" figure understates the correlated nature of the loss (there is no meaningfully separate path to bear-cyclical that avoids bear-structural risk if the trend continues past 12 months). This compounding is carried into the Risk Register (§9) and Kill Criteria (§10).

**Span/conjunction check:** The bull case (+46.1%) is well outside a single ordinary weekly move — no span violation. The bull case requires two conditions simultaneously (commodity reversion AND demand recovery) — a genuine, not manufactured, conjunction; the two bear cases require only one thing (continued deterioration) — this asymmetry is deliberate and reflects that deterioration is already partly realized (Q1 2026 already printed −6.9% revenue) while recovery has not yet been evidenced in any reported quarter.

**Executed math** (see §14 for the full reconciliation): probability-weighted expected return **+3.02%**; probability-weighted target price **CNY 22.41**; risk/reward **0.11**; downside risk **26.9%**.

Main upside driver: North America normalization + commodity-cost reversion (bull case). Main downside driver: continued commodity-cost/China-demand deterioration (both bear cases, correlated). Given a +3.0% expected return against 26.9% downside and a risk/reward of 0.11, **the expected return is not worth the risk at today's price** — this is the central quantitative reason behind the Watchlist rating.

## 11. Positioning and Trade Construction

- **Recommendation:** Wait — do not open a position before the 2026-08-27/28 H1 2026 print. If a position is initiated after a clean beat, size it as a starter position only, not a full position, given the forensic-mosaic ceiling and the thin margin of safety.
- **Entry style (if initiated post-print):** Scale in only after the print confirms gross margin ≥26.3% and the segment P&L reconciles the North America claim — do not enter on the headline beat/miss alone.
- **Add levels:** Only on confirmed, print-by-print stabilization of gross margin over two consecutive quarters (H1 2026 and Q3 2026) — a single quarter is not enough evidence given the trajectory's own volatility.
- **Stop-loss logic:** A move toward the bear-cyclical level (CNY 16.79, −22.8%) should trigger a full re-underwrite, not an automatic stop. **The stop may not protect us on an earnings gap** — the H1 2026 print is a discrete, binary-risk event two weeks away, and Haier's FQ4 2025 print already showed a −43.9% single-quarter EPS surprise magnitude; a gap through any mechanical stop is a real risk into this date.
- **What not to do:** Do not treat the fortress balance sheet as a reason to hold through deteriorating earnings — net cash protects solvency, not the equity multiple.
- **Hedge:** Given the thesis's own correlated-tail structure (commodity costs + China demand + moat trajectory are one variable, not four), a direct short against a stronger-margin China appliance peer (see §12) is a more precise hedge than an index short.
- **Options vs. stock:** No IBKR options/positioning data exists in this pool — this question cannot be answered from available data.

## 12. 2nd Best Bet

**Midea Group (SZSE:000333)** — named repeatedly across the business-model, valuation, and management-governance modules as Haier's closest, stronger-margin domestic peer (LTM EBIT margin 9.8% vs. Haier's 6.9%; gross margin ties Haier's 26.3%; the SOTP module used Midea's own 12.71x multiple for Haier's Laundry segment). Midea shares the same underlying macro exposure (China trade-in subsidy fade, raw-material costs, the same consumer/property cycle) but has shown structurally less margin erosion, making it a less risky expression of the same "China appliance sector at an inflection" thesis. **This is a known peer name referenced only via this pool's Capital IQ competitor/comp data — no primary Midea filing, consensus, or governance data was reviewed in this run, so this is Level 2–3 evidence at best (a named comp, not a full underwrite) and would require its own dedicated run before sizing any position.**

- Why it is #2: same thesis vector (China appliance demand/commodity cost cycle), materially less margin erosion in the data already reviewed here.
- How it diversifies: if the China appliance sector overall stabilizes, Midea's stronger margin base should capture more of the upside per unit of macro-cycle improvement than Haier's thinner margin cushion.
- Why it may be safer: it is not carrying Haier's specific related-party financing dependency or the accounting-integrity mosaic flagged in this dossier.
- Catalyst that would make it better: the same H1 2026 China-demand data point that determines Haier's near-term trajectory also applies to Midea — a comparative read of both companies' H1 prints would be the natural next step.

## 13. Thesis → Antithesis Iteration

### Thesis 1
Haier is a global-scale, net-cash appliance maker trading close to fair value with real incentive alignment and no disqualifying red flags — a reasonable, lower-risk way to own China consumer-durables exposure.

### Antithesis 1
"Close to fair value" is doing a lot of work: an 8.1% margin of safety is thin, not a bargain, and it is calculated against a base case that assumes the current deceleration does not continue — an assumption the most recent quarter (Q1 2026, −6.9% revenue) already argues against.

### Revised Thesis 2
The balance sheet genuinely limits catastrophic downside (a full 100% EBITDA wipeout does not exhaust liquidity), but balance-sheet safety and equity-value safety are different things — the equity is exposed to a re-rating if the moat erosion (already confirmed, not hypothesized: 460bp gross-margin decline over 5 years) continues rather than stabilizes, and the near-term catalyst (H1 2026 print) is set up to test exactly that, with its own setup already favoring a miss.

### Antithesis 2
Two consecutive misses have already happened and consensus has already been cut ~14% — is this not already priced in, making the risk/reward attractive precisely because expectations are now low?

### Final Thesis
Partially, not fully. The peer-relative method — this dossier's most trustworthy method — finds that once quality-adjusted, most (not all) of Haier's discount to peers is warranted by its weaker margins and confirmed-eroding moat, leaving only a modest ~1.5% residual gap. Combined with a forensic-mosaic caution (three sub-threshold accounting-integrity signals compounding across two modules) and a genuinely poor probability-weighted risk/reward (+3.0% expected return against 26.9% downside, ratio 0.11), the setup does not clear the bar for a position today. The correct posture is to watch the print, not to pre-position for it.

**Insight threshold reached: the remaining uncertainty is mostly data-dependent, not reasoning-dependent.**

## 14. Math Validation

Executed via Python (see the exact snippet and output below — no scratch/mental arithmetic used, per CLAUDE.md §10 and the Step 4 workflow rule):

```
Scenarios: bull 20% @ CNY31.78 (+46.11%), base 40% @ CNY23.67 (+8.83%),
           bear_cyclical 25% @ CNY16.79 (-22.80%), bear_structural 15% @ CNY15.90 (-26.90%)

Sum of probabilities:                  100%
Probability-weighted expected return:  +3.02%
Probability-weighted target price:     CNY 22.41
Expected return from weighted target:  (22.41 - 21.75) / 21.75 = +3.02%   [reconciles exactly with the above]
Risk/reward:  (22.41 - 21.75) / (21.75 - 15.90) = 0.66 / 5.85 = 0.11
Downside risk:  -min(scenario returns) = -(-26.90%) = 26.90%
Margin of safety (base case): (23.67 - 21.75) / 23.67 = 8.11%
```

These figures are copied verbatim into the §2 Headline Scorecard, §8 Scenario Model, and `decision_record.json` — no re-typed or independently-recalculated numbers appear anywhere else in this dossier.

**Sensitivity note:** the entire spread between the base case (+8.8%) and the two bear cases (−22.8% to −26.9%) is driven by a single underlying assumption — whether the confirmed moat-erosion trend (already firing: 460bp five-year gross-margin decline, two consecutive ROIC declines) continues or stabilizes. This is the single fragile assumption behind this entire thesis, and it is exactly what the 2026-08-27/28 print begins to test.

## 18. Balance Sheet and Survival Test

*(Deferring in full to `balance-sheet-survival/99_balance-sheet-survival-synthesis.md` — see Chapter C above for the full account. Summarized here per the No-Bloat Rule.)*

Net debt is negative (net cash) on every basis since FY2021 — CNY (4,952.2)mn strict, CNY (16,975.1)mn broad. Cash: CNY 47,621.7mn on hand. Maturity wall: 55.0% of gross debt (CNY 23,452.2mn) sits in one within-12-month bucket, covered 2.0x by cash alone. Floating vs. fixed: 70% of FY2025 borrowings are floating-rate; a +200bp shock adds only CNY 509.4mn/yr pre-tax interest — immaterial given the net-cash position. Interest burden: EBITDA/interest coverage 9.91x. Liquidity risk: low in substance (27.3-month runway) but the confidence on that figure is capped at 60/100 because no committed/undrawn bank-facility figure exists anywhere in the pool. **If EBITDA fell 40–60%:** liquidity is never exhausted at any tested level, even a full 100% EBITDA wipeout for a year — only an indicative, unconfirmed leverage-covenant proxy (3.5x gross debt/EBITDA, not a real disclosed covenant) breaks, and only at a 54.1% EBITDA decline. This is fed directly into the Risk Register (§9) and Kill Criteria (§10) above as the balance-sheet break-point.

## business-model — module synthesis

_Source: `business-model/99_business-model-synthesis.md`_

# Business Model Reality Check — HAIER (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Haier Smart Home makes and sells refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, and water heaters worldwide under owned brands including Haier, Casarte, GE Appliances, and Candy, built largely through regional acquisitions since 1984. Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions is the biggest segment, generating 41.7% of FY2025 revenue and 43.4% of segment profit before tax. The clearest positive is a five-year through-cycle return on capital (ROIC) of 8.32%, comfortably above an estimated 3.9%–4.8% cost of capital (WACC). The clearest negative is a five-year, 460-basis-point gross-margin slide (30.9% to 26.3%), with an EBIT margin (6.9%) that trails both named Chinese peers, Midea (9.8%) and Gree (17.4%). No disqualifier triggered; this is an average, commodity-exposed manufacturer with a narrow, eroding moat, worth deeper work only if the price is cheap.

## 1. First-Pass Verdict

### Automatic Disqualifier Check

(Restated from `01_disqualifier-scan.md` — all eight tests came back N, and 0 of 5 quantitative near-miss bands were in range.)

| # | Disqualifier | Triggered (Y/N) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Auditor qualification or going-concern note (last 3 years) | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.1 — standard unqualified opinion; going-concern assessment finds no material uncertainty |
| 2 | >50% promoter / insider shares pledged | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.103-104 — pledge/freeze status "无" (none) for both largest Haier-affiliated holders; 0% pledged |
| 3 | Related-party transactions >25% of revenue or expenses | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 十三(三) — sales side 1.18% of revenue; purchases side 9.55%–10.83% of expenses under either reading |
| 4 | Auditor changed twice in last 3 years without disclosed reason | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.3931 — 13 consecutive years with the same domestic auditor; FY2025 was a re-appointment |
| 5 | Material restatement (>5% of revenue or net income) in last 2 years | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.9 — FY2024 restatement was a routine common-control combination, 0.012% of revenue / 0.054% of net income |
| 6 | Active regulatory enforcement action on financial reporting | N | Capital IQ News / Key Developments logs — no matches on CSRC/enforcement/investigation keywords |
| 7 | >40% of revenue from single customer with no long-term contract | N | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.43-44 — top 5 customers combined are only 19.6% of sales |
| 8 | Negative operating cash flow in 3 of last 4 years (excl. growth-stage) | N | Capital IQ Cash Flow export — positive operating cash flow in every one of the last 4 fiscal years |

No row triggered. The Verdict below is not locked.

### Verdict

- **Verdict:** Average business — worth deeper work only if valuation is cheap
- Disqualifier triggered: N
- Business clarity /100: **68** — the five-segment, nine-region revenue structure and brand portfolio are clearly disclosed (`02_business-identity.md`, `03_segment-map.md`), but the 13.0%-of-revenue "Other Business" catch-all carries no product-level split and no unit-volume or ASP figure exists anywhere in the pool for any segment (`04_unit-economics.md`), which caps true clarity on how value is actually created unit by unit
- Business quality /100: **42** *(Weak, upper end — from `07_business-quality.md`)*
- Moat /100: **48** *(strongest single moat source — Brand — from `09_moat.md`; overall verdict is "Narrow moat," eroding)*
- External dependency risk /100 *(inverted — higher = worse)*: **52** *(from `10_external-dependency.md`)*
- Capital allocation & governance /100: **66** *(from `11_capital-allocation-governance.md`)*
- Data quality /100: **82** — audited FY2025 annual reports on both the CAS (SSE) and IFRS (HKEX) bases, plus a Q1 2026 quarterly filing, all inside the sufficiency window (`00_data-triage.md` verdict: "Sufficient"); held back from a higher score by the absence of any post-2019 earnings transcript or investor deck and the total absence of unit-volume/capacity data
- Overall usefulness /100: **58**
- Business type (one line): Multi-brand, acquisition-built global manufacturer of major home appliances, selling through third-party retail/distribution channels and owned e-commerce, with a local-for-local manufacturing footprint built mainly through regional brand acquisitions (GE Appliances 2016, Fisher & Paykel 2018, Candy 2019) rather than organic entry [`02_business-identity.md`]
- Biggest business-model risk (one line): A thin, commodity-exposed core (raw materials are 84.0% of appliance-segment cost of sales) combined with a discretionary, non-contracted China sales channel (48.5% of revenue) and a moat that is measurably eroding — gross margin down 460bp over five years while two named Chinese peers, Midea and Gree, earn materially higher margins in the same product categories [`06_value-chain.md`, `05_customer-geography.md`, `09_moat.md`]

**REJECTOR-FILTER CAPS (CLAUDE.md §24).**
- **Filter 1 — Crooks / integrity.** Not tripped. `01_disqualifier-scan.md` found no proven fraud and no unverified adverse "buzz" on the controller (Haier Group Corporation) or senior management. No conviction cap applied.
- **Filter 4 — Serial acquirers.** Not tripped. `11_capital-allocation-governance.md` scored the acquisition-pattern row 35/100 severity — well under the 70 trigger (roughly one material third-party deal every 3–4 years, confined to the core appliance industry, no evidence of forced divestitures). Capital allocation & governance score is NOT capped at 50, and Overall usefulness is NOT capped at 70.
- **Filter 5 — Fast-changing industry.** Not tripped. `07_business-quality.md` scored the industry rate-of-change / disruption row 72/100 — above the 40 threshold (mature, decades-stable category, same handful of global brands leading every product line for 20+ years). Business quality is NOT capped at 65, and no `RF-BQ-005` tag was emitted.

No caps apply from this module's three owned filters.

**CAPITAL STRUCTURE TRANSACTION CAP.** Not applied. `11_capital-allocation-governance.md` shows Total Debt/EBITDA holding a stable, low 1.34x–1.51x range across FY2021–FY2025 and shares outstanding drifting down only ~0.5% (9,323.0m Dec-2024 → 9,275.5m Mar-2026) on modest buybacks. Neither threshold (debt change >50% YoY, or share count change >25% YoY) was crossed in the period, so the Capital allocation & governance score is not capped by this rule.

**FORENSIC TAG PROPAGATION.** No `RF-DISQ-001`, `RF-RFS-001`, `RF-BQ-005`, or equivalent standalone forensic tag was emitted by any upstream module in this pool — `01_disqualifier-scan.md` found 0 of 5 near-misses in band (below the 2-near-miss compounding-signal threshold), and `12_red-flags-sweep.md` did not name an aggressive-accounting-practice pattern as a standalone tagged flag. Nothing to propagate here.

**Module Disconfirmation (CLAUDE.md §8; fix F37).**
- **Strongest bear point:** Gross margin fell 460bp over five years (30.9% FY2021 → 26.3% FY2025) and through-cycle ROIC has now declined for two consecutive readings from its FY2024 peak (9.12% → 7.97% FY2025 → 7.56% LTM Mar-2026), even as China offline refrigerator share rose 3.6pp to 47.7% — consistent with share being defended through price/promotion rather than pricing power, the opposite of a widening moat [`09_moat.md` §5; `07_business-quality.md` §4].
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** Despite the margin slide, five-year through-cycle ROIC (8.32%) still clears an estimated cost of capital (≈3.9%–4.8% CAPM inference) by 350–440 basis points, the balance sheet carries net cash on a strict basis with Total Debt/EBITDA under 1.5x, the disqualifier scan returned zero triggers and zero near-misses across all eight tests, and disclosure quality (68/100) is unusually strong for a dual-standard (CAS + IFRS) filer [`09_moat.md` §3; `11_capital-allocation-governance.md`; `01_disqualifier-scan.md`; `07_business-quality.md`].
- **Single killer risk specific to the business model:** A sustained commodity-cost shock (steel/aluminium/copper/plastics are 84.0% of appliance-segment cost of sales) landing on top of an already price-competed, non-contracted China channel (48.5% of revenue, orders placed "at such time and in such quantities as they deem appropriate"). The unit-economics module's own arithmetic shows a 20% unmitigated rise in the refrigerator product line's COGS would turn the entire Household Food Storage & Cooking segment's ~RMB6.1bn profit into roughly a RMB5.6bn loss [`04_unit-economics.md` §4; `06_value-chain.md` §5 — inference, not from filings, on the zero-pass-through assumption].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** The business-quality module's own industry rate-of-change score (72/100) argues this is not a disruption story — the same handful of global brands (Haier, Whirlpool, Electrolux, LG, Midea) has led every major appliance category for 20+ years with no platform-style discontinuity disclosed anywhere in the pool, so the margin erosion reads as competitive/cyclical pressure in a stable-technology category, not a fast-changing-industry problem [`07_business-quality.md` Industry rate-of-change row; `09_moat.md` §5].

| red-flags-sweep | Two new flags beyond upstream coverage; no standalone disqualifier | Goodwill + indefinite-life intangibles are 25.3% of parent-company equity, 76% of it concentrated in the 2016 GE Appliances deal, tested over an unusually long 5–15 year DCF budget window, and sitting behind the one segment (North America) the company says tariffs are currently hurting (severity 50/100) |

## 3. Reconciliation

Two specialists computed return on capital differently and reconciled explicitly rather than averaging. `09_moat.md` found Capital IQ's own reported "Return on Capital %" for FY2025 (7.97%) diverges from a manually built NOPAT ÷ average invested capital figure (10.96%) — the two exports do not disclose enough about Capital IQ's exact averaging window and capital-base definition to fully reconcile them. Per CLAUDE.md §4's conservative-default rule, the moat module used the lower, vendor-computed figure (7.97% FY2025 / 8.32% five-year average) for its ROIC-vs-WACC test rather than the higher manual estimate, and this synthesis carries that same conservative figure forward.

A second minor item: the CAS-basis (SSE) and IFRS-basis (HKEX) FY2025 annual reports report slightly different total revenue (RMB302,346.78m vs RMB302,329m, a 0.006% gap) and slightly different "Other Business" segment profit (RMB354.29m CAS vs RMB336m IFRS). `03_segment-map.md` already reconciled this as a normal CAS/IFRS presentation difference rather than a data conflict, and no downstream module treated it as material — this synthesis agrees it does not affect any segment-share or margin conclusion.

No other material disagreements between specialists were found.

## 4. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Strongest business-model positive:** Through-cycle ROIC (8.32%, five-year average) sits 350–440bp above an estimated cost of capital (≈3.9%–4.8%, CAPM inference) — the company clears the absolute economic-moat test even though it trails named peers on margin [`09_moat.md` §3-4].
- **Strongest business-model negative:** Gross margin fell 460bp over five years (30.9% FY2021 → 26.3% FY2025), and the company's own MD&A attributes the FY2025 leg of that decline directly to Q4 copper/bulk-material price rises and intensifying domestic competition overwhelming its cost-reduction program — pricing power is trending the wrong way, not the right one [`06_value-chain.md` §3; `07_business-quality.md` Pricing power row].
- **Most important segment:** Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions (refrigerators/freezers + kitchen appliances) — 41.7% of FY2025 revenue, 43.4% of segment profit before tax, with no revenue-vs-profit conflict to resolve [`03_segment-map.md` §2].
- **Cleanest unit-economics read:** Cannot be built to a true per-unit level — Haier discloses no unit-volume or ASP figure for any product line, so "does each new appliance sold create value" cannot be separated from "is the aggregate segment profitable" (the latter is answered: yes, at a thin 7.24% margin for refrigerators, slightly improving; the kitchen-appliance line is deteriorating) [`04_unit-economics.md` §3].
- **Where the company sits vs named peers:** Bottom of the three profiled peers on margin — LTM EBIT margin 6.9% vs Midea 9.8% and Gree 17.4%, ahead only of Whirlpool (5.4% GAAP operating margin); gross margin (26.3%) roughly ties Midea (26.3%) and trails Gree (29.8%) [`08_competitive-map.md` §2; `09_moat.md` §4].
- **Main external dependency:** Four simultaneously High-rated variables — commodity prices (steel/aluminium/copper/plastics at 84.0% of appliance COGS), the fading China trade-in subsidy, US/EU tariffs and geopolitics, and the China/US consumer-property cycle — with commodities and tariffs already shown moving FY2025 gross margin [`10_external-dependency.md` §1, §4].
- **Most important capital allocation or governance signal:** Related-party financial-services concentration is the single item that would move the classification if it worsened — up to RMB33,988m (~57% of group cash & short-term investments) is parked with Haier Group's own affiliated finance company, and related-party borrowing from that entity jumped ~19x year on year (RMB196m → RMB3,767m against a RMB10,000m cap); this is fully disclosed and independent-director-reviewed today, not a red flag on its own, but it is the signal to watch (severity 45/100, inverted) [`11_capital-allocation-governance.md` §1, §3].
- **Severity ≥40 red flag requiring propagation:** Goodwill + indefinite-life intangibles are 25.3% of parent-company book equity, with 76% of that goodwill (RMB20,883.0m of RMB27,300.2m) concentrated in the single 2016 GE Appliances acquisition, tested over an unusually long 5–15 year discounted-cash-flow budget period (versus the standard 5-year explicit horizon), and sitting directly behind the North America segment — the one segment the company itself says US tariffs are currently hurting. No impairment has been taken and the audit opinion is unqualified; this is a monitoring item for the North America/GE Appliances thesis, not a standalone disqualifier (severity 50/100) [`12_red-flags-sweep.md` §2-3].
- **Lower-severity flag (below 40, summarized per discretion):** A modest defined-benefit pension/post-retirement-medical net liability (RMB1,293.5m, ~6.6% of FY2025 net profit attributable to owners) sits inside two foreign subsidiaries tied to the same GE Appliances / CCR acquisitions — real but small, not requiring separate escalation (severity 25/100) [`12_red-flags-sweep.md` §2].
- **Whether any automatic disqualifier triggered:** No. All eight tests came back N with zero near-misses in band [`01_disqualifier-scan.md`].
- **Which rejector filters tripped:** None of the three this module owns (crooks/integrity, serial acquirers, fast-changing industry) tripped — see the REJECTOR-FILTER CAPS block in Section 1 for the evidence and thresholds on each.
- **Biggest missing data point:** Unit-volume and average-selling-price figures for any product segment — without them, revenue and margin moves can be split by segment and geography but not by volume vs. price/mix within a segment, and true per-unit value creation cannot be tested [`02_business-identity.md` §3a; `04_unit-economics.md` §1].
- **Whether the business deserves deeper work, and what would change the answer:** Worth deeper work only if valuation is cheap relative to a business earning modestly above its cost of capital but trailing peers on margin and showing a real, multi-year erosion in gross margin and ROIC. What would upgrade the answer: gross margin and ROIC stabilizing once the China trade-in subsidy fully laps and commodity costs normalize, and/or the margin gap to Midea/Gree closing. What would downgrade it further: a further leg down in China property-linked demand, an unmitigated commodity-cost shock given the segment's thin ~7% margin cushion, a GE Appliances goodwill impairment if North America tariff pressure persists, or a deepening of the related-party finance-company concentration.

## 5. Simple Summary

- **What it does:** Makes and sells refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, kitchen appliances, and water heaters worldwide under Haier, Casarte, Leader, GE Appliances, Candy, Fisher & Paykel, and AQUA — built largely by buying established regional appliance makers rather than growing organically.
- **How it makes money:** Revenue = units sold × average selling price, summed across five product segments and nine geographic regions; the household refrigeration/kitchen segment alone supplies 41.7% of revenue and 43.4% of profit.
- **Whether each new unit creates value:** Not provable to a true per-unit level — no unit-volume or price-per-unit figure is disclosed for any product line — but the aggregate refrigerator segment is profitable at a thin, slightly improving 7.24% margin, while kitchen appliances are deteriorating.
- **Which segment matters most:** Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions (refrigerators/freezers + kitchen appliances) — the clear leader on both revenue and profit share, with no close second.
- **Whether it has a moat, and against whom:** A narrow, eroding moat. It clears its own cost of capital (ROIC 8.32% vs WACC ≈3.9%–4.8%) but earns less on every disclosed margin line than two of its three named peers, Midea and Gree, and the gap has been widening, not closing.
- **What external variables it depends on:** Commodity input prices (84% of appliance COGS), the now-fading China appliance trade-in subsidy, US/EU tariffs, and the China/US consumer-property cycle — all four rated High dependency, with two already shown moving reported margin.
- **Whether capital is allocated well:** Mostly — net cash balance sheet, low leverage, a covered and growing dividend, a flat-to-shrinking share count, no promoter pledging, clean unqualified audits — but a growing share of group cash and borrowing runs through the controlling shareholder's own affiliated finance company, the one signal to watch.
- **Whether it deserves deeper work:** Only if the valuation is cheap enough to compensate for weak business quality (42/100), a narrow and eroding moat, and material external dependency (52/100) — this is not a durable-compounder story on the business-model evidence alone.

(RMB 15,244,521,006, an equity-method associate, not consolidated) and 青岛海尔零部件采购 (RMB 3,335,266,987). ## business-model / 02_business-identity.md

_Source: `business-model/02_business-identity.md`_

# Business Identity — HAIER

## 1. What The Company Actually Does

Haier Smart Home makes and sells large home appliances — refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, water heaters, and kitchen appliances — under a family of owned brands: Haier (the mass-market flagship), Casarte (the premium brand), Leader (value-tier), GE Appliances (United States), Candy (Europe), Fisher & Paykel, and AQUA [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A / Business Review, p.27–28]. Its customers are households, reached mainly through retail chains and third-party distributors (for example New Zealand's The Warehouse Group), plus the company's own e-commerce and brand stores; no single customer accounted for 10% or more of FY2025 revenue [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Customers.xls, current disclosed-customer list; FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4]. The company is headquartered in Qingdao, China, and its revenue splits roughly evenly between mainland China (RMB146,537m of FY2025 revenue) and everywhere else — chiefly North America (RMB79,871m) and Europe (RMB38,491m), with smaller amounts from South Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia/New Zealand, Japan, and the Middle East/Africa [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4 (Segment Information)]. It grew from a single Qingdao refrigerator factory founded in 1984 into its current footprint largely by buying established appliance makers in each region it wanted to enter — the former GE Appliances business in the US (2016), Fisher & Paykel (2018), Candy in Europe (2019), and two smaller 2024 deals (CCR, a commercial-refrigeration business, and Kwikot, a South African water-heater brand) [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, Note 1 (General Information); FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A, p.28]. The problem it solves for a customer is a basic replacement or new-household need — a fridge, a washer, an air conditioner, or a water heater for the home — sold at a price and brand tier that matches the buyer's budget, from the value-tier Leader brand up to the premium Casarte brand [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A, p.27].

## 2. How The Company Makes Money

`Revenue = units sold × average selling price`, summed across five reported product segments and across geography.

FY2025 external revenue by IFRS reportable segment [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4 (Segment Information); consistent with Preliminary Annual Report, Mar-26-2026, p.10–11]:
- Refrigerators / freezers: RMB84,487m
- Kitchen appliances: RMB41,488m
- Air conditioners ("Air Energy Solutions"): RMB54,021m
- Washing machines / laundry care ("Household Laundry Care Solutions"): RMB65,386m
- Water heaters / water purifiers ("Whole-House Water Solutions"): RMB17,736m
- Other businesses (small appliances, channel distribution for third-party brands, logistics services): RMB39,211m
- Total: RMB302,329m, up 5.7% year on year [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, p.1]

**What drives volume:** appliance replacement cycles and new-household formation, plus government demand-support programs — the FY2025 shareholder letter and MD&A both flag China's appliance trade-in subsidy program as a volume driver whose effect faded through the second half of 2025, and a weak China property market as a further drag on new-appliance demand [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, "致股東的函件" (Letter to Shareholders); FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A, p.30].

**What drives price/mix:** the blended selling price moves with brand-tier mix (premiumization toward Casarte versus the value-tier Leader) and with the "other businesses" channel-distribution and small-appliance lines, which carry a different price structure from the core five appliance categories [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A, p.27–29].

**What drives margin:** raw-material costs (steel, copper, plastics/resins are the main appliance input costs), the RMB translation of the roughly half of revenue earned outside China, and trade policy — the FY2025 shareholder letter explicitly names 2025 US tariffs on China-linked appliance imports as a factor that hurt the North America segment's operating results, on top of high US interest rates depressing appliance demand there [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, "致股東的函件"].

## 3. Business Type Classification

Multi-brand, acquisition-built global manufacturer of major home appliances, selling through third-party retail/distribution channels and owned e-commerce, with a local-for-local manufacturing footprint (R&D, production and marketing in 30+ countries) built mainly through regional brand acquisitions rather than organic entry [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Corporate Profile p.2 and MD&A p.28].

## 3a. Sector Overlay & Required-KPI Checklist

No row in `frameworks/SECTOR_OVERLAYS.md` matches "multi-brand global home-appliance manufacturer" specifically — it is not a subscription/SaaS business, a bank/insurer/REIT, a commodity/oil & gas producer, a store-based retailer (Haier does not run its own store network as the primary channel, so same-store-sales and sales-per-sq-ft do not apply), a telecom, an asset manager, or a pharma company. **No sector overlay for multi-brand global appliance manufacturer — generic read** applies, using the "Generic operating company" row's required KPIs:

| Required KPI (generic operating company) | Present / Absent in pool | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Volume (units sold) | **Absent** | The pool discloses revenue by segment and geography in RMB (Note 4) and a market-share/rank claim ("global appliance retail-volume rank #1 for 17 consecutive years" per Euromonitor), but no absolute unit-volume figures for Haier itself anywhere in the pool. |
| Price / mix | Present | Five-segment product mix and nine-region geographic mix disclosed in FY2025 Annual Report Note 4 (Segment Information). |
| Utilization (manufacturing capacity) | **Absent** | Not disclosed anywhere in the pool. |
| Order book / backlog | **Absent / not typically disclosed for this business type** | Appliance retail sales are not project/backlog-based; no backlog figure appears in the pool. |
| Segment mix | Present | IFRS five-segment split (Note 4) plus nine-region geographic revenue split, both FY2025 and FY2024 comparatives. |
| Working-capital cycle | Present | Inventory RMB46,847m, trade receivables (net) RMB27,066m, trade payables RMB77,415m, all FY2025 [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, Notes 10–12]. |

**Data gap flagged for synthesis:** the absence of unit-volume and capacity-utilization data means downstream `earnings/02_revenue-drivers` and `03_margin-drivers` cannot fully separate a revenue or margin move into volume vs. price/mix vs. cost — they can decompose by segment and geography (both present) but not by units × ASP within a segment. This caps how cleanly a revenue-growth or margin move can be attributed without inference.

## 4. What Drives Variance

Revenue moves are mostly volume and mix, not headline price: unit demand tracks appliance replacement cycles, new-household formation, and government subsidy programs — the China trade-in subsidy program's fading effect and a weak China property market were both named as 2025 revenue headwinds — while segment and brand-tier mix shifts (premium Casarte vs. value-tier Leader, and the "other businesses" distribution/small-appliance line) move the blended average selling price [FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), MD&A, p.30; Preliminary Annual Report, Mar-26-2026, Letter to Shareholders]. Margins move mainly with raw-material input costs, RMB translation of the roughly half of revenue earned outside China, and trade policy — 2025 US tariffs on China-linked appliance imports were called out as a specific drag on the North America segment's operating results [Preliminary Annual Report (HKEX Results Announcement), Mar-26-2026, Letter to Shareholders].

# Segment Map — HAIER

Company: Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. — dual-primary listed SSE (A-share, 600690) and HKEX (H-share, 6690), plus a Frankfurt D-share and a US Level-I ADR program. Fiscal year ends Dec-31. Figures below are FY2025 (ended Dec-31-2025) unless stated otherwise, reported in RMB million (CNY mn).

Two audited annual filings cover the same FY2025 period on different accounting standards and were cross-checked against each other:
- A-share Annual Report (China ASBE / CAS basis) — `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11 (分部信息/Segment Information), pp.222-225`
- H-share Annual Report (IFRS basis) — `FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4 (經營分部資料/Operating Segment Information), pp.227-228`

The two filings' segment revenue figures reconcile to within RMB 18mn on a RMB 302,347mn base (a 0.006% difference — CAS external revenue by segment sums to RMB302,346.78mn vs IFRS's RMB302,329mn) — consistent with normal CAS/IFRS presentation differences, not a data conflict. Segment profit differs slightly more (CAS "Other Business" segment profit RMB354.29mn vs IFRS RMB336mn) because IFRS nets a small amount differently in the "Other Business" line; the four core product segments' profit figures match to the RMB million. No `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker (per data-triage), so all figures below are this agent's own sourced read from the filings, cross-checked against the CapIQ Segments workbook, which independently reproduces the identical CAS figures (`Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Financials Segments.xls, tab: Segments`).

## 1. Segment Table

The company defines 5 reportable segments (`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1)`, and identically in `FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4`). The first segment — Household Food Storage and Cooking Solutions — is disclosed with two product-line splits (Refrigerators/Freezers and Kitchen Appliances) carrying their own revenue, profit, and asset figures, so both are shown as separate rows below with a combined subtotal.

| Segment | What It Does | Revenue Share (external revenue) | Profit Share (segment profit before tax) | Margin Quality | Capital Intensity | Cyclicality | Main Risk |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions — Refrigerators/Freezers | Makes and sells refrigerators/freezers ("冰箱/冷柜产品的生产与销售") | 27.9% (RMB84,487mn) | 29.4% (RMB6,115mn) | Mid — 7.2% segment margin, stable/improving from 5.5% (FY22) to 7.2% (FY25) | Mid — assets/revenue ≈0.66x | Mid — China offline market share 47.7% gives some replacement-demand cushion, but domestic real-estate weakness and fading government trade-in subsidy are pressuring China retail | Domestic real-estate slowdown + tapering "trade-in" subsidy effect on China retail; raw-material (steel/aluminum/plastic) cost swings; US tariffs on China-linked appliance exports |
| Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions — Kitchen Appliances | Makes and sells kitchen/cooking appliances ("厨电产品的生产与销售") | 13.7% (RMB41,488mn) | 13.9% (RMB2,893mn) | Mid — ~7.0% segment margin, stable (6.95%-7.72%, FY22-25) | Mid — assets/revenue ≈0.54x | Mid — same domestic housing-linked demand pattern as refrigerators | Same as above |
| — Subtotal: Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions (combined) | — | **41.7% (RMB125,975mn)** | **43.4% (RMB9,008mn)** | — | — | — | — |
| Air Solutions | Makes and sells air conditioners, plus (per business-description note) central air conditioning and commercial refrigeration | 17.9% (RMB54,021mn) | 11.3% (RMB2,341mn) | Low — thinnest of the named segments, 4.3% margin, though improving from 2.7% (FY22) | High — assets/revenue ≈1.06x, and assets nearly doubled FY24→FY25 (RMB32,729mn → RMB57,700mn, +76%) against only 9.6% revenue growth, consistent with the Carrier commercial-refrigeration / India Carrier acquisitions disclosed elsewhere in the filing | High — China's central air conditioning market fell 7.4% in FY2025, explicitly attributed by the company to the real-estate downturn hitting fitted-project shipments | Domestic central-air/property-linked demand contraction (-7.4% China market FY2025); price-war risk in a fragmented, oversupplied sub-industry |
| Home Laundry Care Solutions | Makes and sells washing machines and dryers ("洗衣机及干衣机产品的生产与销售") | 21.6% (RMB65,386mn) | 31.8% (RMB6,597mn) | High — 10.1% margin, trending from 8.9% (FY22) to double digits (10.3% FY24, 10.1% FY25) | Mid — assets/revenue ≈0.81x | Mid — China offline share 47.4% gives replacement-demand resilience despite housing slowdown | Same domestic real-estate/subsidy-taper exposure as refrigerators; competitive intensity in a concentrated market |
| Household Water Solutions | Makes and sells water heaters and water-purification products ("热水器及净水产品等水家电的生产与销售") | 5.9% (RMB17,736mn) | 11.6% (RMB2,418mn) | High — best segment margin at 13.5%, stable/improving from 11.3% (FY22) | High — assets/revenue ≈1.11x | High — company states directly that the water-heater industry was "明显承压" (notably pressured) by the FY2025 real-estate downturn | Real-estate-linked demand pressure on water heaters (company-stated); category migration in water purifiers ("从有一台设备向全屋好水迁移") requiring product-mix investment |
| Other Business | Channel distribution, equipment/component parts manufacturing, small home appliances, logistics services and other ("渠道分销、装备部品、生活小家电、物流服务及其他") | 13.0% (RMB39,229mn) | 1.7% (RMB354mn) | Low — near-breakeven, 0.3% margin, has never exceeded 0.34% margin FY22-FY25 | Mid — assets/revenue ≈0.77x (on total segment revenue including intersegment) | Mid — heterogeneous catch-all bucket, no single cyclicality driver disclosed | Thin/near-zero pricing power; heterogeneous catch-all with limited disclosure granularity (see §3) |

Note: segment profit rows sum to 99.76%; the residual 0.24% (RMB50mn) is a small positive inter-segment-elimination reconciling item, not a business segment (`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1)`) — included here for arithmetic completeness, not as a row.

## 2. Dominant Segment

Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions (refrigerators/freezers plus kitchen appliances, disclosed as one reportable segment with two product-line splits) is the dominant segment by both measures: 41.7% of FY2025 external revenue (RMB125,975mn of RMB302,347mn) and 43.4% of segment profit before tax (RMB9,008mn of RMB20,768mn) `[FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1), pp.222-223; cross-checked FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4, p.227]`. It leads on both revenue and profit share by a wide margin over the next-largest segment (Home Laundry Care Solutions, 21.6% of revenue / 31.8% of profit), so there is no revenue-vs-profit conflict to resolve. This is not a single-segment company (no segment exceeds 85% of revenue or profit) — Haier Smart Home is a multi-category white-goods manufacturer with a clear lead product line, not a de facto single-product business.

## 3. Segment Disclosure Quality

Segment definitions changed materially between FY2021 and FY2022 and have been consistent since: CapIQ's longer segment history (`Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Financials Segments.xls, tab: Segments`) shows a standalone "Overseas Home Appliance and Smart Home Business" segment worth RMB100,623mn / RMB113,725mn (roughly 44-50% of total revenue) in FY2020/FY2021 that disappears entirely from FY2022 onward, with overseas revenue folded into the five product-based segments used today (evidenced by Kitchen Appliances jumping from RMB3,496mn in FY2021 to RMB38,953mn in FY2022 — a reclassification, not 11x organic growth). Downstream agents should not compare pre-2022 and post-2022 segment figures without treating this as a structural break; the current 5-segment structure has been stable and comparably disclosed for FY2022-FY2025 (`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1)`, showing both current-period and prior-period figures on the same basis). The "Other Business" bucket is large — 13.0% of external revenue (RMB39,229mn) — which exceeds the 10% materiality threshold for a catch-all line, and it is disclosed only as a single aggregate ("channel distribution, equipment/component parts, small appliances, logistics services and other") with no further product-level split, unlike the four named product segments. Profit is disclosed at segment level, not just revenue — segment profit before tax, segment assets, and segment liabilities are all reported for every segment in both the CAS and IFRS filings, a meaningfully deeper disclosure than a revenue-only segment note. One real gap: geography and business segment are not cross-tabulated — the geographic-revenue note (`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(2), p.225`) breaks external revenue into 8 regions (Mainland China, Americas, Australia, South Asia, Europe, Southeast Asia, Middle East & Africa, Japan, Others) and non-current assets into 2 buckets (Mainland China vs Others), but discloses no profit by geography and no segment-by-region matrix, so a reader cannot see, for example, how much of Air Solutions' profit comes from China versus the rest of the world.

## 4. Citations

- Segment revenue/profit by product line, IFRS cross-check, FY2025 and FY2024 (restated) comparatives: `FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4 (經營分部資料), pp.227-228`

## business-model / 04_unit-economics.md

_Source: `business-model/04_unit-economics.md`_

# Unit Economics — HAIER

## 1. Natural Unit

The natural economic unit for Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions (the dominant segment — 41.7% of FY2025 external revenue, 43.4% of segment profit before tax, per `03_segment-map.md`) is the **appliance unit sold** — a refrigerator/freezer or a kitchen appliance (range hood, cooktop, oven, dishwasher, microwave, built-in fridge). Haier Smart Home discloses no unit-count or average-selling-price (ASP) figure for either product line — only aggregate RMB revenue, cost, and profit — so this table is built on product-line revenue, gross margin, and segment margin as the best available per-unit proxies, not on a true per-appliance dollar figure. The table below covers **Refrigerators/Freezers** (电冰箱/冰箱冷柜), the larger of the segment's two disclosed product lines (RMB84,487mn of the segment's RMB125,975mn combined revenue, `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1), pp.222-223`). The secondary unit type is the **kitchen appliance** (厨电: range hoods, cooktops, ovens, built-in fridges, dishwashers, microwaves) — its own gross margin and segment margin are given inline for comparison, and it moved in the opposite direction (deteriorating) over the same year.

## 2. Unit Economics Table

Basis: Refrigerators/Freezers product line (电冰箱), FY2025 vs FY2024, RMB. Kitchen appliances (厨电) figures given in the Evidence column for comparison.

| Unit Economic | Value | Period | Direction vs Prior Year | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue per unit (ASP) | Not disclosed — no unit-count or ASP figure published for the segment or the product line | — | Unknown | Company discloses only aggregate revenue (RMB84,165mn for 电冰箱, RMB84,487mn for the 冰箱/冷柜 segment); no "units sold" line exists in the segment note or MD&A. Isolated hero-model call-outs exist (e.g. "麦浪系列冰箱...总销量突破100万台" — the Mile Wave fridge line's cumulative retail sales passed 1 million units) but are single-SKU marketing disclosures, not a segment-wide volume, and are not usable as a segment ASP denominator `[FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Business Review, line ~193]` |
| Gross margin per unit (% of revenue, no physical unit count available) | 30.15% (Refrigerators); 28.57% (Kitchen appliances) | FY2025 | Deteriorating — Refrigerators −0.62pp YoY (30.15% vs 30.77% FY2024); Kitchen appliances −0.76pp YoY (28.57% vs 29.34% FY2024) | `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), 收入和成本分析 — 主营业务分产品情况, p.42` (电冰箱: revenue RMB84,165.1mn, cost RMB58,788.0mn, gross margin 30.15%, stated YoY change −0.62pp; 厨电: revenue RMB41,322.8mn, cost RMB29,515.4mn, gross margin 28.57%, stated YoY change −0.76pp) |
| Contribution margin per unit — proxy: segment profit margin (segment profit before tax ÷ segment external revenue; nets out SG&A/R&D allocated to the segment, but not financial expense, fair-value items, or tax — see Note 11 scope note) | 7.24% (冰箱/冷柜 segment, combining refrigerators+freezers); 6.97% (厨电 segment) | FY2025 | Refrigerators/freezers segment: slightly Improving (7.24% vs 7.17% FY2024, +0.07pp) despite gross-margin compression — implies opex efficiency partly offset raw-material cost pressure. Kitchen appliances segment: Deteriorating (6.97% vs 7.73% FY2024, −0.76pp) | `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1), pp.222-223`: 冰箱/冷柜 segment profit RMB6,114.8mn / external revenue RMB84,486.7mn = 7.24% (FY2025) vs RMB5,974.5mn / RMB83,343.5mn = 7.17% (FY2024); 厨电 segment profit RMB2,892.9mn / revenue RMB41,488.1mn = 6.97% (FY2025) vs RMB3,179.0mn / RMB41,119.1mn = 7.73% (FY2024) |
| Cost to acquire / build the unit (per-unit capex, per-unit input cost) | Not disclosed — no per-unit or per-line capex, capacity-unit cost, or D&A figure published by segment or product line | — | Unknown | Note 11 explicitly scopes segment assets/liabilities/profit but discloses no segment-level capex or depreciation & amortisation add-back; the only capacity data point found is aggregate and for a different product (Thailand air-conditioning plant, "年产能600万台" — 6 million units/year), not refrigerators `[FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Business Review, line ~1457]`. Segment assets are disclosed in aggregate (RMB55,796mn assets / RMB81,067mn liabilities for the combined food-storage segment, FY2025) but not decomposable into a per-unit build cost |
| Payback period or unit lifetime | Not disclosed | — | Unknown | No warranty-driven replacement-cycle, product-lifetime, or cohort/vintage data disclosed in the annual report, MD&A, or transcripts in the data pool. The China offline market-share figures (47.7% refrigerators) cited in `03_segment-map.md` support a qualitative "replacement demand" argument but carry no period figure that would let a payback calculation be built |

## 3. Value Creation Read

**Unclear — the core per-unit math (contribution margin × unit lifetime vs. acquisition cost) cannot be built because Haier discloses no unit volume, no ASP, and no per-unit build cost for either product line.** What the filings do support: the refrigerators/freezers segment is unambiguously profitable at the aggregate level (segment margin 7.24% of external revenue, up 0.07pp YoY) even as its gross margin compressed 0.62pp on rising input costs (cost growth of 2.02% outpaced revenue growth of 1.11% for the 电冰箱 product line, `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42`) — opex efficiency, not pricing power, is doing the offsetting work this year. The segment also runs with segment liabilities (RMB81,067mn) exceeding segment assets (RMB55,796mn) by RMB25,271mn `[FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1)]` — consistent with a negative-working-capital manufacturing model where suppliers effectively fund a slice of operations, a structural positive for cash generation, though this is a segment-level balance-sheet observation, not itself a per-unit value-creation proof, and it is not close to a "returns" calculation given segment liabilities mix trade payables with other items the filing does not decompose (Inference, not from filings, on the exact driver of the gap). The single most valuable missing disclosure is unit volume (or ASP) by product line — without it, "does each new refrigerator sold create value" cannot be separated from "is the aggregate refrigerator business profitable," which the filings do answer (yes, at a thin and slightly improving margin) but which is not the same question.

Kitchen appliances, the segment's secondary unit type, reads differently: gross margin (−0.76pp) and segment margin (−0.76pp) moved down in lockstep, with no offsetting opex efficiency this year — a cleaner (if still aggregate, not per-unit) deteriorating read.

## 4. Sensitivity

Given a 7.2% segment margin for refrigerators/freezers, the business is running on thin operating leverage, so either a price move or a cost move swings profit by a large multiple of the margin itself. Raw-material cost is the more historically volatile of the two: the filing itself attributes the FY2025 gross-margin compression to input-cost pressure (steel/aluminum/plastic, flagged as the segment's "Main Risk" in `03_segment-map.md`), and cost already grew faster than revenue this year (+2.02% vs +1.11%). Doing the arithmetic: a 20% rise in the 电冰箱 product line's COGS (RMB58,788mn), if not passed through in price, adds RMB11,758mn of cost — nearly double the entire 冰箱/冷柜 segment's RMB6,115mn FY2025 profit, which would flip the segment from a ~RMB6.1bn profit to roughly a RMB5.6bn loss on this single input alone `[calculated from FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42 and Note 11(1); Inference, not from filings, on the assumption of zero price pass-through]`. A 20% ASP increase, by the same logic, would add roughly RMB16,897mn to segment revenue (20% of RMB84,487mn external revenue) — a swing of similar or larger magnitude in the other direction if costs held flat. Both are Inference, not from filings (the filing provides no elasticity or pass-through data), but the arithmetic shows the segment's thin ~7% margin leaves almost no room to absorb an unmitigated input-cost shock of this size, which is the more evidence-grounded tail risk given the filing's own attribution of this year's margin move to cost, not price.

# Customer And Geography Map — HAIER

Company: Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. — dual-primary listed on SSE (A-share, 600690, China ASBE/CAS basis) and HKEX (H-share, 6690, IFRS basis), plus a Frankfurt D-share and a Level-I ADR. Figures below are FY2025 (ended Dec-31-2025) unless stated. Reporting currency is RMB (CNY); no cross-currency conversion is needed as both filings report in RMB.

## 1. Customer Map

Haier Smart Home is a business-to-consumer household-appliance maker. It does not sell to a small set of named corporate customers the way a component supplier or contract manufacturer would — it sells through mass-market retail and distribution channels to millions of end consumers. The company's own filings confirm this structure and give one aggregate concentration figure; they do not name individual customers.

| Customer Type | Importance (% of revenue if disclosed) | Long-term Contract? (Y/N/Not disclosed) | Evidence | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Top 5 customers combined (names not disclosed) | 19.6% of FY2025 total sales (RMB 5,927,312,850 combined); related-party sales within this group = 0% of total sales | Not disclosed — no minimum-purchase or contract-term language given | FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, China ASBE), Section 3(7)A, p.43 | Low. Company explicitly checked "not applicable" for: (i) any single customer >50% of sales, (ii) new entrants in the top-5 list, and (iii) "severe dependence on a small number of customers" — FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, China ASBE), Section 3(7)B, p.44 |
| China domestic retail/distribution network — franchise/specialty stores, appliance-chain retailers, integrated-store retailers, plus online (own Haier Smart Home App/Tmall flagship store, and B2B2C platforms such as JD.com) | Not disclosed by channel; China overall = 48.5% of FY2025 revenue (see Section 2) | Not disclosed. Company states distributors/retailers/online platforms "may place orders with us at such time and in such quantities as they deem appropriate" — no minimum-commitment or contract-term disclosed | FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), "Relationship with Customers", p.80 | Medium. Relationships described as "stable" with "no material breach" of terms, but orders are placed at the retailer's/distributor's own discretion — no binding volume commitment |
| North America & Europe retail/online channels (Haier's two largest overseas markets; includes wholly-owned subsidiary brands GE Appliances (US, acquired 2016) and Candy Hoover/Haier Smart Home UK & I (Europe)) | Not disclosed by individual retailer; North America = 26.4% and Europe = 12.7% of FY2025 revenue combined (see Section 2) | Not disclosed. Retailers in Europe are selected on market share, market positioning and reputation; relationships described as "stable," no contract-term or volume-commitment disclosed | FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), "Relationship with Customers", p.80 | Medium. Same discretionary-order structure as China; concentrated in "local retailers," unnamed |
| Named entities on the Capital IQ customer list (Candy Hoover Group Srl, Controladora Mabe, Haier US Appliance Solutions/GE Appliances, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries-Haier Qingdao JV, The Warehouse Group NZ, and several Haier-affiliated trading/distribution units) | Not disclosed as a % of revenue — this list is a relationship/ownership map, not a revenue-concentration disclosure | Not disclosed | Capital IQ Customers export ("Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Customers.xls") — vendor relationship data, not a filing | Low informativeness for concentration: most of these are wholly- or majority-owned subsidiaries/JVs (intra-group), or a single overseas distributor (Warehouse Group NZ, Hnr Company Pakistan) with no revenue % attached |

Shares sum to ~100.0% (rounding).

## 3. Concentration Flags

| Concentration Flag | Triggered (Y/N) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| One customer >20% of revenue | N | Company's own top-5-combined figure is 19.6% of FY2025 sales, and it explicitly certifies no single customer exceeded 50% of sales and there is no "severe dependence on a small number of customers" — FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, China ASBE), Section 3(7)A/B, p.43-44. Since even the top FIVE combined are below 20%, no single customer can exceed 20% |
| Top 3 customers >40% of revenue | N | Top 5 customers combined = 19.6% of sales; the top 3 must be a subset of that and so cannot reach 40% — FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, China ASBE), Section 3(7)A, p.43 |
| One geography >50% of revenue | N | Mainland China is the largest geography at 48.5% of FY2025 revenue — below 50%, but close, and was above 50% as recently as FY2020 (51.3%) — FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4, p.233; Capital IQ Segments export (FY2020 figure) |
| One customer or geography >30% with no long-term contract disclosed | Y | Mainland China is 48.5% of FY2025 revenue (>30%), and no long-term contract or minimum-volume commitment is disclosed for the underlying China retail/distribution channel — the filing states distributors/retailers/online platforms order "at such time and in such quantities as they deem appropriate" — FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS), Note 4 p.233 and "Relationship with Customers" p.80 |

## 4. Read

This is a geography-concentrated business, not a customer-concentrated one: no single customer or small customer group is material (top 5 combined are only 19.6% of sales, certified as not severely dependent), but Mainland China alone still supplies 48.5% of FY2025 revenue — just under the 50% single-country threshold and above 50% as recently as FY2020. The China concentration is naked, not contractually secured: the filing itself describes distributors, retail chains and online platforms as ordering "at such time and in such quantities as they deem appropriate," with no minimum-volume or contract-term commitment disclosed for any channel, in China or overseas. The single biggest dependency the synthesizer should know: just under half of group revenue still depends on discretionary, non-contracted order flow from the Chinese domestic appliance retail and distribution channel, with North America (26.4%, built substantially on the GE Appliances brand) as the second-largest and similarly uncommitted geography.
