## earnings — module synthesis

_Source: `earnings/99_earnings-synthesis.md`_

# Earnings Module — HAIER (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Haier's earnings are decelerating: revenue growth cooled from +12.57% in FY2023 to +5.71% in FY2025 and turned outright negative (-6.86% year-on-year) in Q1 2026, while gross, EBITDA, and EBIT margins all fell together off a FY2024 peak. The biggest driver is raw-material cost inflation — 84% of appliance-segment cost of sales, worth -178bps of revenue before mitigation — compounded by the fading China trade-in subsidy, the single largest revenue lever at 48.5% of sales. Consensus has already been cut sharply (FY2026 EPS down roughly 14% in six months) yet the last two reported quarters still missed that lowered bar, with revision breadth still net negative. The biggest risk is that roughly RMB25 billion (about 8% of revenue) of receivable factoring and supplier finance underpins a cash-conversion cycle that has narrowed from -10.8 to -1.2 days. Red-flag severity: Material concerns. The setup favors a miss into the Aug-27-2026 print.

## 1. Earnings Verdict

- **Verdict: Earnings decelerating**
- Earnings quality /100: **66** *(from 06_earnings-quality — "mostly clean but some working capital or adjustment noise")*
- Consensus setup /100 *(higher = more beatable)*: **28** *(derived by this synthesis from 04's qualitative "Bar is high — miss risk elevated" read: consensus was cut sharply over the last 6-12 months but the last two reported quarters still missed the already-lowered bar, and revision breadth remains net negative heading into the next print — this is a genuinely hard, not easy, bar to clear. No hard partial-data cap applies here since consensus data itself IS present in the pool; the low score reflects the qualitative bar assessment, not a data gap)*
- Earnings volatility /100 *(higher = worse)*: **62** *(from 07_earnings-sensitivity)*
- Next-quarter setup: **Favors miss** *(from 05_beat-miss-setup §8)*
- Biggest earnings driver (one line): Raw-material commodity cost inflation (steel/aluminium/copper/plastics, 84% of appliance-segment cost of sales) — the single highest-ranked sensitivity variable (avg impact ~RMB5,350mn EBITDA-equivalent), with no disclosed pass-through mechanism to customers, mechanically linked to (not independent of) the cost-reduction program that is currently offsetting it.
- Biggest earnings risk (one line): Consensus has already been cut sharply (FY2026 EPS down ~14% over six months) yet the last two reported quarters both missed that already-lowered bar, with revision breadth still net negative (EPS 1 up/11 down) heading into the Aug-27-2026 print — meaning the Street has not finished cutting, and the module's own case against extrapolating this forward rests on one unverified management claim (ex-North-America Q1 2026 operating profit +10%) never reconciled to a segment P&L.
- **Red-flag severity verdict (from `08_earnings-red-flags.md`, reported verbatim): Material concerns** — 35 flags triggered (0 Critical / 12 High / 23 Medium / 3 Low / 3 Unclear).

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** China domestic demand — 48.5% of FY2025 revenue and the single biggest revenue driver by size and correlation — is deteriorating on both a cyclical basis (Q1 2026 China retail ex-3C -6.2% YoY, AVC data) and a structural one (management's own words: 2026 industry growth "expected to face pressure" under "the high base" the 2024-2025 trade-in subsidy created) [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §7]. This is not a modelled risk; it is a company-stated headwind already visible in the most recent quarter.
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** Management's own Q1 2026 claim that, excluding North America, operating profit grew over 10% [`2026 First Quarter Report, p.2`] — if true, the consolidated miss was concentrated in a dated, weather-and-tariff-driven regional shock rather than a broad-based deterioration, and China's share gains (refrigerator 47.7% offline, +3.6pp; washer 47.4%; water heater 32.5%, all gained in a shrinking market) are cushioning, not merely masking, the domestic decline [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §3-4]. Cash conversion has also never broken down in five years (CFO/EBITDA never below 93.9%) and the company's own non-GAAP adjustments run conservative, not inflationary [`06_earnings-quality.md` §2, §7].
- **Single killer risk specific to earnings quality & the beat/miss setup:** The North America "one-time shock" narrative is unverified and unreconciled to a segment P&L — if it is wrong (tariffs persist rather than "gradually ease" as management's own forward-looking, unverified claim states, or the weather-driven demand drop masked a structural softening), the single reason this module has for not extrapolating two consecutive misses forward disappears, compounding directly with China's already-deteriorating demand [`05_beat-miss-setup.md` §10; `08_earnings-red-flags.md` §7].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** Two consecutive reported quarters (FQ4 2025 and FQ1 2026) missed an ALREADY-lowered consensus on both revenue and EPS, and the FY2025 full-year print itself missed EPS by -7.1% [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6]; revision breadth remains net negative into the next print (EPS 1 up/11 down; gross margin 3 up/20 down) [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §5]. This is standing, already-printed evidence against the bull case, not a hypothetical.

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| revenue-drivers | China domestic demand is the single biggest revenue driver by size and correlation, and it is deteriorating | A 10-20% swing in China (48.5% of revenue) moves 4.85-9.7pp of group revenue; management's own FY2026 outlook flags a "high base" pressuring growth |
| margin-drivers | Past the FY2024 margin/growth peak, mid-decelerating phase, with a fading one-time policy tailwind | Raw materials (84% of appliance-segment COGS) would have driven a -178bps gross-margin hit alone, roughly 72% offset by a cost-reduction program explicitly labelled "not guaranteed to repeat" |

| earnings-sensitivity | Volatility score 62/100 (inverted, higher = worse) | Raw-material cost inflation is the single highest-sensitivity variable (~RMB5,350mn avg EBITDA-equivalent impact) and is mechanically linked, not independent, from the cost-reduction program that offsets it |

## 3. Reconciliation

Two genuine internal tensions were surfaced by upstream agents themselves, not papered over, and are reconciled here conservatively per CLAUDE.md §4:

1. **D&A basis conflict (`03_margin-drivers.md` §2-3):** COGS-embedded depreciation rose +12.66% YoY (linked to the Air Solutions segment's asset base nearly doubling on the CCR/Kwikot acquisitions) while CapIQ's broader total-D&A measure fell -7.3% YoY. The two bases are not reconcilable from this pool. This synthesis treats the narrower, filing-sourced, segment-linked COGS-embedded D&A trend (rising) as the more conservative read per CLAUDE.md §4, since it ties directly to a named, verifiable acquisition-driven asset build, while the CapIQ aggregate is an unexplained residual improvement. This affects only the EBITDA-margin-vs-EBIT-margin decline gap (-102bps vs -76bps), not the headline gross-margin or revenue findings.

2. **Cash strength vs. counterparty concentration (`06_earnings-quality.md` vs. `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md`, flagged at `08_earnings-red-flags.md` §2.9/#32):** `06_earnings-quality` concludes cash conversion is strong on an accounting basis (CFO/EBITDA never below 93.9% in five years) — this is correct as far as it goes, but it does not examine that roughly 57% of group cash (RMB33,988mn) sits with the controlling shareholder's own affiliated finance company, and related-party borrowing from that entity rose roughly 19x YoY (RMB196mn → RMB3,767mn). This is a coverage gap between modules, not a factual disagreement — the earnings-quality score (66/100) should be read as "the accrual-to-cash bridge is genuinely strong" alongside, not instead of, "a material share of that cash sits with a related party," a point this earnings module cannot itself score but must not let disappear.

Beyond these two self-flagged tensions, *no material disagreements exist between specialists on the direction of the earnings setup* — 01 through 07 converge on deceleration, margin pressure, and elevated miss risk (`08_earnings-red-flags.md` §1, "Contradictions Between Agents").

**Conflict between the red-flag agent's verdict and this synthesis:** none. The red-flag agent's "Material concerns" verdict and this synthesis's "Earnings decelerating" verdict point the same direction and are mutually consistent — both rest on the same underlying evidence (deceleration already reported, not modelled; consensus cuts not yet validated by results; the optimistic case resting on one unverified claim).

| Transcript role filled ONLY by a sell-side proxy (no verbatim) | N — no proxy exists at all (this is the stricter "no call-derived source at all" case, distinct from this row) | Earnings clarity | Same cap value (max 70) reached via the row above, not this trigger |
| Only inferred sensitivities | Partial — the single largest-magnitude variable (raw-material cost inflation) is agent-derived with Medium confidence (no company-wide commodity/EBITDA sensitivity is disclosed), but three of the seven sensitivity variables (interest rate, RMB/USD, RMB/EUR) are company-disclosed with High confidence | Earnings volatility confidence | Not a full module-wide "Low" — confidence on the #1-ranked variable specifically is capped at Medium (already applied upstream in `07_earnings-sensitivity.md` §2, §7); the module's overall volatility score (62/100) is not further discounted |

## 5. Earnings Setup Summary

### Revenue Setup

The current revenue trajectory is not sustainable at its recent FY2023-2024 pace, and a meaningful share of it was never organic to begin with: FY2025's fastest-growing segments (Air Solutions +9.6%, Water Solutions +10.8%) both carry an unquantified inorganic overlay from the 2024-vintage CCR and Kwikot acquisitions, and the single fastest-growing revenue bucket in the whole company (Other Business, +18.5-19.9%) is a near-zero-margin channel/distribution line, not core appliance demand. The single factor that would flip the direction is China domestic demand: at 48.5% of revenue and already falling roughly 6% YoY on an industry basis in Q1 2026, it is the one lever big enough and correlated enough to move group revenue by several points on its own, and management's own words ("high base" pressure into 2026) point the same way it is already moving. There is a real gap between the reported FY2025 growth story and the underlying organic picture: two of six named growth contributors (Air Solutions +1.65pp, Water Solutions +0.60pp of the 5.71pp total) embed an unquantified M&A boost, and the largest single contributor by geography (Europe, +2.24pp) and by segment (Other Business, +2.14pp) are not the deteriorating China bucket — meaning FY2025's headline growth was already leaning on drivers other than the core China franchise before Q1 2026's outright decline arrived.

### Margin Setup

Current margins are not at a sustainable run-rate — they sit past a FY2024 peak (EBITDA margin 9.80% → 8.78%, EBIT margin 7.66% → 6.90%) that was itself inflated by the now-fading China trade-in subsidy cycle, so FY2024 should not be used as a normalization anchor. If raw-material costs move adversely by another 10-20% at the current pace (Q4 2025's copper/bulk-material rise already cost -178bps of revenue before mitigation), it takes the largest single bite out of consolidated margins by a wide margin — larger than the entire observed -110bps gross-margin decline — because the offsetting cost-reduction program is a discretionary management lever explicitly labelled "not guaranteed to repeat," not a structural cost advantage. Management has no contractual or structural margin-protection mechanism: business-model `06_value-chain.md` confirms there is no escalator, indexed-pricing, or cost-plus clause with any customer, so Haier is a price-taker on raw materials and has already absorbed, not passed through, cost inflation in two consecutive periods (FY2025 and Q1 2026).

### Quality Check

The single largest gap between reported and economic earnings is not a headline non-GAAP adjustment — the company's own adjustments run conservative (deducting non-recurring gains, not adding back real costs) — it is the working-capital financing scaffolding underneath an already-thinning cash-conversion cycle: roughly RMB25bn (~8% of revenue) of receivable factoring, bill discounting, and supplier-finance arrangements sit beneath a cash conversion cycle that narrowed from -10.8 days (FY2023) to -1.2 days (FY2025), and this gap is widening, not narrowing, as the buffer between customer collections and supplier payments keeps shrinking. The recurring, ~5-7%-of-net-profit government-subsidy stream that management excludes from "adjusted" earnings every year for three straight years is genuinely one-time by the CSRC's own definition but behaves economically like recurring income given its stability across three years — a real gray area, not a clean "one-off." To model normalized earnings for next year, start from GAAP reported net profit, not the company's adjusted figure — the adjusted number moves in the conservative direction and both figures track closely (a ~4.9% gap), but the accrual-quality flag (RF-EQ-001: revenue outgrowing CFO for two years, receivables outgrowing revenue in two of three years) means neither figure should be extrapolated without the cash-conversion-cycle caveat above.

### Consensus Bar

For Haier to beat the current bar by a material margin, North America would need to genuinely normalize post-weather-shock AND the cost-reduction program would need to sustain its FY2025 offset rate against continued raw-material inflation — a conjunction of two things going right, not one, since the two named beat scenarios (North America normalization, cost-program repeat) are largely independent of each other and neither alone has been validated by a reported quarter yet. The bar is most likely set too high relative to where results have actually landed: consensus has been cut sharply (FY2026 EPS down ~14% over six months) but the last two reported prints still missed that already-lowered number, meaning the Street's cuts have consistently lagged the deterioration rather than overshooting it. A meaningful share of the current consensus revenue base (FY2026 revenue consensus implies only +2.24% growth, itself already a sharp deceleration from FY2025's own +5.71%) is anchored to the assumption that China's subsidy-driven demand pull-forward from 2024-2025 does not reverse further — exactly the mechanism management itself has flagged as a headwind for 2026.

## 5b. Leverage & Capital Structure

Leverage is within normal range and did not change materially during the period — no dedicated treatment required. Haier remained net-cash on a strict basis throughout FY2021-FY2025 (net debt/EBITDA ranging from -1.24x to -0.19x), and the year-over-year move in that ratio (FY2024 -0.57x to FY2025 -0.19x, a +0.38x shift) falls well short of the 1.0x trigger for material leverage change; no evidence in this pool indicates total debt rose more than 50% YoY. The one related trend worth flagging for the record, though it does not meet either leverage trigger: the net-cash cushion has thinned steadily since FY2022 on both the strict basis and CapIQ's broader cash-inclusive basis, and separately (a capital-allocation/governance finding, not a leverage one) roughly 57% of group cash sits with the controlling shareholder's own finance company, with related-party borrowing from that entity up roughly 19x YoY [`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` §1, surfaced at `08_earnings-red-flags.md` §2.9].

## 6. Key Numbers

- Revenue growth rate: FY2025 +5.71% YoY (RMB302,346.8mn); Q1 2026 standalone -6.86% YoY (RMB73,686.7mn) [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, §3]
- EBITDA margin: FY2025 8.78%, down 102bps from FY2024's 9.80% peak [`01_historical-financials.md` §1]
- EPS: FY2025 diluted RMB2.10 (adjusted ex-non-recurring RMB2.02); Q1 2026 RMB0.50, -15.25% YoY [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, §3; `06_earnings-quality.md` §4]
- CFO / EBITDA: 98.0% FY2025, 97.6% on a trailing-twelve-months basis to Mar-2026 — never below 93.9% in five years [`06_earnings-quality.md` §1-2]
- Biggest driver current level: raw materials = 84.0% of appliance-segment cost of sales (up from 82.0% FY2024), the highest share in the disclosed history [`03_margin-drivers.md` §2, §8]
- Consensus gap: FY2026 EPS consensus CNY2.13 (down ~14.1% from six months ago); FY2026 revenue consensus CNY309,111mn implies only +2.24% growth, a sharp deceleration from FY2025's own +5.71% [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4, §3]
- Estimate revision direction: net negative into the next print — EPS 1 up/11 down, gross margin 3 up/20 down over the trailing ~3 months [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §5]
- Earnings volatility score: 62/100 (inverted — higher = worse) [`07_earnings-sensitivity.md` §7]

## 7. What Would Change The Earnings Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Upgrade It | What Would Downgrade It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earnings decelerating | The Aug-27-2026 H1 print beats the (already-cut) consensus on both revenue and EPS, AND management's ex-North-America +10% operating-profit claim is corroborated by an actual segment-level margin recovery; a reversal in China's "high base" demand deterioration | A third consecutive miss against consensus; evidence that North America softness is structural (tariffs persisting, not "gradually easing") rather than a one-time weather shock; the cash-conversion cycle turning positive, signalling the factoring/supplier-finance buffer is being drawn down rather than supporting genuine collections | The Aug-27-2026 H1 2026 results (two weeks away); a segment-level P&L reconciling the ex-North-America claim; a company-wide commodity/EBITDA sensitivity disclosure; a post-print consensus revision update |

## 8. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Dominant earnings trend: deceleration confirmed across revenue (FY2023 +12.57% → FY2025 +5.71% → Q1 2026 -6.86%), margins (FY2024 peak, FY2025 decline across gross/EBITDA/EBIT), and the beat/miss record (two consecutive misses against an already-cut bar). Biggest driver: raw-material commodity cost inflation (84% of appliance-segment COGS), mechanically linked to the cost-reduction program that offsets it — read the two as one combined exposure, not two independently mitigating factors [High flags #4, #11, #12].
- Earnings are largely clean and cash-backed on an accrual-to-cash basis (CFO/EBITDA never below 93.9% in five years, conservative non-GAAP adjustments) but that conclusion sits atop a narrowing buffer: the cash conversion cycle has thinned from -10.8 to -1.2 days and roughly RMB25bn (~8% of revenue) of factoring/supplier-finance underlies it [High flags #9, #10]. RF-EQ-001 (rising accruals divergent from cash earnings) fired in `06_earnings-quality.md` §6 and is propagated here as a standalone forensic tag.
- Consensus bar assessment: high, hard to beat. Consensus has already been cut sharply (FY2026 EPS -14% over six months) yet the last two reported quarters both missed that already-lowered bar [High flags #6], and revision breadth remains net negative into the next print [High flag #7] — treat any "the bar has already been lowered enough" read as unproven.
- No disclosed commodity-cost pass-through mechanism exists — margin has no offsetting price lever, and two consecutive periods (FY2025, Q1 2026) already show unmitigated cost absorption [High flag #5].
- China domestic demand (48.5% of revenue, the single biggest revenue driver) is deteriorating on both a cyclical and a management-flagged structural basis ("high base" from the fading subsidy) [High flag #3]; gross/EBITDA/EBIT margins all inflected downward together off a FY2024 peak that should not be read as the normalized run-rate [High flags #1, #2].
- Next-quarter setup: favors a miss, per `05_beat-miss-setup.md` §8. The module's own case against extrapolating the last two misses forward rests entirely on one unverified management claim (ex-North-America Q1 2026 operating profit +10%, never reconciled to a segment P&L) [High flag #8] — treat any "beat likely" lean with this caveat attached.
- Second-quarter look-ahead (per `05_beat-miss-setup.md` §9): visibility past the Aug-27 print is limited (no formal guidance); Q3 2026 likely swaps which of the two named headwinds dominates (North America potentially easing if tariffs recede as management claims, China's "high base" still pressuring for the full year) rather than clearly improving or worsening overall.
- Top sensitivity variable and its current direction: raw-material commodity cost inflation, currently a headwind (Q4 2025 copper/bulk-material rises cited by the company as ongoing) [`07_earnings-sensitivity.md` §3-4].
- Partial-data cap applied: earnings clarity capped at 70 module-wide — no verbatim transcript or sell-side proxy exists for any period after Q3 2019, so no management tone/candor read is available anywhere in this module [High flag context, Medium-severity data-completeness flags #13-15].
- Biggest missing data point: a company-wide commodity/EBITDA sensitivity disclosure — the single highest-magnitude sensitivity variable (raw-material costs) is agent-derived with only Medium confidence, not company-disclosed [Medium flag #29].
- What would change the verdict: see Section 7 — resolved one way or the other within two weeks by the Aug-27-2026 H1 2026 print.
- Coverage gap flagged for the synthesizer to reconcile across modules: this earnings module's "cash is strong" read (CFO/EBITDA basis) does not examine that ~57% of group cash sits with the controlling shareholder's own finance company, with related-party borrowing from that entity up ~19x YoY [`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` §1, `08_earnings-red-flags.md` §2.9].
- Framing risk: the setup sits atop a business-model verdict of a "narrow, eroding moat" (gross margin -460bps over 5 years); a near-term "stabilizing" earnings read should not be conflated with a healthy, widening-moat business [Medium flag #34]. Goodwill (25.3% of parent equity, 76% concentrated in the 2016 GE Appliances deal) sits directly behind North America, the segment currently absorbing the tariff hit, and is not covered by this module's own EBITDA→CFO→FCF bridge [Medium flag #35].
- Red-flag severity verdict (reported verbatim, not softened): **Material concerns**.

## 9. Simple Summary

- Revenue: growing more slowly every year since FY2023, and turned negative (-6.86% YoY) in the most recent quarter — the main driver is China's fading trade-in subsidy and a soft property market.
- Margins: peaked in FY2024, fell in FY2025 — the main driver is rising raw-material costs (steel, copper, aluminium) that the company cannot pass through to customers.
- Earnings are mostly clean — cash backing them has never broken down — but a big chunk of that clean look (~8% of revenue) rests on receivable factoring and supplier-finance deals, and that support cushion is shrinking fast.
- The consensus bar is hard to beat: analysts already cut their numbers a lot, but the company still missed the lowered numbers the last two times it reported.
- Next quarter (due Aug-27-2026) is set up to favor a miss — the main hope for a better result rests on one unverified management claim about North America.
- Biggest single swing factor: raw-material costs, and it moves against Haier with no price-lever to offset it.
- Earnings are meaningfully sensitive to a small number of inputs (volatility score 62/100, where higher is worse) — not extreme, but real.
- This module is useful: it gives the master synthesizer a clear, evidence-backed "decelerating, miss-favored, cash-mostly-clean-but-thinning" read with a two-week-away catalyst to test it against.

- **Active partial-data caps:**

## earnings / 01_historical-financials.md

# Historical Financials — HAIER (Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd., SHSE: 600690 / SEHK: 6690)

**Jurisdiction note:** Haier Smart Home is a mainland-China-incorporated, dual-primary-listed filer (Shanghai Stock Exchange A-shares + Hong Kong Stock Exchange H-shares, plus a Frankfurt D-share line). The A-share annual and quarterly filings are prepared under China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE); the H-share annual report restates to IFRS, but the filings state net profit and equity attributable to owners "are not different" between the two bases [FY2025 Annual Report (H-share/IFRS), Apr-27-2026, contents page]. All figures below are in RMB (CNY) millions unless stated otherwise, fiscal year ending December 31. Where a number is drawn from the CapIQ workbook export rather than a company filing, it is labelled "CapIQ export" — no `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker, so these are this agent's own sourced reads, not a mechanically-pinned sidecar value.

**Data limitation flagged up front:** the only call-derived commentary source in the pool is two ~7-year-stale 2019 transcripts (no probative value) and no sell-side proxy exists, so all narrative colour below comes from filings' MD&A, not a call — consistent with the `00_earnings-data-triage` finding. Separately, Haier's quarterly filings (CAS "quarterly report" format) disclose only revenue, net profit attributable to shareholders, net profit excluding non-recurring items, EPS, and operating cash flow at the discrete-quarter level — **not** a quarterly income statement with COGS/gross margin or EBITDA. Gross margin is disclosed narratively only for the standalone latest quarter and cumulative year-to-date; EBITDA is never disclosed on a quarterly basis. This caps what Section 3 can show — flagged in place, not silently left blank.

Both bases show the same direction: Haier's net-cash cushion has shrunk every year since FY2022, i.e., leverage has been rising off a very light base even though the company remains net-cash on both measures through FY2025.

**Gross margin reconciliation flag:** the company's own FY2025 P&L movement table gives 营业成本 (cost of revenue) of RMB 221,738.8mn against revenue of RMB 302,346.8mn — a gross margin of 26.66% — versus the CapIQ-derived 26.33% shown above (COGS 222,732.5mn); FY2024 shows a similar ~34bp gap (27.82% company-derived vs. 27.48% CapIQ) [FY2025 Annual Report (A-share/CAS), Mar-26-2026, p.40, "利润表及现金流量表相关科目变动分析表"]. The gap is consistent in direction and small (30–35bps); it likely reflects a different classification of a minor cost line (e.g., taxes and surcharges) between CapIQ's standard template and the company's own COGS line. The CapIQ-based series is used throughout for cross-year comparability since FY2021–FY2022 company-reported COGS is not in this data pool; the company's own audited FY2025/FY2024 figures are the higher-tier source where the two diverge (§4).

## 2. TTM Snapshot

Latest TTM = 12 months ended Mar-31-2026 (CapIQ "LTM" column, reconciling Q1 2026's reported figures into the trailing period). A true prior-TTM ending Mar-31-2025 cannot be cleanly computed from this pool: it would require a standalone Q1 2024 figure, and the only Q1 2024 number available (CapIQ quarterly consensus "actual," RMB 68,977.5mn) pre-dates the Dec-2024/Mar-2025 restatement from the Youjin and COSMOPlat business combinations under common control, so combining it with the restated FY2024 total would silently mix two accounting bases (§15). Instead, **FY2025 (12 months ended Dec-31-2025)** is shown as the nearest reconcilable prior 12-month window — it overlaps 9 of the latest TTM's 12 months rather than being a clean non-overlapping prior year, and that overlap is the reason the "change" column reads small.

Note: net debt is a point-in-time balance-sheet figure, not a TTM flow — the two dates shown are Mar-31-2026 and Dec-31-2025, three months apart, not a 12-month change. The company adjusts **net profit and basic EPS only** — for non-recurring items defined under China's CSRC disclosure rules (asset-disposal gains/losses, government subsidies unrelated to core operations, fair-value gains on equity investments, and similar one-off items) [FY2025 Annual Report (A-share/CAS), Mar-26-2026, p.12–13 and p.15 ("非经常性损益项目和金额")]. It does **not** publish an adjusted/non-GAAP EBITDA or EBIT.

Whether this is a repeating seasonal pattern or specific to 2025 cannot be established from one year of clean data.

## 6. Key Trend Summary

Revenue growth is **volatile, not smoothly decelerating or accelerating**: +7.25% (FY2022) → +12.57% (FY2023, the strongest year) → +4.31% (FY2024) → +5.71% (FY2025) → +1.25% on a trailing-twelve-month basis to Mar-2026 [CapIQ Key Stats, LTM growth-over-prior-year] → an outright −6.86% year-on-year decline in the standalone Q1 2026 quarter [2026 First Quarter Report, p.2]. Margins **expanded through FY2024 and then compressed in FY2025**: gross margin fell steadily from 30.9% (FY2021) to 26.3% (FY2025, a ~460bp compression over the period, largest single-year drop in FY2023), while EBITDA and EBIT margins rose from FY2021 through a FY2024 peak (9.80% EBITDA margin, 7.66% EBIT margin) before falling back in FY2025 (8.78% and 6.90% respectively) — both margin lines inflect downward in the same year. Seasonality cannot be confirmed with the available data (Section 5), though FY2025's one clean year shows Q4 as the softest quarter for both revenue share and profit. The clearest inflection point in the most recent data is Q1 2026: management attributes the quarter's profit weakness explicitly to two dated, named, one-time items in the North American market — unusual winter storms that management says cut industry volume by roughly 10%, and a year-on-year increase in tariff costs — stating that **excluding North America, operating profit grew over 10%** in the quarter [2026 First Quarter Report, Apr-27-2026, p.2]. That is a company claim about an ex-one-off result, not an independently verified figure, and it has not been reconciled to a segment P&L in this report — but it is directly relevant to how the Q1 2026 revenue and profit decline should be read: as a plausible one-time regional shock layered on an already-decelerating consolidated growth rate, not evidence that the whole business inflected negative. Separately, the balance sheet shows a genuine multi-year trend, not noise: Haier's net-cash cushion has shrunk every year since FY2022 on both the strict basis (net debt/EBITDA moving from −1.24x in FY2022 to −0.19x in FY2025) and CapIQ's broader cash-inclusive basis — the company remains net-cash through the latest quarter, but the cushion is visibly thinner than it was three years ago.

# Revenue Drivers — HAIER (Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd., SHSE: 600690 / SEHK: 6690)

**Currency and standard note:** all figures in RMB (CNY) million unless stated. Segment and geographic figures are from the China ASBE (CAS) A-share Annual Report, which the segment-map cross-check confirms reconciles to within RMB18mn (0.006%) of the IFRS H-share Annual Report for the same period. No verbatim earnings-call transcript exists in the pool less than ~82 months old and no sell-side analyst note exists either (per `00_earnings-data-triage`), so all driver commentary below is drawn from the MD&A and Business Review sections of the FY2025 Annual Report and the Q1 2026 Quarterly Report — not from a call. This caps earnings clarity per the module's score-cap table; it does not affect this report's use of filed, audited/regulatory MD&A text.

---

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Segment decomposition applied — 5 segments from the business-model module's `03_segment-map.md`, cross-checked directly against `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1), pp.222-224`. Haier is not a single-segment business: no segment exceeds 85% of revenue (the largest, Household Food Storage & Cooking Solutions, is 41.7%). A geographic decomposition (8 regions, `Note 11(2), p.225`) is also applied as a second, independently reconciling cut of the same growth number.

---

## 2. Revenue Driver Tree

| Business Type | Revenue Formula |
|---|---|
| Multi-segment manufacturer | Sum of segment revenue drivers, each ≈ units sold × realized average selling price (ASP) |

**Company-specific formula:** Group revenue = Σ across 5 reportable segments (Refrigerators/Freezers, Kitchen Appliances, Air Solutions, Home Laundry Care, Household Water Solutions, plus a residual "Other Business" channel/component/logistics bucket) — each segment itself ≈ units sold × realized ASP, blended across China and 8 disclosed overseas regions (Americas, Australia, South Asia, Europe, Southeast Asia, Middle East & Africa, Japan, Others), with two 2024-vintage acquisitions (CCR commercial refrigeration, folded into Air Solutions; Kwikot South African water heaters, folded into Household Water Solutions) adding an inorganic overlay on top of organic unit/price growth. [`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11(1)-(2), pp.222-225`; `03_segment-map.md`]

## 3. Market / Share / Price / Mix Split

| Driver Bucket | Current Direction | Evidence | Importance /100 |
|---|---|---|---:|
| End-market demand (China) | Deteriorating | China home-appliance retail (ex-3C) fell 6.2% YoY in Q1 2026 per AVC all-channel data, cited by the company itself; FY2025 China central-air-conditioning market fell 7.4% "attributed to the real-estate deep adjustment." [`2026 First Quarter Report, Apr-27-2026, p.3`; `10_external-dependency.md`] | 75 |

| End-market demand (North America) | Deteriorating (temporary, weather-driven) | US industry demand fell ~10% YoY in Q1 2026 per AHAM data, attributed by the company to "rare blizzards"; FY2025 North America results separately "impacted by tariffs and other factors." ## 6. Revenue Growth Decomposition

Haier does not disclose a company-wide unit-volume/average-selling-price split, so the classic Volume/Price/Mix/FX/M&A/Other template cannot be filled directly from a single source. Instead, two independent, exactly-reconciling decompositions of the same FY2025 revenue growth (+5.71% YoY, RMB302,346.78mn vs RMB286,015.29mn) are shown — by segment and by geography — both sourced from the same audited note (`FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Note 11`) and both summing to the reported total with no meaningful residual, because they are actual reported revenue splits, not modelled ratios.

**By segment:**

| Component | Contribution to Growth (pp) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Refrigerators/Freezers | +0.40 | Segment external revenue RMB84,486.69mn vs RMB83,343.54mn [`Note 11(1), p.222-223`] |
| Kitchen Appliances | +0.13 | RMB41,488.07mn vs RMB41,119.05mn [same] |
| Air Solutions | +1.65 | RMB54,021.47mn vs RMB49,300.60mn [same] |
| Home Laundry Care | +0.79 | RMB65,385.52mn vs RMB63,134.45mn [same] |
| Household Water Solutions | +0.60 | RMB17,736.20mn vs RMB16,014.27mn [same] |
| Other Business | +2.14 | RMB39,228.84mn vs RMB33,103.39mn [same] |
| Other / residual | ~0.00 | Rounding only — segments sum to 5.71pp exactly against the reported total (computed by this agent, Bash-verified) |
| **Total revenue growth** | **+5.71** | `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.12` |

**By geography (second, independent cut of the same total):**

| Component | Contribution to Growth (pp) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Mainland China | +1.52 | RMB146,554.58mn vs RMB142,201.32mn [`Note 11(2), p.225`] |
| Americas | +0.12 | RMB79,870.72mn vs RMB79,528.52mn [same] |
| Europe | +2.24 | RMB38,490.75mn vs RMB32,089.19mn [same] |
| South Asia | +0.93 | RMB14,199.35mn vs RMB11,525.06mn [same] |
| Southeast Asia | +0.31 | RMB7,520.29mn vs RMB6,632.70mn [same] |
| Middle East & Africa | +0.52 | RMB4,167.40mn vs RMB2,674.20mn [same] |
| Japan | +0.12 | RMB3,778.64mn vs RMB3,425.63mn [same] |
| Australia | +0.02 | RMB6,697.77mn vs RMB6,642.44mn [same] |
| Other regions | −0.08 | RMB1,067.29mn vs RMB1,296.24mn [same] |
| Other / residual | ~0.00 | Rounding only |
| **Total revenue growth** | **+5.71** | `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.12` |

**Volume / Price / Mix / FX / M&A — not decomposable at the consolidated level.** No company-wide unit count or blended ASP is disclosed. The nearest volume datapoint (room air-conditioner global unit sales +14.8% YoY, `p.30`) sits on a different classification basis than the Air Solutions segment revenue figure above (which also includes central air conditioning, down 7.4% in China, and CCR commercial refrigeration) — see Section 6a for why this cannot be used to derive a price/mix pp figure. M&A (CCR, Kwikot) is qualitatively confirmed to be inside the Air Solutions (+1.65pp) and Water Solutions (+0.60pp) rows above but is not separately quantified by the company (Section 3, Section 5). FX is not disclosed at the revenue level (Section 3).

## 6a. Decomposition Attribution and Residual (MODULE_RULES "Driver Attribution" / §15)

**Segment decomposition — asserted from disclosure, no ratio applied.** Each of the six segment rows above is a directly reported external-revenue figure from `Note 11(1)`, divided by the prior-year total revenue (RMB286,015.29mn) to get its pp contribution. No sensitivity, ratio, or cost-basis was applied — this is arithmetic on reported figures, not a modelled attribution, so there is no basis-mismatch risk to check.

```
Sum of segment components = 0.40 + 0.13 + 1.65 + 0.79 + 0.60 + 2.14 = 5.71pp
Stated Total (Section 6) = 5.71pp
Residual = 0.00pp (rounding only; Bash-verified against Note 11(1) source figures, zero residual to 2 decimal places)
```

**Geography decomposition — asserted from disclosure, no ratio applied.** Same method, same source class (`Note 11(2)`), same result:

```
Sum of geography components = 1.52 + 0.12 + 2.24 + 0.93 + 0.31 + 0.52 + 0.12 + 0.02 - 0.08 = 5.71pp
Stated Total (Section 6) = 5.71pp
Residual = 0.00pp (rounding only; Bash-verified)
```

Both decompositions are fully reconciled — this is expected, since each is a complete partition of the same total revenue figure by a different axis, not an estimate derived from a sensitivity coefficient. There is no large unexplained residual in either cut.

**Where a ratio WAS available (room air-conditioner unit volume) — refused, basis mismatch:**

```
Air Solutions segment revenue growth: +9.6% (RMB54,392mn, "Air Smart Solutions" business-line figure)
  [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.30]
Room air-conditioner GLOBAL UNIT volume growth: +14.8%
  [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.30]
  → basis MISMATCH — refused. The +14.8% figure is Haier-brand room air-conditioner
    UNIT sales only. The +9.6% (or, on the Note 11 reportable-segment classification,
    +9.575%) figure is the Air Solutions SEGMENT's total revenue, which also includes
    central air conditioning (China central-AC market fell 7.4% in FY2025, per
    `10_external-dependency.md`) and CCR commercial refrigeration (a 2024-vintage
    acquisition contributing an unquantified inorganic overlay, Section 5).
    Subtracting 9.6% from 14.8% to assert "price/mix fell ~5.2 points" would apply a
    unit-volume ratio measured on the room-AC-only basis to a segment-revenue figure
    measured on a broader, partly-inorganic basis — refused per CLAUDE.md §15.
```

This is a genuine data gap, not an oversight: Haier does not publish a company-wide, or even a segment-wide, volume/ASP reconciliation. A true price/mix read for Air Solutions — or for any segment — is **Not proven from available data.**

## 7. The Single Biggest Revenue Driver

**China domestic demand — governed jointly by the national appliance trade-in subsidy cycle and the real-estate market — is the single driver most likely to move group revenue by a large amount if it swings 10–20%, on both size and correlation grounds, even though it was NOT the largest contributor to FY2025's realized growth.** China is 48.5% of FY2025 revenue (RMB146,555mn of RMB302,347mn); a 10–20% swing in this single, policy-and-property-linked bucket moves 4.85–9.7pp of total group revenue — a High-magnitude, correlated move, unlike "overseas" (51.5% of revenue but split across 8 regions the company itself says "mitigat[e] the impact of fluctuations in a single region," `2026 First Quarter Report, p.3`). Its current direction is deteriorating: Q1 2026 China retail sales (ex-3C) fell 6.2% YoY (AVC), and management's own FY2026 outlook explicitly flags "under the pressure of a high base from the subsidy years, 2026 industry-wide growth is expected to face pressure" (`FY2025 Annual Report, p.3`) — a direct, company-sourced statement that the FY2023-2025 subsidy-driven demand was not run-rate and is now reversing. As a rough supporting check (**Inference, not from filings**: FY2025's full-year domestic/overseas revenue WEIGHTS, 48.5%/51.5%, applied to the disclosed Q1 2026 figures — total revenue −6.86% YoY and overseas revenue −3.2% YoY — implies domestic revenue fell roughly 10-11% YoY in Q1 2026, sharper than the group-level decline, though the company does not disclose the actual Q1 2026 domestic/overseas split so this cannot be verified against a filed number). This is distinct from, and does not contradict, Section 6's finding that Europe (+2.24pp) and Other Business (+2.14pp) — not China (+1.52pp) — were actually the largest single contributors to FY2025's realized growth: that decomposition describes what happened last year; this section answers what single lever carries the largest correlated swing risk to the next few quarters, and the company's own words point at the same lever (subsidy/property) that Q1 2026 has already started to show reversing.

# Margin Drivers — HAIER (Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd., SHSE: 600690 / SEHK: 6690)

**Currency / standard:** RMB (CNY) millions unless stated otherwise, FY ends Dec-31. Cost-structure and by-product figures below are China ASBE (CAS), A-share basis — this is the only basis on which the company discloses a cost-of-sales breakdown by input line (raw materials / labor / depreciation / energy / other) and by product. IFRS (H-share) figures are used only where explicitly labelled and cross-checked. No `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker, consistent with `01_historical-financials.md`.

**Data limitation carried forward from `01_historical-financials.md`:** no probative call-derived commentary source exists (only two ~7-year-stale 2019 transcripts), so all narrative colour below is drawn from filings' MD&A, not a call. Chinese CAS quarterly filings disclose gross margin narratively only for the standalone latest quarter and cumulative year-to-date — EBITDA and a full quarterly income statement are never disclosed at the discrete-quarter level. This caps how finely the margin walk can be shown intra-year; flagged in place, not silently left blank.

## 0. Sector Overlay Status

**No sector overlay for multi-brand global home-appliance manufacturer — generic cost stack applies.** `frameworks/SECTOR_OVERLAYS.md` has no row matching "multi-brand, acquisition-built global appliance manufacturer" — it is not a bank/insurer/REIT, commodity/oil & gas producer, SaaS business, store-based retailer, telecom, asset manager, or pharma company, confirmed at business-model `02_business-identity.md` §3a. The generic operating-company candidate list (raw materials, labor, freight, energy, SG&A, R&D, D&A, mix, one-offs) governs Sections 2–7 below.

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Business-model `03_segment-map.md` is available and used. Haier is **not** a single-segment company (no segment exceeds 85% of revenue or profit) — it reports 5 IFRS/CAS segments (Refrigerators/Freezers, Kitchen Appliances, Air Solutions, Home Laundry Care, Household Water Solutions) plus an "Other Business" catch-all (channel distribution, equipment parts, small appliances, logistics), 41.7% revenue / 43.4% profit share in the dominant Food Storage & Cooking combination [`analyses/HAIER_2026-08-13/business-model/03_segment-map.md`, §2]. Segment-level **gross margin** by product line is disclosed in the FY2025 Annual Report's own by-product cost-analysis table (revenue, cost of sales, gross margin %, and each figure's YoY change, both FY2025 and FY2024) [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Mar-26-2026, p.42, "分产品情况" (By-Product Analysis)], and segment **operating profit before tax** is disclosed in Note 11(1). This is materially deeper than a revenue-only segment note, so full segment-level margin decomposition is performed below (Sections 5–7). Geography-level gross margin (domestic vs overseas) is also disclosed on the same page and used as a second, cross-checking cut. What is **not** disclosed: a geography-by-segment matrix (e.g., how much of Air Solutions' margin comes from China vs overseas) [`03_segment-map.md`, §3] and unit volumes / ASP by segment [`02_business-identity.md`, §3a] — so the bridge below decomposes margin by product and by region, but cannot separate a segment's margin move into volume vs price within that segment.

Figures are FY2025 vs FY2024, CAS basis. The "raw materials / labor / depreciation / energy / other" split below is disclosed by the company **only for the five core appliance product segments' combined cost of sales** (RMB185,255.24mn of the RMB220,515.59mn total product-level cost base — i.e., it excludes the "Other Business" channel-distribution/equipment-parts segment, RMB35,260.35mn of cost, which is not broken out by input line) [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Mar-26-2026, p.42, "成本分析表" (Cost Analysis Table)]. This basis is named explicitly because it is used again in Section 7's bridge.

| Energy | 0.4% / 0.4% | Neutral — $ grew +6.17% YoY but the line is too small (0.4% of cost base) to move margin materially | [Same table, p.42] | Low (<30bps even on a large percentage move) |
| SG&A — Selling expenses | 11.2% of total revenue / 11.8% (ratio improved 0.55pp; company states "0.6 percentage points") | **Tailwind** — domestic unified-warehouse ("TC") logistics/marketing efficiency, overseas retail-innovation efficiency | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24, item (2); computed 33,877.8/302,346.8 vs 33,608.8/286,015.3] | Mid |

## 3. Gross Margin → EBITDA Margin → EBIT Margin Walk

| Margin Level | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change bps | Main Reason | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Gross margin (company-stated, total revenue basis) | 26.7% | 27.8% | **-110bps** | Q4 2025 copper/bulk-material cost rises plus intensifying China price competition (average selling price falling faster than the company's own cost-reduction program could offset); overseas, cost-program gains offset by high tariffs | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24, item (1)] — full arithmetic bridge in Section 7 |
| EBITDA margin (CapIQ-derived) | 8.78% | 9.80% | **-102bps** | Roughly tracks the gross-margin decline; SG&A ratio improvements (selling -55bps) were largely offset by admin-ratio deterioration (+31bps), leaving net opex-line effects close to neutral at this level | [`01_historical-financials.md`, §1] |
| EBIT margin (CapIQ-derived) | 6.90% | 7.66% | **-76bps** | Smaller decline than EBITDA margin because CapIQ's total-D&A line (all D&A, not just COGS-embedded) fell as a % of revenue (2.14%→1.88%) — a basis different from the COGS-embedded D&A row in Section 2, which rose. **A full bps reconciliation between the company's own "Operating Profit" formula (Revenue − Cost of Revenue − Taxes/Surcharges − Selling/Admin/R&D + Impairments) and CapIQ's EBIT construct is not possible from this pool — the two use different D&A and impairment treatments, and this gap is not resolved here** | [`01_historical-financials.md`, §1; Q1 2026 Report (HKEX), p.3, footnote 1 (Operating Profit formula)] |

**Pass-through lag:** business-model `06_value-chain.md` states plainly that Haier has **no** disclosed escalator, indexed-pricing, or cost-plus clause with any customer — input-cost increases are managed financially (commodity hedging, "volume-price betting" with suppliers) and operationally (cost-reduction programs), not passed through via price [`business-model/06_value-chain.md`, §2]. The evidence this buffer is incomplete is direct and repeats across two consecutive periods: FY2025 gross margin fell 110bps because "Q4 copper and other bulk-material rises… offset" the cost-reduction gains [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24], and Q1 2026 gross margin fell a further 10bps for the same stated reason in overseas markets ("the positive impact from global supply-chain layout and extreme cost optimization was offset by high tariffs and rising bulk material prices") [Q1 2026 Report (HKEX), p.5]. There is no evidence of even a lagged pass-through mechanism — cost increases have been absorbed, not recovered, in both periods measured.

---

## 4. Margin Walk — Which Margin Level Matters Most?

**Gross margin is the most useful level to track Haier at, and it is also the only one with enough disclosure granularity to actually track.** The company discloses gross margin at product-segment level (5 categories + Other Business), at region level (China vs overseas), and — narratively — at the standalone-quarter level, all with the underlying revenue/cost drivers named [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42; Q1 2026 Report (HKEX), p.4]. EBITDA, by contrast, is **never disclosed by the company at any interim frequency** — it is a CapIQ-derived construct only available annually — and EBIT/operating-profit is disclosed only at the consolidated annual and (via a company-defined formula) standalone-quarter level, with no segment split. Because raw materials are 84% of the dominant cost line and gross margin is where 100% of the company's own MD&A commentary on margin drivers is concentrated (Section 3), gross margin is the primary tracked metric for this manufacturer — a capital-light services business would look to gross margin for a different reason (thin fixed-cost base); here it is because gross margin is where the disclosed evidence actually lives.

## 5. Margin Driver Table (consolidated)

| Driver | Impact on Margins | Direction | Magnitude | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw-material commodity costs (steel, aluminium, copper, plastics/foam) | Largest single cost line at 84% of appliance-segment cost of sales; grew 7.46% YoY, nearly double appliance-segment revenue growth (3.77%) | **Headwind** | **High** (see Section 7: -178bps of total revenue before mitigation) | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42, p.58 item 3] |

## 7. Margin Bridge — Latest Period (FY2025 vs FY2024, Gross Margin)

**Basis note (must be read before the table):** the company's own headline figure is a **-110bps** decline in gross margin, 26.7% (FY2025) vs 27.8% (FY2024), on **total consolidated revenue** (RMB302,346.8mn) [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24, item (1)]. The bridge below is built from the company's own by-product cost-analysis table, which is disclosed on a narrower **"main business revenue"** base (RMB300,581.68mn FY2025 — the sum of the six named product/business lines, excluding a small non-core "other operating revenue" residual of ~RMB1.77bn) [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42]. Prior-year (FY2024) absolute revenue and cost figures for each product line are **back-calculated** from the company's own disclosed FY2025-vs-FY2024 YoY growth rates (given to two decimal places), which introduces small rounding error — this is labelled *Inference, not from filings* for the FY2024 absolute figures only (the FY2025 absolutes and all growth-rate percentages are directly filed).

| Component | Margin Impact (bps, of total revenue) | Derivation | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Raw materials (appliance segments) | **-178.0** | Actual FY2025 raw-material cost RMB155,542.0mn vs a counterfactual RMB150,192.0mn (FY2024's RMB144,742.1mn grown at the appliance segments' own +3.77% revenue growth) = RMB5,350.0mn of "excess" cost growth ÷ FY2025 appliance revenue (RMB261,689.0mn) × appliance revenue's 87.06% weight in total revenue | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42]; computed by this agent |
| Labor (appliance segments) | -12.2 | Same method: RMB12,218.9mn actual vs RMB11,852.5mn counterfactual = RMB366.4mn excess | [Same source]; computed |
| Depreciation, COGS-embedded (appliance segments) | -8.8 | RMB3,364.3mn actual vs RMB3,098.8mn counterfactual = RMB265.6mn excess (Air Solutions capacity build, Section 2) | [Same source]; computed |
| Energy (appliance segments) | -0.5 | RMB748.9mn actual vs RMB731.9mn counterfactual = RMB17.0mn excess | [Same source]; computed |
| Cost-reduction program / other cost items (appliance segments) | **+128.4** | RMB13,381.0mn actual vs RMB17,239.5mn counterfactual (this line fell in absolute terms, -19.46% YoY) = RMB3,858.5mn of cost AVOIDED relative to the revenue-scaled counterfactual | [Same source]; computed |
| *Appliance-segment subtotal (within-segment effect)* | *-71.1* | Sum of the five rows above; reconciles to the appliance-only gross margin change of -81.7bps × its 87.06% weight in total revenue | Computed, cross-checked two ways |
| Other Business segment's own margin change | +6.3 | Other Business gross margin improved 49bps (9.34% vs 8.85% implied FY2024) × its 12.94% weight in total revenue | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42]; computed |
| Mix (product mix: shift toward lower-margin Other Business segment) | -32.7 | Other Business revenue share rose from 11.40% to 12.94% (+1.54pp) × the ~21pp gross-margin GAP between Other Business (8.85%) and the appliance blend (30.03%) it displaced, using FY2024 margins as the mix-effect weight (standard shift-share method) | Computed by this agent from [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42] |
| **Subtotal (product-segment basis, "main business revenue")** | **-97.5** | Sum of all rows above | Computed; **cross-checked exactly via shift-share decomposition (within-segment -64.9bps + mix -32.7bps = -97.5bps, matching a direct total-margin recomputation to 0.0bps)** |
| Residual (scope: "main business revenue" base vs total consolidated revenue; rounding in back-solved FY2024 absolutes from 2-decimal disclosed growth rates) | -12.5 | -110bps (company-stated, total-revenue basis) minus -97.5bps (this agent's product-segment-basis computation) | Quantified gap, not rounded away |
| **Total margin change (company-stated)** | **-110.0** | [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24, item (1)] | |

**What this bridge does NOT separate:** volume vs price within each product segment (no unit/ASP disclosure — `business-model/02_business-identity.md` §3a data-gap flag), and tariff-specific cost (tariffs are blended into the raw-material/other-cost lines by product, not separately geography-tagged in this table — the region-level cut below is the closest available proxy).

**Cross-check — region-level cut of the same total change (not additive to the table above, a second view of the identical underlying revenue base):** domestic (China) gross margin fell 103bps (28.81% vs implied 29.84% FY2024) on +3.05% revenue growth; overseas gross margin fell 82bps (24.58% vs implied 25.40% FY2024) on +8.15% revenue growth — the faster-growing overseas business also has the lower margin, reinforcing the mix-driven headwind identified in the product-segment cut, but computed independently, so it is presented as corroboration, not summed into the -110bps total a second time. [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.42]; computed.

## 7a. Bridge Attribution and Residual

```
Raw materials (appliance segments): 7.46% actual cost growth vs 3.77% appliance-segment revenue growth
  = (155,542.0 − 144,742.1×1.0377) / 261,689.0 × (261,689.0/300,581.68)
  = 5,350.0mn excess cost ÷ 300,581.68mn total-revenue base = 178.0bps of the -110bps observed change
  → basis: FY2025 vs FY2024 by-product cost-analysis table, "main business revenue" base, CAS filing —
    same basis used throughout Section 7, no cross-basis application

Cost-reduction / other cost line (appliance segments): -19.46% actual cost change vs +3.77% revenue growth
  = (16,613.9×1.0377 − 13,381.0) / 300,581.68 = 128.4bps of OFFSET against the -110bps observed change
  → same basis as above

Mix (Other Business share +1.54pp × ~21pp margin gap to the appliance blend, at FY2024 margins)
  = 0.0154 × (8.85% − 30.03%) ≈ -32.7bps of the -110bps observed change
  → basis: shift-share decomposition using FY2024 margins as weights (standard method); refused to apply
    FY2025 margins to FY2024 weights, which would double-count the within-segment effect already
    captured in the rows above
```

Reconciliation: sum of components (-178.0 -12.2 -8.8 -0.5 +128.4 +6.3 -32.7 = **-97.5bps**) vs the company's stated Total (-110.0bps) = **97.5bps reconciled, 12.5bps residual** (11.4% of the total observed change). The residual is attributed to (a) the ~0.6% scope gap between "main business revenue" (the bridge's base) and total consolidated revenue (the company's headline base), and (b) compounding rounding from using 2-decimal disclosed growth rates to back-solve FY2024 absolute revenue/cost figures. This residual is small enough that it does not change which driver is largest (raw materials, by a wide margin), but it is reported here rather than folded into any other row.

---

## 8. The Single Biggest Margin Driver

**Raw-material commodity cost inflation** (steel, aluminium, copper, plastics/foam) is the single biggest driver if it moves adversely again. The bridge above shows it at **-178bps of total revenue before mitigation** — on its own, larger than the entire -110bps observed gross-margin decline. Its current direction is a headwind: the company's own MD&A attributes FY2025's margin compression specifically to "Q4 rises in copper and other bulk materials" [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.24], and 84% of the appliance segments' cost of sales is now raw materials (up from 82%) — the highest weight in the disclosed history. **The adjective must match the number here:** raw material cost growth alone would have been the dominant story, but it was roughly 72% offset in FY2025 by the company's own cost-reduction program (+128bps) — an offset that is a management lever, not a structural cost advantage, and is not guaranteed to repeat at the same magnitude every year. If that program's effectiveness reverts even partway toward its FY2023/FY2024 pace while commodity prices keep rising at the FY2025 rate, the net raw-material drag (currently netting to roughly -50bps after mitigation, per the bridge above) could widen materially. This is consistent with, and reconfirms, business-model `10_external-dependency.md`'s own conclusion that commodity prices are "the single biggest lever" in Haier's external-dependency profile [`10_external-dependency.md`, §5].

---

## 9. Investment Spend — Both Signs

**Not triggered as a primary theme — capex is not running above its own history.** FY2025 capex (RMB8,851.6mn) sits below the FY2023 peak (RMB10,541.6mn) and below FY2024 (RMB10,080.1mn); the five-year capex trend (FY21 RMB7,372.4mn → FY22 RMB8,209.8mn → FY23 RMB10,541.6mn → FY24 RMB10,080.1mn → FY25 RMB8,851.6mn) is a decline off a FY2023 peak, not a wave running above history [`01_historical-financials.md`, §1]. Q1 2026 capex was RMB2.246bn, in line with a normal quarterly run rate [Q1 2026 Report (HKEX), p.5, §VI].

The one related item worth flagging briefly, because it sits inside the margin bridge above: the **Air Solutions segment's asset base nearly doubled** FY24→FY25 (RMB32,729mn→RMB57,700mn, +76%) against only 9.55% segment revenue growth — but this is **M&A-driven** (the CCR/Carrier commercial-refrigeration and Kwikot acquisitions closing in the period), not organic capex ahead of demand, so it does not fit the two-sided "capex as cost vs capex as demand signal" framework this section is built for. It shows up in Section 2/6/7 as a COGS-embedded depreciation headwind (-8.8bps of total revenue), and the one forward-looking demand-side counterpart is management's FY2026 guidance for CCR: "high single-digit revenue growth, and further improvement in operating margin" [`04_guidance-consensus.md`, §2] — qualitative, no bps figure, and not verifiable against a segment-level consensus in this pool. Per the self-check rule, both signs are stated: the cost side is measured and reconciled (Section 7); the demand side is a management claim, unverified.

---

## 10. Cycle Position (Cycle-Position Rule)

Haier sits **past its FY2024 margin and revenue-growth peak, mid-way through a decelerating phase, with a named one-time policy tailwind now fading.** Evidence:

- **Margin peak already passed.** EBITDA margin peaked at 9.80% in FY2024 and fell to 8.78% in FY2025 (-102bps); EBIT margin peaked at 7.66% in FY2024 and fell to 6.90% in FY2025 (-76bps) [`01_historical-financials.md`, §1]. Both margin lines inflect downward in the same year.
- **Revenue growth is decelerating, not accelerating.** +12.57% (FY2023, the strongest year) → +4.31% (FY2024) → +5.71% (FY2025) → +1.25% (CapIQ LTM-vs-LTM to Mar-2026) → an outright -6.86% YoY decline in the standalone Q1 2026 quarter [`01_historical-financials.md`, §6].
- **A named, one-time policy tailwind is fading, and management labels it so itself.** China's national appliance trade-in subsidy (15% of price, capped RMB1,500/unit) supported 2024/H1-2025 demand; the company's own FY2026 outlook states plainly that industry growth "is expected to face pressure" under "the high base" the subsidy years created [`business-model/10_external-dependency.md`, §1, Government Policy row]. This is labelled **non-run-rate** for the period it boosted (FY2024–H1 2025) — the FY2024 margin peak should not be read as Haier's normalized run-rate.
- **Q1 2026's specific weakness is a named, dated, one-time regional shock layered on the deceleration, not evidence the whole business inflected negative.** Management attributes the quarter's profit decline explicitly to North American blizzards (industry volume -10%) and a YoY tariff-cost increase, stating "excluding North America, operating profit grew over 10%" [Q1 2026 Report (HKEX), p.2] — a company claim, not independently verified or reconciled to a segment P&L in this report, but directly relevant: it should not be read as the base-rate run-rate for the rest of FY2026.
- **Reconciliation with `10_external-dependency.md`:** that module scores external dependency 52/100 (mixed exposure, material but not extreme) and separately flags commodities, government subsidy policy, tariffs/geopolitics, and consumer cycle as simultaneously "High" [`10_external-dependency.md`, §3–4]. This agent's read agrees — the cycle position described here (past-peak, decelerating, with a fading policy tailwind) is consistent with, not divergent from, that assessment.

---

## Data Sufficiency & Limitations Summary

- **No verbatim transcript or sell-side proxy exists** for any period after 2019 — all commentary above is MD&A/filing narrative, not call color. Per the module's partial-data rule, this caps earnings clarity module-wide (see `00_earnings-data-triage.md`).
- **No unit-volume or ASP disclosure by segment** — the bridge in Section 7 nets price and volume together inside each segment's "revenue growth" figure; it cannot separate a segment's margin move into a price effect vs a volume/utilization effect.
- **No quarterly EBITDA or full quarterly income statement** — the margin walk (Section 3) and driver tables are annual-frequency for anything below gross margin; only gross margin itself has any within-year granularity (narrative, not tabulated, for interior quarters).
- **The 12.5bps bridge residual (Section 7a) is real and disclosed, not rounded away** — it does not change the ranking of drivers but is a genuine gap between the product-segment-level cost-analysis table and the company's consolidated headline figure.

## 7. Bar Assessment

**Bar is high** — miss risk elevated.

No formal consolidated guidance exists to anchor a "sandbagged, ready-to-beat" case, and the one quantified segment target in the filing (CCR "high single-digit" revenue growth) cannot be gap-tested against a segment-level consensus that does not exist in this pool. Estimates HAVE been cut sharply over the past 6–12 months (FY2026 EPS consensus down ~14% from six months ago, FY2026 revenue down ~4.8% from twelve months ago) — the classic ingredient of a "low bar" setup. But that cutting has not been validated by results: the two most recently reported quarters (FQ4 2025 and FQ1 2026) both missed the ALREADY-lowered consensus on both revenue and EPS, and the FY2025 full-year print itself missed by −7.1% on EPS. Revision breadth in the trailing ~3 months remains heavily net negative into the next print (EPS 1 up vs. 11 down; gross margin 3 up vs. 20 down), meaning the Street has not yet finished cutting. Per CLAUDE.md §4's conservative-default rule — when evidence conflicts, weight the more recent, higher-quality signal — two consecutive missed prints against a falling bar outweigh the fact that the bar has fallen. Treat any read of "estimates have already been cut enough" as unproven going into FQ2 2026 (due 2026-08-27).

# Beat / Miss Setup — HAIER

## 1. Next Quarter Context

The next print is HAIER's H1 2026 interim results (six months ended Jun-30-2026), due **Aug-27-2026** — two weeks from today. Consensus tracks this as a derived "FQ2 2026" (H1 total minus the already-filed Q1 2026 actual): revenue CNY 75,075.97mn and EPS CNY 0.58 [CapIQ Estimates, Trends tab, current]. Per `04_guidance-consensus.md` §7, the bar is assessed as **high, with miss risk elevated** — consensus has been cut sharply over the past 6–12 months (FY2026 EPS consensus down ~14% from six months ago), but the two most recently reported prints (FQ4 2025 and FQ1 2026) both missed the ALREADY-lowered consensus, and revision breadth remains net negative heading into this print.

## 2. Beat Scenarios

| Scenario | Driver | What Would Need To Happen | Likelihood (High / Mid / Low) | Evidence |

| North America normalizes post-weather shock | North America market (§3/§4, `02_revenue-drivers`) | The Q1 2026 blizzard-driven ~10% industry volume drop (AHAM data) does not recur in Q2; management's claim that "excluding North America, operating profit grew over 10%" in Q1 proves durable once the one-off passes | Mid | `2026 First Quarter Report, Apr-27-2026, p.2-4` — a company claim, unverified against segment P&L |
| Overseas emerging-market momentum continues | Overseas emerging markets — South Asia/SE Asia/MEA (§3/§4, `02_revenue-drivers`) | South Asia (+17% YoY Q1 2026) and SE Asia (+12% YoY Q1 2026) sustain double-digit growth into Q2, continuing to offset China softness | Mid | `2026 First Quarter Report, Apr-27-2026, p.4` |
| Cost-reduction program repeats its FY2025 offset magnitude | Company cost-reduction program ("极致成本战略") (§5/§8, `03_margin-drivers`) | The "Other" cost-of-sales line, which fell −19.46% YoY in FY2025 and offset ~72% of the −178bps raw-material headwind, continues at a similar offset rate in H1 2026 despite continued input-cost inflation | Low-Mid | `03_margin-drivers.md` §7-8 — explicitly flagged as "not guaranteed to repeat" |
| China share gains cushion the domestic decline more than modeled | Company market share (China core categories) (§3/§4, `02_revenue-drivers`) | Refrigerator (47.7%, +3.6pp), washer (47.4%), and AC share gains continue widening in a shrinking market, holding China revenue closer to flat than the ~6% Q1 decline implies | Low | `FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.27, p.30` |

| Raw-material cost inflation outpaces the cost-reduction offset | Raw-material commodity costs — single biggest margin driver (§8, `03_margin-drivers`) | Copper/steel/aluminium costs keep rising (already 84% of appliance-segment COGS, up from 82%) while the cost-reduction program's offset reverts toward its smaller pre-FY2025 pace, widening the net raw-material drag beyond the ~-50bps net effect seen in FY2025 | Mid | `03_margin-drivers.md` §7-8 |

## 5. In-Line Print But Bad Guidance Risk

| Risk | Evidence | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| In-line H1 print but 2026 outlook commentary turns more cautious | Management already flags "high base" pressure and 2026 industry growth headwinds in the FY2025 Annual Report [`FY2025 Annual Report, p.3`] — a broadening or sharpening of that language in the H1 report's MD&A would be a negative signal even if H1 numbers land near consensus | No formal numeric guidance exists to "guide down" from, so this risk shows up only in MD&A tone/wording, which cannot be read for candor without a transcript (§0, `04_guidance-consensus.md`) — a real blind spot |
| Revenue in line but gross margin misses (raw-material headwind not offset) | Gross margin is the only sub-annual-disclosed margin line and the level the company's own MD&A commentary concentrates on (`03_margin-drivers.md` §4); FY2025 gross margin already missed the prior year by −110bps on unmitigated copper/bulk-material cost rises | A revenue-in-line, margin-miss print would be read by consensus (EBITDA/EPS-focused) as a bigger miss than the topline suggests, since EBITDA is EBITDA-consensus-tracked but not directly disclosed quarterly |
| EPS beats on below-the-line items, but operating quality is flat or worse | FY2026 EBITDA consensus has stabilized (+1.3% trailing 90 days) while EPS consensus keeps falling on rising modeled interest expense (`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4) — the inverse pattern could also occur: a one-off FX or interest gain could lift EPS above consensus while the operating line disappoints | An EPS "beat" driven by a non-operating swing (interest/FX, which reversed direction between FY2025 and Q1 2026 per `03_margin-drivers.md` §2/§5) would be a quality-flag for `06_earnings-quality`, not a genuine operating beat |
| CapIQ-derived quarter concentrates a one-off (FQ4-2025-style distortion) | FQ4 2025's derived-quarter EPS surprise was −43.9%, versus FQ4 2024's similarly large −51.3% — both CapIQ-derived quarters, both extreme, both flagged as possibly definitional/seasonal (`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6) | The FQ2 2026 figure being reported is also CapIQ-derived (H1 minus Q1); a large headline surprise in either direction should be checked against the actual H1 cumulative filing before being read as an operating signal |

## 6. Seasonality Read

Seasonality cannot be confirmed with the available data — only one clean fiscal year (FY2025) of quarterly splits exists in the pool, and FY2024's quarterly data cannot be reconciled to the post-restatement annual total (`01_historical-financials.md` §5). As directional colour only, FY2025's Q2 revenue share was 25.59% of the full year, essentially in line with Q1 (26.17%) and Q3 (25.65%) — no evidence of Q2 being a structurally strong or weak quarter for Haier. This means seasonality is roughly neutral to the setup: it neither helps nor hurts the beat/miss case, and the module cannot lean on a seasonal tailwind or headwind argument for this specific print.

## 7. Historical Pattern

HAIER does not show a clean, systematic beat or miss pattern across the last four reported quarters — it is mixed (Q-4: revenue miss/EPS beat; Q-3: both beat; Q-2: both miss; Q-1: both miss) — but the pattern has trended negative into the most recent two quarters, both of which missed on revenue AND EPS against an already-lowered consensus, and the FY2025 full-year print itself missed EPS by −7.1% [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6]. This should be weighted moderately-to-heavily by the synthesizer: two consecutive misses against a falling bar, combined with revision breadth that remains net negative into this print (EPS 1 up/11 down; gross margin 3 up/20 down over the trailing ~3 months, `04_guidance-consensus.md` §5), is stronger evidence than the four-quarter mixed record alone would suggest — recency should dominate per CLAUDE.md §4's conservative-default rule.

## 8. Setup Verdict

**Setup favors miss.**

The single most important factor is that the Street's estimate-cutting has not been validated by results: consensus has already been cut sharply (FY2026 EPS down ~14% over six months) yet the two most recently reported quarters both missed the already-lowered bar, and revision breadth remains net negative heading into this print (EPS 1 up/11 down, gross margin 3 up/20 down over the trailing ~3 months) — the Street has not finished cutting. The single biggest risk that could flip this verdict is North America genuinely normalizing post-weather-shock: management's own (unverified) claim that ex-North-America operating profit grew over 10% in Q1 2026 implies the consolidated miss was concentrated in a dated, one-time regional event that should not repeat in Q2.

## 9. Second-Quarter Look-Ahead

Visibility past this print is limited — no formal guidance exists for any period beyond qualitative FY2026 statements. The quarter after next (Q3 2026, reporting ~Oct-2026) likely carries a different mix of risk: if management's claim that tariff impact will "gradually ease in 2026" proves true, North America could turn from a headwind to neutral, but the China "high base" effect from the fading trade-in subsidy is a full-year 2026 phenomenon (not a one-quarter event) and should still be pressuring the China segment in Q3. Net, the setup does not clearly improve or worsen for Q3 versus Q2 based on available evidence — it is simply a different balance of the same two named forces (North America improving, China still fading).

## 10. Pre-Mortem

If this setup call fails, the most likely reason is that the "North America is a one-time weather-and-tariff shock" narrative was wrong — either the blizzard-driven demand drop masked a more structural North American softening, or the tariff costs did not ease as management (unverified) claimed, and the segment continued to drag results below the "ex-North-America op profit grew over 10%" claim that this report leaned on as the main upside case. A secondary failure mode is that the China subsidy-fade effect proved milder than the company's own cautious language implied, letting the largest single revenue driver come in better than the deteriorating direction assumed here.

# Earnings Quality — HAIER (Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd., SHSE: 600690 / SEHK: 6690)

**Basis note:** all figures RMB (CNY) millions unless stated otherwise, China ASBE (CAS) A-share basis, fiscal year ending December 31, per upstream `01_historical-financials`. Cash flow statement IS available for HAIER (CapIQ export cross-checked against the FY2025 Annual Report), so the partial-data cap for missing cash-flow data does NOT apply here. Quarterly EBITDA and quarterly gross margin are not disclosed by the company (CAS quarterly filings show revenue, net profit, EPS, CFO only) — this caps QoQ cash-conversion granularity but not the annual bridge below, which is filing-and-CapIQ-sourced. No `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker (confirmed absent), so all figures below are this agent's own sourced reads, computed via an executed Python script (shown in-line), not a mechanically-pinned sidecar value.
