**Basis note:** this is understated versus Haier's true available liquidity because no committed/undrawn facility total exists in the data pool to add. There is no minimum-liquidity or springing-covenant requirement disclosed to subtract (no covenant package exists in the pool at all — `04_coverage-and-covenants.md`). Reporting currency: RMB (CNY). At Mar-31-2026 the same two components total CNY 66,675.5mn (cash CNY 50,580.3mn + short-term investments CNY 11,011.2mn + trading securities CNY 5,084.0mn) — a higher figure, shown here for reference only; it is not used in the headline calculation below because `02`'s 12-month maturity figure is built off the Dec-31-2025 balance sheet, and mixing an as-of-Mar-2026 liquidity figure against a Dec-2025-anchored uses figure would overstate the cushion.

---

## 2. Near-Term Uses (next 12 months, FY2025-anchored to match `02`)

| Use | Amount (CNYmn) | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Debt maturities (from `02`) | 23,452.2 | `02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing.md` §1 — the within-12-months (to Dec-31-2026) current bucket: short-term unsecured/pledged/guaranteed credit loans + current portion of long-term loans + current finance-lease liabilities + current bond-interest adjustment |
| Cash interest | 2,679.5 | FY2025 income-statement "Interest Expense" line [CapIQ "Financials.xls" — Income Statement tab, FY2025]. **Data-quality flag:** CapIQ's own cash-flow-statement supplemental line "Cash Interest Paid" shows only CNY 150.9mn for FY2025 (versus a "Net Interest Exp." of CNY 570.3mn, net of interest income, on the same tab) — none of the three figures (2,679.5 gross expense / 570.3 net-of-income / 150.9 supplemental) reconcile to each other in this pool, and the 150.9 figure looks anomalously low against either. This agent uses the gross income-statement Interest Expense (2,679.5) as the conservative, best-sourced figure for the near-term-uses table; the true cash outflow is almost certainly lower once interest income (Net Interest Exp. of only 570.3 implies roughly CNY 2,109mn of interest income against a large net-cash balance sheet) is considered, but that reconciliation cannot be performed precisely from this pool |
| Maintenance capex | 8,851.6 (total capex, FY2025) | `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §2 / `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` fn.4. **No maintenance-vs-growth capex split is disclosed** — the FY2025 Annual Report discloses a washing-machine capacity-expansion project, so some share of this figure is growth, not maintenance, capex; using the total is the conservative (higher) reading |
| Committed dividends / buybacks | 19,873.4 (dividends 13,873.4 + buyback 6,000.0) | Dividends: FY2025 actual "Common Dividends Paid" [CapIQ "Financials.xls" — Cash Flow tab], used as a trend-based near-term expectation, **not a legally binding 12-month commitment** — Chinese A-share dividends are declared annually at the AGM following each fiscal year-end, but the payout ratio has risen from ~35% (FY2022) to ~71% (FY2025) with per-share dividend growth of 19.8%–30% every year since FY2021 [`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` §Dividend policy & coverage], making a materially lower FY2026 dividend unlikely absent a policy change. Buyback: a **new CNY 6,000mn buyback authorization was announced 2026-03-26** (part-funded for an employee share plan, unused shares to be cancelled after 3 years) — a board-approved program, distinct from FY2025's already-executed CNY 1,233.6mn buyback, but its execution pace/timing within the next 12 months is not specified, so including the full authorization amount is a conservative (maximal near-term) assumption [`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` §Net share count trajectory; Corporate Timeline.rtf, Buyback Transaction Announcement, Mar-26-2026] |
| **Total near-term uses** | **54,856.7** | Sum of the above — shown for completeness; **not** the figure used in the headline runway math below (see Section 3, net-of-FCF basis) |

---

## 3. Runway

Haier's FY2025 FCF (CFO − total capex) of CNY 17,151.3mn is positive, has been positive and broadly stable in every year FY2021–FY2025 (CNY 15,863.0mn → 12,046.8 → 15,994.2 → 16,238.0 → 17,151.3mn, per `earnings/01_historical-financials.md`), and is cash-backed: CFO/EBITDA ran 93.9%–98.0% in FY2024–FY2025 and has never fallen below 93.9% across five years [`earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` §2, earnings-quality score 66/100 — "mostly clean"]. FCF is meaningful, not negative or unreliable, so this agent uses the **net-of-FCF basis**.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Total committed liquidity | CNY 59,644.6mn |
| Annual FCF (FY2025, CFO − total capex) | CNY 17,151.3mn |
| Basis used | **Net-of-FCF** (FCF meaningful and cash-backed) |
| Annual net cash burn (net-of-FCF basis) | CNY 26,174.3mn — see formula below |
| Monthly net cash burn (annual ÷ 12) | CNY 2,181.2mn |
| **Liquidity runway (months) = liquidity ÷ monthly net cash burn** | **≈27.3 months** |

**Formula (net-of-FCF basis, per MODULE_RULES §8):**
`Annual net burn = (12-month debt maturities + committed dividends/buybacks) − FCF = (23,452.2 + 19,873.4) − 17,151.3 = 26,174.3`
`Monthly net burn = 26,174.3 ÷ 12 = 2,181.2`
`Runway = 59,644.6 ÷ 2,181.2 = 27.3 months`

Cash interest and maintenance capex are deliberately **not** re-added here — FCF (= CFO − total capex) already carries both cash interest paid (inside CFO) and all capex; re-adding them would double-count and understate the true runway.

**Sensitivity — if the CNY 6,000mn buyback authorization is excluded** (on the view that its 12-month execution is discretionary and unconfirmed, versus the dividend which is policy-driven): annual net burn falls to CNY 20,174.3mn, monthly burn to CNY 1,681.2mn, and the runway extends to **≈35.5 months**. The headline figure above (27.3 months) is the more conservative of the two and is retained as the reported runway.

**Cross-check — gross-obligations basis (informational only, not the headline basis since FCF is positive/meaningful):** if FCF is ignored entirely and the full Section-2 uses bucket (CNY 54,856.7mn) is treated as the annual burn with no offset, the runway would be CNY 59,644.6mn ÷ (CNY 54,856.7mn ÷ 12) = CNY 59,644.6mn ÷ CNY 4,571.4mn/month ≈ **13.0 months**. This is shown only as a stress cross-check — it is not the reported basis, since Haier's FCF is positive and cash-backed, not negative or unreliable (the trigger condition for using the gross-obligations basis).

### Seasonality / Peak Liquidity Need (Hard Check)

Household-appliance demand can be seasonal (e.g., summer air-conditioner sales, year-end restocking), but `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §5 and `earnings/05_beat-miss-setup.md` §6 both find **seasonality cannot be confirmed** from this data pool — only one clean fiscal year (FY2025) of quarterly splits exists, and no quarter that year fell outside a 20–30% revenue-share band (Q1 26.17%, Q2 25.59%, Q3 25.65%, Q4 ~22.6%), so there is no evidence of a structurally strong or weak quarter. Separately, `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` §3 flags that Haier's **negative cash conversion cycle has been narrowing sharply** — from −10.8 days (FY2023) to −7.0 days (FY2024) to −1.2 days (FY2025) — meaning the cushion where customers effectively pre-fund supplier payments is nearly gone; if this trend continues and the cycle turns positive, working capital would start pulling cash out of CFO rather than releasing it, independent of any seasonal pattern. **No disclosed peak-quarter working-capital cash-usage figure exists in this pool — per the Hard Check, "Peak working-capital need not disclosed — runway may be overstated."**

---

## 4. Sources & Uses Bridge

Cash on hand alone (CNY 47,621.7mn) already covers the full next-12-month debt-maturity bucket (CNY 23,452.2mn) 2.0x over, and total committed liquidity (CNY 59,644.6mn, cash + liquid short-term investments) covers the entire near-term uses bucket (CNY 54,856.7mn) 1.1x over even before counting a single yuan of FY2025 FCF — internal sources cover the next 12 months without needing external access (refinancing, an asset sale, or a facility drawdown). Of the reported ≈27.3-month runway, the large majority is already-in-hand liquidity (CNY 59,644.6mn sitting on the balance sheet today) rather than FCF that must still materialize — FCF only needs to hold near its FY2025 level (CNY 17,151.3mn) to offset roughly two-thirds of the annual maturities-plus-distributions bucket; even a full FCF shortfall to zero would still leave CNY 59,644.6mn of liquidity against CNY 43,325.6mn of 12-month maturities-plus-distributions (a 1.4x cushion), so the runway conclusion does not hinge on FCF holding up, only on its rough magnitude.

---

## 5. Liquidity Read

Haier's liquidity runway is **≈27.3 months** on the net-of-FCF basis (formula: [12-month maturities CNY 23,452.2mn + committed dividends/buybacks CNY 19,873.4mn − FY2025 FCF CNY 17,151.3mn] ÷ 12 = CNY 2,181.2mn/month monthly burn; CNY 59,644.6mn liquidity ÷ CNY 2,181.2mn = 27.3 months) — and even the more conservative gross-obligations cross-check (ignoring FCF entirely) still clears 13.0 months. This runway depends far more on cash already on the balance sheet than on FCF materializing: cash alone covers the 12-month debt wall 2.0x, and total liquidity would still cover 12-month maturities plus distributions 1.4x with zero FCF contribution. The single biggest liquidity risk is not a shortfall risk but a **data and concentration** risk: no committed/undrawn bank-facility figure exists anywhere in this pool (capping this agent's liquidity-runway confidence at 60/100 per MODULE_RULES), and roughly 57% of the Group's cash sits with the affiliated Haier Group Finance Co. rather than diversified independent banks — a disclosed, drawable, non-restricted balance, but a real counterparty-concentration exposure that a headline "cash covers everything" read should not paper over.

Out-of-scope request received: none — this report stays within the liquidity-runway mandate (source amounts, uses, and the runway calculation); it does not build the debt stack, assess covenants, or run the stress test.

## balance-sheet-survival / 04_coverage-and-covenants.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants.md`_

# Coverage & Covenants — HAIER

**Company:** Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (SHSE:600690 / SEHK:6690). Household-appliance manufacturer — the Business Type Applicability Gate does not exclude this module (not a bank/insurer/REIT). Reporting currency: RMB (CNY) millions. Reporting standard: China ASBE (CAS), A-share basis (H-share/IFRS restatement shows no material difference in net profit/equity, per `01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md`).

**No `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker** (confirmed absent in `01`'s read of the pool), so all figures below are this agent's own sourced reads of the CapIQ workbook exports and the FY2025 Annual Report, computed transparently via an executed Python script (shown inline in the commentary) — not a mechanically pinned sidecar value.

---

## 1. Coverage Ratios

**Basis:** EBITDA = reported (not adjusted — Haier does not disclose an adjusted/non-GAAP EBITDA, per `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §4). Interest = **gross** interest expense (the P&L "Interest Expense" line, CNY 2,679.5mn for FY2025, presented before netting against "Interest and Invest. Income" of CNY 3,249.8mn — Haier is actually a net interest *receiver*, net interest expense is only CNY 570.3mn, but gross is used here per MODULE_RULES §5 default). All figures FY2025 (year ended Dec-31-2025) unless noted.

| Ratio | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| EBITDA / interest | **9.91x** (= 26,543.4 ÷ 2,679.5) | Computed by this agent: CapIQ "Financials.xls" — Income Statement tab, FY2025 (EBITDA 26,543.362314; Interest Expense 2,679.5) |
| EBIT / interest | **7.79x** (= 20,866.8 ÷ 2,679.5) | Computed by this agent, same source. Matches CapIQ's own precomputed Ratios-tab figure of 7.787605x exactly — the two agree for this ratio |
| (EBITDA − capex) / interest | **6.60x** (= (26,543.4 − 8,851.6) ÷ 2,679.5) | Computed by this agent: capex CNY 8,851.6mn, CapIQ "Financials.xls" — Cash Flow tab, FY2025 |
| Fixed-charge coverage | **2.04x** (= (26,543.4 − 8,851.6) ÷ (2,679.5 + 4,356.5 + 1,631.3)) | Computed by this agent. Denominator = gross interest (2,679.5) + scheduled debt amortization, proxied by the current portion of long-term loans (4,356.5, from `01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md` §1) + the next-12-month finance-lease payment (1,631.3, CapIQ "Capital Structure Summary" tab, "Cap. Lease Payment Due +1") |

**A CapIQ-internal reconciliation flag (already noted in `01`, repeated here because it affects this section directly):** CapIQ's own precomputed "Ratios" tab states a materially *higher* EBITDA/Interest for FY2025 (**10.57065x**) and Total Debt/EBITDA (**1.506483x**, vs. this agent's own 1.61x computed from the same tab's own EBITDA line) — working the numbers backward shows CapIQ's ratio engine is using an EBITDA figure of roughly CNY 28,325–28,328mn for these specific pre-computed ratios, about CNY 1,785mn (6.7%) higher than the Income Statement tab's own reported FY2025 EBITDA of CNY 26,543.4mn used above. **EBIT/Interest is the one ratio where the two CapIQ views agree exactly** (this agent's 7.79x = CapIQ's own 7.787605x), which confirms the interest-expense denominator is not the source of the gap — the discrepancy sits entirely in which EBITDA figure feeds CapIQ's internal credit-ratio calculator. Per CLAUDE.md §5, this report uses the figures computed transparently from the Income Statement tab's own reported EBITDA and Interest Expense lines (reproducible, CNYmn ÷ CNYmn, shown above), not CapIQ's separate pre-computed Ratios-tab number, for the same reason `01` gave: no filing anywhere in the pool states an EBITDA figure at all (Haier does not disclose EBITDA), so neither CapIQ figure is a filing number — the Income Statement tab's own EBITDA is simply the more transparent and internally consistent of CapIQ's two readings.

**EBITDA is cash-backed — no coverage caveat needed on that count.** `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` finds CFO/EBITDA ran 93.9%–127.5% across FY2021–FY2025 and never fell below 93.9% in any year (FY2025: 98.0%; LTM to Mar-2026: 97.6%) — "cash conversion is genuinely strong and has never broken down." The coverage ratios above are therefore not flattered by non-cash EBITDA. The one earnings-quality caveat that *does* apply, carried from `earnings/06`: the negative cash-conversion cycle that partly supports this strong cash conversion has narrowed from −10.8 days (FY2023) to −1.2 days (FY2025) and is partly propped up by ~CNY 25bn of disclosed receivable-factoring and supplier-finance arrangements — a structural feature to watch, not a reason to discount today's EBITDA/interest coverage.

**LTM (to Mar-31-2026), for reference:** EBIT/interest 8.48x; EBITDA/interest 10.79x; (EBITDA−capex)/interest 6.99x — computed the same way (EBIT 20,385.9 / EBITDA 25,950.2 / capex 9,137.2 / interest 2,404.0). Coverage is broadly stable quarter to quarter, not deteriorating.

---

## 2. Covenant Inventory

**No maintenance-covenant disclosure exists anywhere in the data pool for Haier's own debt.** The CapIQ Fixed Income Summary states explicitly: **"There are no Indentures or Credit Agreements available for this company"** [CapIQ "Fixed Income Summary.rtf", accessed 2026-08-13]. The two Medium-Term Notes (CNY 1,500mn @ 1.99% due 2028-02-25; CNY 2,000mn @ 1.66% due 2028-06-17) are senior unsecured NAFMII/interbank-market instruments — this market format typically does not carry US-leveraged-loan-style maintenance financial covenants (max leverage, min coverage tested quarterly), and no covenant terms for these notes, or for the unsecured bank term loans that make up the bulk of the debt stack, appear in the FY2025 Annual Report's debt notes or anywhere else in the pool. A targeted search of the pool for cross-default, change-of-control, and rating-trigger language also returned nothing for Haier's own borrowings (the only "cross-default"-adjacent hits in the pool relate to unrelated corporate-governance/takeover-defense boilerplate, not debt terms). **Per the MODULE_RULES partial-data rule, this agent applies a labeled typical-market-covenant assumption below, computes indicative headroom against it, and marks true covenant headroom "Not assessable" for scoring purposes.**

| Covenant | Threshold | Current Actual | Headroom | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Max Total Liabilities / Total Assets | **70% (assumed)** — a standard maintenance-covenant format (资产负债率不超过70%) in Chinese onshore bank-facility and bond documentation for an investment-grade-profile borrower | 57.41% (FY2025: CNY 169,818.1mn ÷ CNY 295,795.1mn) | **+18.0%** (direction: MAX/ceiling; (70% − 57.41%) ÷ 70%) | Assumption labeled *Inference, not from filings*. Actual ratio: CapIQ "Financials.xls" — Balance Sheet & Ratios tabs, FY2025 (matches CapIQ's own stated "Total Liabilities/Total Assets %" of 0.574107 exactly) |
| Max gross debt / EBITDA | **3.5x (assumed)** — a typical unsecured-facility ceiling for a non-leveraged industrial borrower (MODULE_RULES gives 4.0–4.5x as the example for a *leveraged* borrower; Haier's credit profile — net cash, unrated but no distress signal — sits well inside investment-grade territory, so a tighter assumed ceiling is the conservative choice per CLAUDE.md §4) | 1.61x (42,669.5 ÷ 26,543.4) | **+54.1%** (MAX/ceiling; (3.5x − 1.61x) ÷ 3.5x) | Assumption labeled *Inference, not from filings*. Actual ratio computed from `01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md` gross debt and this agent's Section 1 EBITDA |
| Min EBITDA / interest coverage | **3.0x (assumed)** — MODULE_RULES example band (2.0–3.0x); 3.0x used as the more conservative end | 9.91x | **+230.2%** (MIN/floor; (9.91x − 3.0x) ÷ 3.0x) | Assumption labeled *Inference, not from filings*. Actual ratio from Section 1 |
| Min liquidity / net worth | Not disclosed — no minimum-liquidity or minimum-net-worth covenant assumed (no clean typical-market analogue for this borrower type without a specific facility to anchor to) | n/a | **Not assessable** | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Springing covenant trigger (e.g., revolver-utilization threshold) | Not disclosed — no committed revolving-credit facility with a quantified commitment/utilization figure appears anywhere in the pool (`01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md` §1 flags this: only a narrative reference to "bank credit facilities from multiple commercial banks" with no quantified total) | n/a | **Not applicable / not assessable** | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Equity cure rights (Y/N, limits) | Not disclosed | n/a | **Not assessable** | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Cross-default / change-of-control / rating-trigger provisions | Not disclosed for Haier's own debt instruments in this pool | n/a | **Not assessable** | Not disclosed in the data pool |

**Why the assumed thresholds, not blanks:** the partial-data rule requires a labeled typical-market covenant so the reader has a reference point, even though — and this is stated plainly — none of these three thresholds is Haier's actual contractual covenant. No real breach can be measured because no real covenant is disclosed.

### Covenant EBITDA Definition & Quality (required if headroom is computed)

| Item | Value / Description | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Covenant EBITDA definition summary | **Unknown — no covenant document exists to define it.** The headroom figures above use plain reported EBITDA (Section 1), not a covenant-defined EBITDA with addbacks, because no covenant-EBITDA definition is disclosed | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Addbacks permitted (types) | Unknown | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Addback caps / limits | Unknown | Not disclosed in the data pool |
| Is covenant EBITDA materially above reported EBITDA? | **Cannot be judged** — this is exactly the "addback illusion" risk the partial-data rule flags. Since the headroom above is computed on reported EBITDA (which is well cash-backed at 98.0% CFO/EBITDA per `earnings/06`, so it is not itself inflated), the illustrative headroom is not overstated by an addback-inflated EBITDA — but this says nothing about what a *real* covenant, if one exists in an undisclosed bank facility, would define as covenant EBITDA | Not disclosed in the data pool — headroom quality on any real (undisclosed) covenant is unknown |

**Per MODULE_RULES score-cap table: "No covenant disclosure" → Covenant headroom = "Not assessable"; "Covenant headroom relies on assumed covenant-EBITDA addbacks" → Covenant headroom capped at 60 even where indicative headroom is computed.** Both caps apply here.

---

## 3. Headroom & Breach Proximity

**All figures below are against the labeled assumed covenants in Section 2 — indicative only, not a real contractual breach distance.**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant (by % headroom, among the assumed set) | Max Total Liabilities/Total Assets (assumed 70% ceiling) |
| Headroom on tightest covenant (%) | **+18.0%** |
| EBITDA decline that would breach it (approx.) | **Not directly meaningful** — this is a balance-sheet leverage ratio, not an EBITDA-driven one; a pure EBITDA decline (with debt and other liabilities held flat) does not move this ratio. See note below |
| Debt increase that would breach it (approx.) | **≈ +CNY 124,128mn of additional liabilities** (holding equity constant, funded liabilities and assets rising together) — about **2.9x today's entire CNY 42,669.5mn gross debt stack**. This is a very large absolute buffer despite the "only" 18.0% relative headroom, because the 70%-of-assets base (CNY 295,795mn) is large relative to Haier's actual debt |

**Second-tightest, and the more operationally meaningful covenant for a stress test:** the assumed max gross debt/EBITDA ceiling of 3.5x has +54.1% headroom and would break on either a **54.1% EBITDA decline** (EBITDA falling from CNY 26,543.4mn to CNY 12,191.3mn, debt held flat) or a **+117.7% increase in gross debt** (from CNY 42,669.5mn to CNY 92,901.8mn, EBITDA held flat). The assumed min-coverage floor (3.0x EBITDA/interest) has the widest headroom of the three (+230.2%) and would need a **69.7% EBITDA decline** (interest held flat) to breach.

**Read:** by strict percentage, the balance-sheet-ratio covenant is "tightest," but it is the least sensitive to a plausible operating shock — breaching it requires either a debt increase roughly triple the current stack or an asset write-down of similar scale, neither plausible from an EBITDA-driven downside alone. The debt/EBITDA covenant (+54.1% headroom, breaks on a ~54% EBITDA decline) is the more operationally relevant tightest constraint for `06_downside-stress-test` to carry forward, since it is the one an EBITDA haircut can actually move.

---

## 4. Coverage / Covenant Read

Earnings comfortably carry interest by the numbers: EBITDA/interest of 9.91x and EBIT/interest of 7.79x (FY2025, gross interest basis) sit well above any plausible maintenance-covenant floor, and the underlying EBITDA is cash-backed (CFO/EBITDA 98.0% FY2025, per `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md`), so this is not a coverage ratio propped up by non-cash accruals. No real covenant is disclosed anywhere in the pool — CapIQ states outright that no indenture or credit agreement is available for this borrower — so the covenant-headroom figures above are all labeled assumptions, not contractual facts, and covenant headroom is marked **Not assessable** for scoring. Under the illustrative assumed set, the tightest by percentage is a 70%-of-assets liabilities ceiling at +18.0% headroom, but it would take roughly 2.9x Haier's entire current debt stack in new liabilities to trip it; the more operationally exposed assumed covenant — a 3.5x max gross debt/EBITDA ceiling at +54.1% headroom — would break on a ~54% EBITDA decline or debt more than doubling, either of which is a genuine, if currently distant, downside scenario for `06_downside-stress-test` to size against.

# Off-Balance-Sheet & Contingencies — HAIER

**Company:** Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (SHSE:600690 A-shares / SEHK:6690 H-shares). Dual filer: A-share Annual Report under China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), H-share Annual Report restated to IFRS. **Reporting currency: RMB (CNY).** Figures below are quoted in RMB yuan as stated in the source note, then converted to CNY millions for comparability with `01`'s debt stack; the guarantee table in the A-share filing is denominated in 万元 (RMB 10,000s) — converted explicitly below. No FX conversion to another currency is applied anywhere in this report.

Both the CAS (A-share) and IFRS (H-share) filings carry the equivalent of a Contingent Liabilities & Commitments note (CAS: "十五、或有事项"; IFRS: "或然負債" in the Financial Review). Both are read and cited directly — the H-share note is in Traditional Chinese and is translated here, not treated as a data gap (CLAUDE.md §27).

Cross-module input used: `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` (capital-commitment and shareholder-guarantee figures, cited there from the same IFRS filing) — cross-checked directly against the primary source below, not taken on faith.

---

Leases") for short-term/low-value leases outside the capitalized lease liability | The CNY 6,182.7mn capitalized lease liability **is** in `01`'s gross-debt total; this CNY 10,994.6mn line is **not** — flagged by `01` as a vendor estimate, not a company-disclosed figure | CapIQ "Financials.xls," Balance Sheet tab, FY2025 (vendor estimate, Tier 5 — no matching commitment note found in either the CAS or IFRS filing text in this pool; treat as unconfirmed) |
| Pension / OPEB underfunding | CNY 1,615.4mn (net defined-benefit plan liability: CNY 1,293.5mn "设定受益计划净负债" closing balance, reclassified as CNY 28.0mn short-term + CNY 1,587.5mn long-term compensation payable) | Same — CAS/IFRS require the funded-status deficit to be recognized in full; no unrecognized actuarial gap disclosed | Not in `01`'s debt stack (pension is not treated as interest-bearing debt) — fully on-balance-sheet, not off-balance-sheet | FY2025 Annual Report (A-share, CAS), Note on defined-benefit plan, p.196–197/245 |
| Receivables factoring (outright/"sold-out" 卖断型保理) | CNY 0 (receivables fully derecognized on transfer — company represents substantially all risks and rewards transferred) | CNY 6,343.0mn derecognized at period end (FY2024: CNY 6,095.2mn) | No | FY2025 Annual Report (A-share, CAS), Note 5 (应收账款/Accounts Receivable), item (8), p.169–171/245 |
| Bills receivable endorsed/discounted, not yet due at balance-sheet date | CNY 0 (derecognized) | CNY 9,969.0mn — endorsed or discounted bank-acceptance bills not yet matured; under PRC negotiable-instruments law an endorser carries secondary/joint recourse liability if the accepting bank dishonors payment | No | FY2025 Annual Report (A-share, CAS), Note 6 (应收款项融资/Receivables Financing), item (3), p.170–171/245 |
| Capital commitments (contracted, not yet incurred) | CNY 0 | CNY 4,757mn at Dec-31-2025 (down from CNY 5,920mn, restated, at Dec-31-2024) — mainly domestic and overseas factory-construction projects | No | FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS, Traditional Chinese) — translated, Financial Review, "資本承擔" (Capital Commitments), p.78 |

**Note on the bank-acceptance-bill exposure:** the CNY 9,969.0mn figure is the single largest number in this report. It is not a litigation-type loss contingency — it is routine trade-finance activity (Haier endorses/discounts bank-accepted bills it holds from customers to accelerate cash collection). The credit risk sits primarily with the accepting bank, not with Haier's own customers; the company does not disclose any history of a drawee/acceptor default triggering recourse against it. It is included here in full because PRC negotiable-instruments law creates a real, if low-probability, contingent liability — not because the company flags it as a live risk.

| Total maximum/gross exposure — core, company-disclosed items (capital commitments CNY 4,757.0mn + endorsed/discounted bills not yet due CNY 9,969.0mn + receivables derecognized via outright factoring CNY 6,343.0mn) | CNY 21,069.0mn |
| Total maximum/gross exposure — broad, including intra-group subsidiary guarantees (CNY 7,213.5mn, not incremental — see §2) and the unconfirmed CapIQ operating-lease estimate (CNY 10,994.6mn) | CNY 39,277.1mn |

| Max exposure (broad) ÷ total equity | ~33.1% |

The ~514x and ~17.7%/33.1% ratios are arithmetically correct but **not informative on their own** — the "recognized" CNY 41.0mn baseline is a litigation provision, while the CNY 21.1bn/39.3bn "maximum exposure" figures are dominated by three non-litigation categories (capex commitments, non-recourse factoring, bank-backed bill endorsement) that were never expected to carry a matching recognized liability. Comparing them as a ratio is a category mismatch, not evidence of an unrecognized loss. See §5.

---

## 5. Contingency Read

The largest number in this report — CNY 9,969.0mn of bank-acceptance bills endorsed/discounted but not yet matured — is routine trade-finance activity where the credit risk sits mainly with the accepting bank, not with Haier's own customers or balance sheet; the company discloses no history of a drawee default triggering recourse, and it is not the kind of exposure the company's own probability language (used for litigation and provisions) applies to. The CNY 4,757mn capital-commitment figure is ordinary, declining, factory-construction capex, not a loss contingency. Both the CAS and IFRS filings make an explicit, audited negative representation — no material contingent liabilities, no material litigation or arbitration this year — and the one recognized litigation provision (CNY 41.0mn) is small and falling year-on-year (from CNY 52.9mn).

Guarantees are essentially internal: CNY 7,213.5mn of guarantees run from the listed parent to its own subsidiaries, whose debt is already consolidated in `01`'s CNY 42,669.5mn gross-debt figure, so crediting this back on top would double-count. External guarantees to third parties, shareholders, or the controller are CNY 0. If the balance sheet is under stress, the item most likely to actually move is the bill-endorsement contingent liability (CNY 9.97bn) — but only in the tail case of a Chinese bank defaulting on an acceptance it has already guaranteed, which is a banking-system event, not a Haier-specific one.

The ratio in §4 crosses both the 3x-of-recognized and 15%-of-equity rule-of-thumb thresholds on paper, but neither condition in the trigger rule for a live contingent-liability spike is met on substance: the company's own probability language marks litigation as immaterial/non-material for the year, and the largest off-balance-sheet items (capital commitments, non-recourse factoring, bank-backed bill endorsement) are not "reasonably possible" or "probable" loss contingencies at all — they are disclosed financing and capex mechanics. No `RF-OBS-001` tag is emitted.

# Downside Stress Test — HAIER

**Company:** Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (SHSE:600690 / SEHK:6690). **Reporting currency: RMB (CNY), millions**, consistent with `01`–`05`. Basis date: FY2025 (Dec-31-2025), matching `02`'s and `03`'s anchor date. No pending or recently-announced material acquisition is identified in `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` or elsewhere in the pool (the acquisition history shown there — GE Appliances 2016, Candy 2018, Kwikot 2024 — is all closed/consolidated, not pending), so no pro-forma base is built; the stress runs directly off the reported FY2025 balance sheet.

**EBITDA basis.** Base EBITDA is CNY 26,543.4mn, FY2025, reported (Haier does not disclose an adjusted/non-GAAP EBITDA, per `01` §5) and is cash-backed: CFO/EBITDA ran 93.9%–98.0% every year FY2021–FY2025 and never broke down [`earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` §2, earnings-quality score 66/100]. No adjustment to a "headline adjusted" figure is needed because none exists — the reported figure is the only figure, and it is well cash-backed, so it is used as-is for every haircut below.

## 2. Stress Scenarios

All figures computed by an executed Python script (shown below the table); net debt and gross debt are held flat within each pure-EBITDA-haircut column (a snapshot re-leveraging test at the current balance sheet, per MODULE_RULES §13/step 5), and are additionally hit by the stated cash/interest shock in the two combined columns.

| Metric | Base | −30% EBITDA | −40% EBITDA | −60% EBITDA | −40% + WC shock | −40% + rates +200bp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| EBITDA (CNYmn) | 26,543.4 | 18,580.4 | 15,926.0 | 10,617.4 | 15,926.0 | 15,926.0 |
| Gross debt / EBITDA | 1.61x | 2.30x | 2.68x | 4.02x | 2.68x | 2.68x |
| Net debt / EBITDA (strict) | (0.19x) net cash | (0.27x) net cash | (0.31x) net cash | (0.47x) net cash | (0.31x) net cash | (0.31x) net cash |
| EBITDA / interest (gross) | 9.91x | 6.93x | 5.94x | 3.96x | 5.94x | 4.99x (interest raised to CNY 3,188.9mn) |
| Tightest covenant headroom (indicative, assumed 3.5x max gross debt/EBITDA) | +54.1% | +34.4% | +23.5% | **−14.8%** | +23.5% | +23.5% |
| Covenant breach? (Y/N) — indicative only, no real covenant disclosed | N | N | N | **Y (indicative)** | N | N |
| 12-month liquidity gap (uses − [liquidity + stressed FCF], negative = surplus) | (33,470.3) surplus | (26,630.1) surplus | (24,350.0) surplus | (19,789.8) surplus | (9,320.9) surplus | (23,912.4) surplus |
| Survives without external action? (Y/N) | Y | Y | Y | **N** (indicative-covenant breach only; liquidity itself still has a CNY 19.8bn surplus) | Y | Y |

**Cyclical-name history-calibrated scenario** (per MODULE_RULES step 3 — `01` §1/§7 flags Haier as cyclical, cyclicality factor 34/100, the weak end of the band, per `business-model/07_business-quality.md`; external-dependency risk 52/100, mid-band, per `business-model/10_external-dependency.md`): the company's own 5-year EBITDA range runs from CNY 18,229.1mn (FY2021, the trough) to CNY 28,024.6mn (FY2024, the peak) — a peak-to-trough decline of **35.0%** (computed below). Applied to the latest-year EBITDA base: EBITDA falls to CNY 17,265.6mn, gross debt/EBITDA rises to 2.47x, EBITDA/interest falls to 6.44x, the indicative leverage-covenant headroom is +29.4% (no breach), and the 12-month liquidity gap remains a CNY 25,501.4mn surplus. This is milder than the flat −30%/−40% columns above because Haier's own realised 5-year swing (FY2021→FY2024, both growth years, no genuine recession print in the pool) has never actually been a deep drawdown — a caveat, not a reassurance, since a genuine China-property or US-tariff shock could easily cut deeper than anything in the company's own 5-year history.

**Floating-rate/hedge and seasonality shocks — both computable here** (unlike a company with no floating exposure or no revenue base to assume against): the rate shock uses the company's own disclosed floating-debt balance (CNY 25,468.0mn) × 200bp = CNY 509.4mn additional pre-tax interest; the WC shock uses a labelled 5%-of-revenue assumption (CNY 15,029.1mn) because no seasonal-build figure is disclosed (`03` §3).

### Executed calculation (Python, run via Bash)

```
EBITDA_latest = 26543.4; gross_debt = 42669.5; net_debt_strict = -4952.2
gross_interest = 2679.5; tax_rate = 0.141; FCF_base = 17151.3
usable_liquidity = 59644.6; obligations_12m = 43325.6
T_leverage = 3.5; T_coverage = 3.0

def row(h, extra_interest=0.0, wc_shock=0.0):
    es = EBITDA_latest*(1-h)
    gd_e = gross_debt/es
    nd_e = net_debt_strict/es
    interest = gross_interest + extra_interest
    cov = es/interest
    headroom_lev = (T_leverage - gd_e)/T_leverage
    breach = "Y" if headroom_lev < 0 else "N"
    fcf_s = FCF_base - EBITDA_latest*h*(1-tax_rate) - extra_interest*(1-tax_rate)
    liq_after = usable_liquidity + fcf_s - wc_shock
    gap = obligations_12m - liq_after
    return es, gd_e, nd_e, cov, headroom_lev, breach, gap
```

Console output (base / −30% / −40% / −60% / history-cal −35.0% / −40%+WC / −40%+rates), reproduced verbatim:

```

-30% EBITDA                  EBITDA= 18,580.4 GrossD/EBITDA= 2.30x NetD/EBITDA= -0.27x EBITDA/Int= 6.93x LevHeadroom=  34.4% Breach=N Liq+FCF-uses=  26,630.1(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=Y
-40% EBITDA                  EBITDA= 15,926.0 GrossD/EBITDA= 2.68x NetD/EBITDA= -0.31x EBITDA/Int= 5.94x LevHeadroom=  23.5% Breach=N Liq+FCF-uses=  24,350.0(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=Y
-60% EBITDA                  EBITDA= 10,617.4 GrossD/EBITDA= 4.02x NetD/EBITDA= -0.47x EBITDA/Int= 3.96x LevHeadroom= -14.8% Breach=Y Liq+FCF-uses=  19,789.8(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=N
History-cal (-35.0%)         EBITDA= 17,266.5 GrossD/EBITDA= 2.47x NetD/EBITDA= -0.29x EBITDA/Int= 6.44x LevHeadroom=  29.4% Breach=N Liq+FCF-uses=  25,501.4(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=Y
-40% + WC shock(15,029.1)    EBITDA= 15,926.0 GrossD/EBITDA= 2.68x NetD/EBITDA= -0.31x EBITDA/Int= 5.94x LevHeadroom=  23.5% Breach=N Liq+FCF-uses=   9,320.9(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=Y
-40% + rates+200bp           EBITDA= 15,926.0 GrossD/EBITDA= 2.68x NetD/EBITDA= -0.31x EBITDA/Int= 4.99x LevHeadroom=  23.5% Breach=N Liq+FCF-uses=  23,912.4(surplus) Survive_noExtAction=Y
```

The stressed-FCF scaling used throughout: `stressed FCF(h) ≈ FCF_base − EBITDA·h·(1−tax_rate)` — lost EBITDA drops through to FCF at the after-tax operating margin, holding cash interest and maintenance capex fixed (both already carried inside FCF = CFO − total capex, per `03` §3 / CLAUDE.md §15), with tax_rate = 14.1% (FY2025 effective tax rate, `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` §8). The two combined-shock columns additionally subtract the labelled WC assumption or add the after-tax cost of the extra rate-shock interest to FCF, as shown in the script.

---

## 3. Break Points

| Break Point | EBITDA Decline That Triggers It |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant breaches (indicative — assumed max gross debt/EBITDA 3.5x, the only assumed covenant that is EBITDA-sensitive; see note below on the other assumed covenant) | **54.1%** |
| Committed liquidity exhausted within 12 months | **Not reached on an EBITDA decline alone (h ≥ 1)** |
| Net leverage exceeds an illustrative 6x refi-market threshold | **Not reached on an EBITDA decline alone (h ≥ 1) — Haier is net cash, so the net-debt numerator is negative** |

**Show the solve, each break point:**

**(a) Covenant breach — MAX/ceiling, assumed max gross debt/EBITDA covenant (`T` = 3.5x).** Formula: `h = 1 − gross_debt ÷ (T · EBITDA)`.
`h = 1 − 42,669.5 ÷ (3.5 × 26,543.4) = 1 − 42,669.5 ÷ 92,901.9 = 1 − 0.4593 = 0.5407 → 54.1%`
This is **indicative only** — no real covenant is disclosed anywhere in the pool (`04` §2), so this is the point at which the *labelled market-typical assumption* would breach, not a confirmed contractual trigger.

**(a′) For reference — the other two assumed covenants, worked the same way, per `04` §3:**
- Assumed min EBITDA/interest coverage covenant (`T` = 3.0x, MIN/floor): `h = 1 − (T·interest)/EBITDA = 1 − (3.0 × 2,679.5) ÷ 26,543.4 = 1 − 0.3028 = 0.6972 → 69.7%` — wider than the leverage covenant, so not the binding constraint.
- Assumed max Total Liabilities/Total Assets covenant (70% ceiling): **not EBITDA-driven** — a pure earnings decline (debt and total assets held flat) does not move this ratio (`04` §3 confirms this directly: "Not directly meaningful... this is a balance-sheet leverage ratio, not an EBITDA-driven one"). It is excluded from this EBITDA-decline solve on that basis, per the step-5 instruction to solve non-EBITDA-driven MIN/MAX metrics on their own driver rather than force the coverage-style formula onto them. `04` separately shows it would take roughly 2.9x the entire current debt stack in new liabilities (or an equivalent asset write-down) to trip it — not something an EBITDA shock alone produces.

**(b) Liquidity exhaustion.** Solve `usable liquidity + stressed 12-month FCF(h) = next-12-month obligations`:
`59,644.6 + [17,151.3 − 26,543.4·h·(1−0.141)] = 43,325.6`
`59,644.6 + 17,151.3 − 43,325.6 = 22,804.8 × h → h = 33,470.3 ÷ 22,804.8 = 1.4679`
`h ≥ 1` — the solve returns a value above 1, meaning even a **complete (100%) EBITDA wipeout** does not exhaust the CNY 59,644.6mn committed liquidity against CNY 43,325.6mn of 12-month obligations. Checked directly at `h = 100%`: stressed FCF = CNY (5,649.5)mn (a real cash burn), liquidity + stressed FCF = CNY 53,995.1mn, still CNY 10,669.5mn above the CNY 43,325.6mn obligations bucket. **Liquidity exhaustion is not reached on an EBITDA decline alone** — this is not a fabricated percentage, it is the direct arithmetic consequence of a CNY 59.6bn liquidity base against a CNY 43.3bn obligations bucket that dwarfs even a full earnings wipeout.

**(refi threshold) Net leverage exceeds an illustrative 6x ceiling.** MAX form: `h = 1 − net_debt ÷ (T·EBITDA)`.
`h = 1 − (−4,952.2) ÷ (6.0 × 26,543.4) = 1 − (−0.0311) = 1.0311 → h ≥ 1`
Net debt (strict) is negative (net cash), so the numerator carries no debt — per the step-5 rule, this means the break point is **not reached on an EBITDA decline alone**; Haier's net leverage cannot cross a positive threshold purely because EBITDA falls, only if net debt itself turns positive (a real cash draw or new borrowing). **Supplementary, gross-debt basis (not net cash, so this one is computable):** gross debt/EBITDA hits 6.0x at `h = 1 − 42,669.5 ÷ (6.0 × 26,543.4) = 1 − 0.2679 = 0.7321 → 73.2%` — i.e., even ignoring the net-cash cushion entirely and looking only at gross debt against EBITDA, Haier would need a 73.2% EBITDA decline (well beyond the −60% base-case haircut) before gross leverage alone would look stretched by a typical refinancing-market yardstick.

---

## 4. Survival Read

Haier survives a 30–40% EBITDA decline — a normal recession, not a tail event — comfortably and without needing a waiver, an asset sale, or new equity: at −40% EBITDA, gross debt/EBITDA rises to a still-moderate 2.68x, EBITDA/interest coverage stays at 5.94x, the indicative leverage-covenant headroom is still +23.5%, and 12-month liquidity carries a CNY 24,350.0mn surplus even after subtracting the full maturity-plus-dividend bucket. The first thing to break, and only in the −60% column, is the **indicative, labelled-assumption** leverage covenant (3.5x max gross debt/EBITDA) — real covenant terms are not disclosed anywhere in the pool, so this is a flag against a market-typical proxy, not a confirmed contractual trigger; the company's actual real-world covenant package, if one exists in an undisclosed bank facility, could sit tighter or looser. Liquidity itself never breaks: the solved break point for exhausting the CNY 59,644.6mn committed liquidity base against next-12-month obligations of CNY 43,325.6mn is `h ≥ 1` — a complete, 100% EBITDA wipeout for a full year still leaves a CNY 10.7bn surplus. **Market closure test:** assuming no new unsecured refinancing is available for 12 months, Haier's cash on hand alone (CNY 47,621.7mn) still covers the entire within-12-month maturity bucket (CNY 23,452.2mn) 2.0x over (`02` §4) — nothing breaks first here, because the wall itself is fully pre-funded by cash, independent of market access. **Haier is net cash on the canonical strict basis (CNY 4,952.2mn, `01` §4/§7, with the broader CNY 16,975.1mn figure shown alongside, labelled) and survives every haircut through −60% EBITDA with no real (disclosed) covenant breach and no liquidity gap** — this is the strongest survival outcome the module can report, and the net cash functions as strategic counter-cyclical capacity (funding continued dividends, buybacks, supplier support, or opportunistic bolt-on M&A if China's property cycle or US tariff conditions worsen further) rather than an idle or "sub-optimal" balance sheet (CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 3). The one caveat worth carrying forward, not from this stress test's own math but from `01`'s liquidity-quality flag: roughly 57% of the cash base sits with the affiliated Haier Group Finance Co. rather than diversified independent banks — a disclosed, drawable, non-restricted concentration risk that does not change any number in this report, but is worth remembering if that counterparty relationship itself ever came under stress.

Out-of-scope request received: none — no probability is assigned to any downside scenario in this report; that judgment belongs to the master synthesizer.

## management-governance — module synthesis

_Source: `management-governance/99_management-governance-synthesis.md`_

# Management-Governance Module — HAIER (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Haier Smart Home's stewardship reads as standard and mixed — a stable, internally promoted CEO and an orderly CFO succession sit above a dividend-led capital-allocation record free of goodwill impairment, but whose newest invested capital turned value-destructive (incremental ROIC -8.3% in FY2025) even as the payout ratio keeps rising. Long-term pay is anchored entirely to ROE and profit-growth hurdles that genuinely missed in FY2025; individual insiders hold a negligible 0.066% of shares, almost all plan-vested, against a 34.49% Haier Group controlling bloc. The biggest risk is the deepening Haier Group Finance Co. relationship — 57% of Group cash parked there, related-party borrowing up roughly 19-fold. No hard disqualifier applies; this is a Watchlist-band governance profile, competent but not confidently aligned.

## 1. Stewardship Verdict

- **Verdict:** Standard / mixed
- **Hard disqualifier flagged (business-model/01)?** N — `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` found no audit qualification, no going-concern note, no promoter pledge (0%, "不适用"/Not Applicable disclosure trigger), no related-party ratio above 25% of revenue/expenses (sales 1.18% of revenue; purchases 9.55%–10.83% of expenses on two readings), no repeated auditor change (13-year continuous tenure), and no material restatement (a disclosed common-control-combination adjustment of 0.012% of revenue / 0.054% of net income, non-error in nature). No verdict lock applies.
- Management quality /100: **64** (from `01`)
- Capital allocation /100: **60** (from `02` — supersedes `business-model/11`'s quick-read score of 66/100; see `02`'s own note on why the deeper dive scores lower)
- Incentive alignment /100: **78** (from `03`)
- Shareholder friendliness /100: **61** (synthesized — see Section 3 for methodology; blends `04`'s Ownership Alignment Score of 69/100 and `05`'s Board & Shareholder Rights Score of 53/100)
- Disclosure candor /100: **56** (from `06`; module partial-data cap is max 65 — non-binding, the evidence-based score already sits below it)
- Governance risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: **40** (synthesized from the Red-Flag Register in Section 5A — six distinct red flags, none reaching Critical severity after reconciliation; see Section 3)
- Data quality /100: **82** *(from `00` — verdict "Sufficient," no hard MODULE_RULES cap triggered, soft caveats only on transcript staleness and new-CFO/new-director biographical thinness)*
- Overall usefulness /100: **85**
- Insider ownership (one line): Controlling bloc (Haier Group Corporation + 4 disclosed concert-party vehicles) holds 34.49% per the filing's own reconciled figure; named directors/officers combined hold just 0.066% of shares, almost entirely from Employee Share Ownership Plan vesting rather than cash purchase; no pledging anywhere in the control group.
- **Biggest governance signal (one line):** The deepening related-party financing relationship with Haier Group Finance Co. — 57% of Group cash (RMB33,988mn) parked there and related-party borrowing up roughly 19x year-on-year (RMB196mn → RMB3,767mn against a RMB10,000mn cap) — the single largest self-dealing/leakage channel available to the controlling shareholder, fully disclosed but growing fast.
- **Governance Score /100** — `0.20×CapAlloc + 0.18×Incentive + 0.18×ShFriendliness + 0.16×Candor + 0.16×MgmtQuality + 0.12×(100 − GovRisk)`:
  `0.20×60 + 0.18×78 + 0.18×61 + 0.16×56 + 0.16×64 + 0.12×(100−40) = 12.00 + 14.04 + 10.98 + 8.96 + 10.24 + 7.20 = 63.42` → **63/100**
- **Confidence-Adjusted Governance Score /100** (= Governance Score × Confidence Score / 100): `63 × 80/100 = 50.4` → **50/100**
- **Governance Rating:** **Watchlist** (55–69 band; Governance Score 63 falls inside it; no hard disqualifier and no Critical-severity red flag to force a lower rating)
- **Confidence Score /100** (source quality): **80** — the great majority of load-bearing findings cite audited FY2025 annual reports (both SSE/CAS and HKEX/IFRS legs, confidence 5) or cross-module outputs already vetted at confidence 5; CapIQ vendor exports carry confidence 3–4 and contain one unresolved reconciliation gap (the ~2.96pp ownership-figure mismatch, finding 04-002) and one now-resolved extraction artifact (the compensation-table row misalignment, finding 03-002); web-sourced peer-pay context is confidence 2 and used only for color. Held below 85 chiefly by the structural absence of any post-2019 earnings-call transcript.
- **Red-Flag Count / Critical Red-Flag Count:** **6 / 0**

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** The related-party financing relationship with Haier Group Finance Co. is deepening fast and on both axes at once — 57% of Group cash (RMB33,988mn) parked with an affiliated, non-independent finance company, and related-party borrowing up ~19x year-on-year to RMB3,767mn (37.7% of a RMB10,000mn cap) [`05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md`, 05-011, 05-012] — combined with a combined Chair/President/CEO role and a sub-majority-independent (60%) Audit Committee [`05`, 05-003, 05-004], the structural counterweights to self-dealing are thinner than the clean anti-takeover profile suggests.
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** Long-term incentive pay — roughly 70–77% of CEO/CFO total compensation — is anchored entirely to ROE and net-profit-growth hurdles with zero revenue/EBITDA/deal-count/headcount exposure, and those hurdles genuinely bit in FY2025: achieved weighted-average ROE of 16.98% missed the 17.7% full-vesting bar for the newest plan vintage [`03_incentives-and-compensation.md`, 03-006]. This is real, checkable evidence that the pay structure is not rigged to reward growth-for-its-own-sake.
- **Single killer risk:** If the Haier Group Finance Co. relationship keeps growing at its current pace (borrowing cap utilization already at 37.7% after a 19x jump in one year) or a future related-party asset injection repeats the 2018 Fisher & Paykel pattern of an undisclosed transfer price [`02_capital-allocation-scorecard.md`, 02-003, RF-CAP-001], minority shareholders could face expropriation-style leakage that this module's own disclosure-candor score (56/100, itself capped by the absence of any post-2019 Q&A record) would not surface until well after the fact.
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** 0% pledging across every disclosed Haier-affiliated holder [`04_ownership-and-insider-behavior.md`, 04-006]; no dual-class stock, cumulative voting for board seats, and a 10%-holder right to call an EGM [`04`, 04-007; `05`, 05-015 to 05-017]; no goodwill impairment across five acquisitions in 12+ years [`02`, 02-002]; the FY2025 buyback tranches priced into a declining stock, not a rising one [`02`, 02-008]; and the FY2025 LTIP hurdle was genuinely missed rather than rubber-stamped [`03`, 03-006] — a real, evidenced counterweight already sitting in the record, not merely asserted.

## 3. Reconciliation

Three material disagreements surfaced across the specialists, reconciled here to the more conservative reading per CLAUDE.md §4:

1. **Capital-allocation score: this module (60/100) vs. `business-model/11`'s quick-read (66/100).** `02_capital-allocation-scorecard` found three things the quick-read did not have: the incremental-ROIC calculation showing a negative FY2025 marginal return (-8.3%), the Carrier Commercial Refrigeration deal (raising the true M&A cadence to roughly one deal every 2 years, not 3–4), and the ESOP-purpose caveat on the FY2026 buyback program. Per `MODULE_RULES.md`, this module's deeper-dive score (60/100) supersedes the quick-read and is the one carried forward.

2. **Ownership-figure conflict: CapIQ's 37.45% vs. the filing's 34.49% controlling-bloc stake.** `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` traced the ~2.96 percentage-point gap to a likely CapIQ reclassification of an existing concert-party holding (HCH (HK) Investment Management, 538,560,000 shares, already counted in the filing's 34.49% aggregate) rather than genuine new accumulation. Per CLAUDE.md §4/§5, the audited filing's own reconciled figure (34.49%) is used as authoritative throughout this synthesis; the CapIQ figure is not cited as insider buying.

3. **RF-RPT-003 severity: "Critical" (05's own materiality tag) vs. this synthesis's reconciled "High."** `05_board-and-shareholder-rights` tagged the related-party borrowing line (05-011) materiality "Critical," driven by the trend (a ~19x year-on-year increase). Applying the MODULE_RULES materiality matrix on a level basis — RMB3,767mn borrowings ÷ RMB125,977mn FY2025 total equity = 3.0% of net worth, which sits in the Medium band (1–5%), not the >10%-of-net-worth Critical band the Red-Flag Trigger Engine reserves for "RPT leakage >10%" — this synthesis reconciles the severity down to High. The trend itself (a 19x increase in one year) remains the single fastest-deteriorating governance metric in this module and is flagged as the top monitoring item regardless of the severity label. This is a conservative reconciliation, not a dismissal: it keeps the Governance-risk floor from forcing this module below the "Weak" rating band on a level that does not itself clear the Critical bar, while preserving the trend as the module's single biggest watch item.

No other material disagreements between specialists were found — the six specialist reads are consistent in direction (a professionally managed, dividend-oriented company with real incentive bite, negligible individual insider ownership, clean pledging, and a growing but not yet disqualifying related-party financing dependency).

## 5. Stewardship Summary

Management has delivered on the concrete commitments it controls — the Mar-2025 buyback closed on schedule, the nine-year-old GE Appliances integration produced enough internal credibility that its CEO now sits on Haier's main board, and no goodwill has been impaired across five acquisitions in over a decade — but the business itself has missed already-lowered Street consensus in each of the last three reported periods, and the most recent tranche of invested capital destroyed value on a marginal basis (incremental ROIC -8.3% in FY2025) even as diluted EPS reversed on a trailing basis. Incentives are genuinely pointed at per-share value, not empire-building: roughly three-quarters of CEO and CFO pay is multi-year-vesting equity anchored solely to ROE and profit-growth hurdles, and those hurdles bit in FY2025 rather than rubber-stamping vesting. Skin in the game sits almost entirely with the corporate controller (Haier Group Corporation, 34.49%), not with individual executives, whose combined holding (0.066%) is nearly all plan-vested rather than bought with personal cash — a real, if common-for-the-regime, alignment gap. Minority shareholders benefit from a clean anti-entrenchment profile (no pledging, no dual-class stock, cumulative voting, a 10%-holder right to call a meeting) but face a combined Chair/President/CEO role, a sub-majority-independent Audit Committee, and a related-party financing relationship with Haier Group Finance Co. that is growing quickly (borrowings up ~19x year-on-year, 57% of Group cash parked with the same affiliate) — disclosed and independent-director-reviewed today, but the single item most likely to change this read if it keeps deteriorating. The single most important reason to trust this team with shareholder capital is that its long-term pay structure has no growth-for-its-own-sake metric in it and those targets were missed, not gamed, in the most recently completed year; the single most important reason for caution is that the controlling shareholder's financial arm is becoming a larger, faster-growing counterparty to the listed company's own cash and credit.

## 5D. Analyst Follow-Up Questions

For each Red or Amber finding carrying real weight in this synthesis:

- **RF-CAP-001 (undisclosed FPA price):** Was the 2018 related-party injection priced at fair value, or below/above what an arm's-length buyer would have paid? Is this a one-off gap in this pool's coverage (a pre-2018 transaction outside the filing window) or a recurring pattern the company should be expected to disclose better going forward? Does it affect minority holders' ability to judge whether Haier Group has historically extracted value through asset transfers?
- **RF-CAP-002 (SBC-purposed buyback):** Is the CNY6,000mn program genuinely likely to result in net share cancellation (via the 3-year unused-share clause), or will most of it flow to employees, diluting the "capital return" framing? Is this company-specific or a common structure across PRC-listed peers?
- **RF-RPT-002 / RF-RPT-003 (related-party financing):** Is the 19x year-on-year growth in Haier Group Finance Co. borrowings a one-off working-capital timing event or the start of a structural trend? Is the disclosed "independent-bank-rate" pricing claim independently verifiable? Does the 57% cash concentration with one affiliated counterparty create a liquidity risk beyond a pure related-party-leakage risk, and does it affect minority holders differently from majority holders?
- **RF-DISC-001 (unreconciled Q1 2026 claim):** Is the ">10% ex-North-America operating profit growth" figure accurate, and would a segment P&L (if disclosed) confirm or contradict it? Is this a pattern (selective favorable-segment framing) or an isolated instance? Would a credible restatement of this claim change the FQ1 2026 miss narrative materially?
- **RF-DISC-002 (recurring "non-recurring" subsidy):** Should this ~RMB1.1–1.3bn/year subsidy stream be treated as part of Haier's true recurring earnings power for valuation purposes? Is the mislabeling company-specific or a sector-wide Chinese-listco convention? Does correcting for it materially change the FY2025 "core" profit figure the company reports?
- **05-004 (sub-majority-independent Audit Committee):** Who is Li Shaohua, and does his lack of independence label plus thin biographical disclosure raise any conflict-of-interest concern specific to the audit function? Should this be re-checked once the FY2026 annual report is published?

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Stewardship verdict:** Standard / mixed. Strongest evidence for it: incentive pay is genuinely returns-anchored (ROE + profit-growth hurdles, zero size-based metrics) and those hurdles were missed, not rubber-stamped, in FY2025 [`03`, 03-006] — real evidence of alignment, not narrative.
- **Capital-allocation record:** Mixed, trending negative at the margin. Backward-looking record is conservative (no goodwill impairment in 12+ years, covered and growing dividend, low leverage), but the most recent, most decision-relevant data point is a negative FY2025 incremental ROIC (-8.3%) and a reversing EPS trend (-4.3% TTM, -15.3% YoY in Q1 2026) [`02`]. This module's capital-allocation score (60/100) supersedes `business-model/11`'s 66/100 quick-read.
- **Incentive/ownership alignment:** Incentives point at per-share value (strong, 78/100); individual insider ownership is negligible (0.066%, almost entirely plan-vested, not bought) sitting beneath a 34.49% corporate-controller bloc — alignment exists at the controller level, not the individual-executive level.
- **Biggest governance risk / severity:** The deepening Haier Group Finance Co. relationship (57% of Group cash parked there; related-party borrowing up ~19x YoY to RMB3,767mn, 37.7% of cap) — reconciled to High severity in this synthesis (see Section 3, item 3), not Critical; it is the fastest-deteriorating metric in the module and the item most likely to force a downgrade if it keeps growing.
- **Hard disqualifier flagged by business-model/01_disqualifier-scan:** None. Verbatim: *"No disqualifier triggered... No verdict lock applies from this scan... Nothing to route to management-governance on this [integrity] signal."*
- **§24 rejector filters tested and NOT tripped:** Turnaround (Filter 2) — not a turnaround thesis, RF-MGT-004 not applicable. Serial-acquirer (Filter 4) — tested explicitly [`02`, 02-005]; higher M&A cadence than previously stated but no deal near company value, no debt funding, no impairments; RF-CAP-004 not triggered. Unaligned owner (Filter 6) — tested explicitly [`04`, 04-008; `05`, 05-021]; Haier Group Corporation is a collectively-owned enterprise, not government-controlled, not a value-maximizing parent's subsidiary, not a sprawling conglomerate; RF-OWN-004 not fired. Integrity (Filter 1) — nothing routed from the disqualifier scan; RF-MGT-005 not emitted. No conviction cap from §24 applies.
- **Partial-data cap applied:** Disclosure candor is capped at max 65 by the "no transcripts/prior letters" rule (only ~7-year-stale Q2/Q3 2019 transcripts exist); non-binding, since the evidence-based score (56) already sits below the cap. No other MODULE_RULES score cap triggered — proxy-equivalent, ownership, board, and multi-year capital-allocation disclosures are all present.
- **Biggest missing data point (single highest-value next request):** An FY2025/Q1 2026-era earnings-call transcript or investor Q&A record — this is precisely where tone and evasiveness in the worst recent quarter would show up, and it cannot be filled from filings alone.
- **Explicit handoff:** This module supersedes `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` (the quick-read) where they overlap. The master synthesizer should treat THIS module's governance verdict (Standard / mixed) and scores (Governance Score 63/100, Confidence-Adjusted 50/100, Rating: Watchlist) as the primary governance read.

## 8. Simple Summary

- Management has kept its word on what it directly controls (a buyback closed on schedule, a nine-year-old acquisition earned enough trust that its subsidiary's CEO now sits on the main board), but the business has missed Wall Street's own already-lowered expectations three quarters running.
- Capital allocation looks safe on the surface (no write-downs, a growing dividend, low debt) but the newest money put into the business in FY2025 actually lost value on the margin, and per-share earnings have started falling again.
- Executive pay is tied almost entirely to return-on-equity and profit-growth targets — not sales growth, not deal-making — and in FY2025 those targets were missed, meaning the pay plan actually has teeth.
- The people running the company personally own almost nothing (0.066% of shares, mostly free grants, not purchases); real ownership sits with the parent company, Haier Group, at 34.49%, and none of it is pledged as loan collateral.
- Minority shareholders have decent voting protections (no poison pill, no dual-class shares, the right to call a meeting), but the CEO also chairs the board with no split, and the audit committee is not majority-independent.
- The biggest thing to watch is money moving between Haier Smart Home and its parent's in-house bank — more than half the company's cash sits there, and related-party borrowing jumped nearly 20-fold in one year.
- No dealbreaker was found — no fraud signal, no pledged shares, no failed audit, no related-party ratio anywhere close to the disqualifying level.
- This module is a strong input for the final call: it rests on audited annual reports in both Chinese-language filing regimes (translated, not treated as a data gap) plus detailed ownership, board, and compensation data — the one real hole is the lack of any recent earnings-call transcript to check management's tone under pressure.

## management-governance / 00_governance-data-triage.md

_Source: `management-governance/00_governance-data-triage.md`_

# Governance Data Triage — HAIER

Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (Qingdao, PRC) is dual-primary listed on the SSE (A-share, 600690) and HKEX (H-share, 6690), plus a Frankfurt D-share and a Level-I ADR (Form F-6). Controlling shareholder: Haier Group Corporation, a Qingdao-registered collectively-owned enterprise (集体所有制企业) — not a family promoter, not a central-government SOE, not an unrelated conglomerate. There is no proxy/DEF 14A, no SEBI-style AGM notice, and no Form 4 in this pool — because none exist for a China-incorporated, dual-listed issuer. The correct local equivalents (SSE Annual Report Board's Report / Corporate Governance section, HKEX Annual Report Connected-Transactions & Directors' Report, CSRC shareholding-pattern disclosures, and Capital IQ ownership/board/compensation exports) are present and are used per CLAUDE.md §27 and this module's Jurisdiction-Aware Source Mapping. Both FY2025 annual reports (SSE/China-ASBE and HKEX/IFRS) were read in their original Chinese and are disclosed, not opaque, per §27.

- **Specialists that can run:** management track record, capital allocation, incentives, ownership, board, candor (candor with the caveat noted below on transcript staleness).
- **Hard disqualifier already flagged by business-model/01_disqualifier-scan?** N — the scan found no audit qualification, no going-concern flag, no promoter-pledge trigger (explicitly marked "not applicable" / "无" (none) in the SSE filing), no related-party ratio above the 25% disqualifier threshold (goods/services RPT ≈5.0% of FY2025 revenue), and no repeated auditor change or restatement pattern beyond a disclosed common-control-combination restatement. No verdict lock applies.
- **Active partial-data caps:** None of the hard MODULE_RULES score caps are triggered (proxy/comp, ownership, and board disclosure are all present). One soft caveat: the LTIP performance-metric/weight breakdown is not itemized in the pool (only aggregate salary/bonus/RSU amounts by executive are available) — agent 03 (incentive alignment) should flag this as a granularity gap in its own findings rather than an unassessable score, and should not claim visibility into specific performance conditions it cannot cite. A second soft caveat: no earnings transcript newer than Q3 2019 exists, so candor/tone evidence for the FY2025/Q1 2026 period must come from filings' MD&A and the Guidance-history tab rather than call transcripts — agent 06 should state this explicitly per finding rather than silently substituting filing narrative for transcript tone.
- **Critical missing items:** None that block the Sufficient verdict.

# Management & Track Record — HAIER

Company: Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. — dual-primary listed A-share (SSE 600690) and H-share (HKEX 6690), plus a Frankfurt D-share and a US Level-I ADR. Controlling shareholder is Haier Group Corporation (海尔集团公司), a Qingdao-registered collectively-owned enterprise (集体所有制企业, not a family promoter, not a central-government SOE) holding 37.45% of shares as of Mar-27-2026 [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Public Ownership Summary.rtf, Top Holders, position date 2026-03-27]. No proxy/DEF 14A or SEBI-style AGM notice exists for a China-incorporated dual-listed issuer; the local equivalents used here are the FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, China ASBE) and FY2025 Annual Report (HKEX, IFRS) — both read in their original Chinese and translated — plus CapIQ board/compensation/ownership exports, per CLAUDE.md §27. No prior shareholder letter or recent earnings-call transcript exists in the data pool (the only verbatim transcripts are ~7 years stale, from Q2/Q3 2019); this caps how much of this report can test dated prior promises against outcomes — see §4 and the Partial-Data note below.

## 1. Key Executives

| Role | Name | Appointed | Tenure | Relevant Background | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chairman, President & CEO | Li Huagang (李华刚) | Director since Jun-18-2019; Chairman/President/CEO since 2019 | ~7 years in the top role; joined the wider Haier organization in 1991 (34 years) | Career Haier-Group manager, not a founder or family owner. Held senior sales/marketing roles across Haier Group's third- and fourth-tier China markets, then CEO (2017–2019) and Executive Director (2019–present) of the group's other listed vehicle, Haier Electronics Group. Also Vice President of the parent, Haier Group. Bachelor's in Economics (Huazhong University of Science and Technology, 1991); EMBA (China Europe International Business School, 2014) | [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Board Members.rtf, Li Huagang entry, current] |
| CFO & VP | Sun Jiacheng (孙加程) | May-28-2025 (succeeding Gong Wei) | ~1 year 3 months as CFO | Internal appointee; the CapIQ management-bio export carries no narrative background paragraph for him (title only) and a targeted web search for his prior career history returned no further public detail beyond his current CFO title — a genuine data gap, not treated as adverse | [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Professionals.rtf, Sun, Jiacheng entry; web search, 2026-08-13, unverified — no additional biographical detail found] |
| Vice Chairman (former CFO, 2010–2025) | Gong Wei (宫伟) | CFO Jan-2010 – May-2025; Director since Jun-18-2019; Vice Chairman since May-28-2025 | 15 years as CFO before promotion | Career Haier finance executive — division CFO (washing machines, air conditioning, appliances group) before group CFO; Fellow, Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (2020); multiple "Outstanding Accounting Worker" honors (2005–2015) | [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Board Members.rtf, Gong, Wei entry, current] |
| VP & Non-Independent Director (GE Appliances CEO) | Kevin Nolan | Director since May-28-2025 | President & CEO of GE Appliances (the 2016-acquired US subsidiary) since shortly after the Haier acquisition; ~35-year GE/GE Appliances career, including 10 years as GE Appliances CTO (from Nov-2006) | Engineer by background (30+ patents); named one of Louisville Business First's "Most Admired CEOs," 2019. His elevation to Haier Smart Home's main board in 2025 is the clearest signal the GE Appliances integration is viewed internally as a success, nine years after the deal | [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Board Members.rtf, Nolan, Kevin entry; web search "Kevin Nolan GE Appliances CEO", 2026-08-13, unverified — pressroom.geappliances.com bio, dated] |

The CEO is **not** a founder or owner-operator. Haier Smart Home's founder-era chairman (Zhang Ruimin) is not part of the current management team or board roster in this pool. The controlling shareholder, Haier Group Corporation, is itself a collectively-owned enterprise rather than a family or state promoter, and its own chairman (周云杰 / Zhou Yunjie, per `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md`) sits one level up from the listed company's day-to-day management — a structurally unusual but fully disclosed control arrangement, not an opaque one.

No CFO, Company Secretary, Compliance Officer, or auditor resignation found in the News or Key Developments logs — a keyword sweep for resignation/departure language returned no matches | [Haier Smart Home Co Ltd SHSE 600690 Key Developments.xls, entry dated 2026-04-28; News.rtf, keyword sweep, no results] |

A further independent director, Siu Paul Yu Hay (Deloitte veteran, CPA), joined Jun-24-2026 following Wong Hak Kun's term expiry, and board committee membership was reshuffled Jun-25-2026. No high-severity red flag is triggered by these findings — the one departure is a routine independent-director term expiry, and the CFO change is a promotion, not a resignation. **Follow-up:** confirm Sun Jiacheng's prior career background directly from the next AGM notice or annual report once published, since the current pool carries no narrative bio for him — a genuine, if immaterial, disclosure-depth gap for a newly appointed CFO.

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management frames the company as evolving from an appliance maker into a "user-centred, platform-based technology ecosystem enterprise" [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), p.2305 region — 以用户为中心的平台服务型科技生态企业], with a near-term product push around "unmanned housework" (无人家务) — appliance-plus-robotics "swarm intelligence" [FY2025 Annual Report (SSE, CAS), Business Review §III, p.2373 region]. The explicit, checkable targets set for FY2026 are: a CCR (Carrier Commercial Refrigeration) segment revenue growth of "high single digits" (roughly 7–9%) with further operating-margin improvement; a formal three-year capital-return floor of ≥58% of net profit paid as dividends in FY2026, stepping up to ≥60% in FY2027 and FY2028 (versus 55% actually paid out of FY2025 net income, up from ~48% in FY2024); and a set of China retail-channel build-out KPIs (3,000+ new specialty stores, 6,000+ store upgrades, 100 new premium Casarte experience centers, 100% direct-to-consumer warehousing by year-end) [Haier_Smart_Home_Co_Ltd_-_Form_Annual_Report(Apr-27-2026).pdf, Business Review §VI "Operating Plan," p.64–65, cited in `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`]. The company does **not** issue formal consolidated revenue, EBITDA, or EPS guidance — the last recorded guidance entry in the CapIQ Guidance tab is from FH1 2012 [`earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`, §2].

The items above are the only dated, checkable prior commitments this pool supports. Separately — not a company "promise" but a competence signal worth recording here — HAIER gives no formal consolidated guidance, and against Street consensus (which the company does not set), the two most recently reported quarters (FQ4 2025, FQ1 2026) and the FY2025 full-year print all missed already-lowered consensus, with FY2025 full-year EPS missing by −7.1% [`earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`, §6]. This bears on the "competence read" in §5 below, distinct from the graded promise-vs-delivery table above.

## 5. Management Read

Leadership is stable and internally promoted, not charismatic-founder-led: CEO Li Huagang has run the company for seven years and the recently retired 15-year CFO was promoted rather than pushed out, which is a genuine stability signal, though the new CFO's background is a real disclosure gap in this pool. On promise-vs-delivery, the only two dated, checkable items both came back Kept (the FY2025 buyback closed as executed, and the nine-year-old GE Appliances acquisition delivered enough credibility that its CEO now sits on Haier's global board) — but the sample is thin because no prior shareholder letter or recent transcript exists to test against, and the company gives no formal consolidated guidance at all. The single biggest management signal is a mixed one: management has quietly kept the concrete commitments it has made (buybacks, integration, a step-up dividend trend), while the business itself has missed already-lowered Street expectations in each of the last three reported periods (FQ4 2025, FQ1 2026, and the FY2025 full year) — competent stewardship of what it controls, against a harder operating backdrop than the Street had modeled.

# Capital-Allocation Scorecard — HAIER

Company: Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (SHSE: 600690 / SEHK: 6690). Reporting currency: RMB (CNY) millions unless a deal is priced in USD (CapIQ's cross-border M&A tab reports deal sizes in US$mm; those are labelled explicitly). Fiscal year ends December 31. Figures below are drawn from the China ASBE (CAS) A-share FY2025 Annual Report [filed 2026-03-26], the IFRS H-share FY2025 Annual Report [filed 2026-04-27], and the CapIQ workbook export (data as of 2026-08-13); no `ciq_facts.json` sidecar exists for this ticker, so all CapIQ-sourced figures below are this agent's own read of the workbook, not a mechanically-pinned value. This report supersedes `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` per `MODULE_RULES.md` where the two overlap — that quick-read scored capital allocation 66/100; this deeper read, using an incremental-ROIC calculation and a fuller M&A history that quick-read did not have, lands lower (see §4).

## 1. Uses of Capital (5 years, FY2021–FY2025)

| Use | Cumulative Amount | Currency | % of CFO | % of FCF | Source |

| Buybacks | 1,233.6 | CNY mn | 1.01% | 1.60% | [CapIQ export, Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Repurchase of Common Stock" row, FY2025 only — no buyback activity FY2021–FY2024] |
| Dividends | 40,410.7 | CNY mn | 33.03% | 52.28% | [CapIQ export, Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Common Dividends Paid" row FY2021–FY2025] |
| Capex | 45,055.5 | CNY mn | 36.83% | n/a (capex is FCF's own subtraction) | [CapIQ export, Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Capital Expenditure" row FY2021–FY2025] |
| Debt repayment (net) | +1,998.8 (net debt **raised**, not repaid) | CNY mn | 1.63% | 2.59% | [CapIQ export, Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Net Debt Issued" row FY2021–FY2025 — sum of five years, gross issuance/repayment churns every year but nets to a small net increase] |
| **Sum of the four discretionary uses (Acq. + Buyback + Div. + Capex)** | 91,305.4 | CNY mn | **74.6%** | n/a | Computed by this agent from the rows above |

Five-year totals used as the denominator: CFO = CNY 122,348.8mn; FCF (CFO − Capex) = CNY 77,293.3mn [both computed by this agent from `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §1, cross-checked against CapIQ Cash Flow tab]. About a quarter of five years' operating cash flow (25.4%) was retained rather than deployed to any of the four uses above — consistent with the cash balance growing from CNY 49,200.0mn (Total Cash & ST Investments, Dec-2021) to CNY 59,644.6mn (Dec-2025) even as debt also grew modestly [CapIQ export, Balance Sheet tab].

Capital allocation over this window is dividend- and capex-led, not M&A- or buyback-led: dividends (33.0% of CFO) and capex (36.8% of CFO) together account for nearly 70% of operating cash flow, while buybacks (1.0%) and net M&A cash spend (3.8%) are comparatively small — though the buyback figure is about to step up sharply (see §3) and a large acquisition (Carrier Commercial Refrigeration) closed just outside this five-year cash-flow window's largest single year (§2).

Goodwill RMB 2,329.3mn was booked under the "CCR" CGU label in the FY2025 Note 21 breakdown, no impairment to date — the filing figure is directionally consistent with (though not an exact reconciliation of) the web-sourced ~$610–640mm signing price and this agent's own read of the FY2024 cash-flow "Cash Acquisitions" line (CNY 4,409.3mn, ≈US$610mm) | This is the one deal in the current 3–5-year window that is a genuine step outside the core appliance category into commercial/foodservice equipment — worth watching for focus dilution, though at ~US$775mm it is under 0.5% of Haier's market capitalization (CNY 249,155.5mn / ≈US$34bn as of Dec-2024) and so does not itself threaten the balance sheet or the core franchise | [FY2025 Annual Report (A-share/CAS), Mar-26-2026, p.189, Note 21, CCR row: RMB 2,329,305,898.20; CapIQ export, Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Cash Acquisitions" FY2024: -4,409.3; Web (unverified, 2026-08-13 search): yicaiglobal.com and prnewswire.com CCR deal coverage] |
